My husband could not get past the consistency of the noodles.  I didn't mind it as much.  Like I said there is no taste to them really and I will eat the rest of them myself.  The packages are small probably meant to be individual servings.

column9: This is the best way to get my fix now that i moved away
column10: I moved to a town that does not carry these, and I was so bummed, but signing up for the automatic delivery means I wont have to be without!
cook in the boil water for 3 mins,rinse it thoroughly. It will not have any stinky smell.Perfect product for my diet.
Theses are great noodle alternatives. No smell or taste once rinsed in a strainer for a couple minutes.I gave it four stars because 15 bucks for 6 single person portions is expensive

Sorry, but did not like the tasteless texture.  Too rubberish in texture.All the noodles clumped together, needed to cut apart, but that is nature of the beast.The House Food brand on noodle has better texture/

I love pasta and have been looking for something to replace some of my pasta cravings.  I think the angel hair noodles do the trick in soups and some dishes.  I have made it several ways, but found that the noodle has to cook in the liquid in the dish you are preparing in order to taste good. I think it works well in oriental cooking.
A great addition to our diet!  Very filling and in our opinion they are better than the wider miracle noodles!
I cannot get that horrible smell out of my nose.  I really wanted to like these but oh my god they are too smelly  yuuuucccckkkk

column9: Information for the first time buyer
column10: I was not familiar with this product, but my wife was interested because of it's mention on popular daytime television.  Here are somethings you should know if you are unfamiliar with the product.1 star: The noodles come packaged in water, so one 7 oz package must be strained to obtain one 3 oz serving of noodles, very different from traditional dry pasta.3 star: The package, noodles in water, is a bit awkward to store on your traditional pantry shelf, you can't really stack them, etc.3 star: The noodles have an expiration date that is approximately four months away.  Don't order more than a few months supply.3 star: Because the noodles are already hydrated, they do not really take on much flavor from cooking liquid, you better put them into a very flavorful dish.2 star: Copared to pasta, these pre-hydrated noodles have a very slimy mouthfeel and they are not able to be cooked al dente, so they do not give the same fished result as a pasta substitute.5 star: As advertised, they are low calorie, filling, and a great source of soluable fiber.

column9: Miracle Noodle Shirataki Angel Hair Pasta.
column10: I wanted this to help me with constipation--again on what I heard on the Dr. Oz show.  I didn't see any help from eating them for that problem. I have bought some of the capsules, to see if I can get any success from them. Just received them today.

column9: "It feels like I am chewing gummy bungee cords..."
column10: These noodles were just delivered and I was excited to make them for my weight and health conscious high school daughter and friend. I carefully read all of the reviews and took them into consideration when preparing these "noodles." Yes, they smell but nothing ~too~ bad; once they are rinsed the smell is pretty much nullified. After running them through really hot water for a few minutes I patted them dry and seasoned them with our favorite seasonings with oil, salt, garlic salt, lawry's, pepper and a little bit of Panda Express' orange chicken sauce and then baked/broiled them for probably 30 minutes (turning frequently). (FYI: After 30 minutes of broiling they would not get the tad crispiness that we enjoy with normal pasta.)Anyway, from pan to serving dish I am at a loss for how to explain these noodles. They are nothing like spaghetti pasta AT ALL. They are translucent and...springy. While first chewing them we all slowed down to figure out what the heck we were eating and why because it didn't quite feel like food was in our mouths. Finally, my daughter's friend said, "It feels like I am chewing gummy bungee cords..." We all thought about it and totally agreed. My daughter kept saying, "I am thinking fish eyeballs..." After giving these what we thought was a fair shot, we politely put our forks down and pushed our plates away. I poured the batch down the sink feeling disappointed, but also knowing that I couldn't in good conscience feed these to my chickens either.

column9: quite pleased with the angel hair noodles
column10: These are my favorite miracle noodle. Much better than the Fettuccine. I think they work best in a tomato marinara sauce. They are a godsend for us diabetics . easy to make too.

THis product is ok.  If does have a foul odor that rinses off.  I'm italian so I really can't see putting marinara on these as some people have done.  In stir-frys and asian type dishes they are pretty good.  Great if you think about the zero calories!

This pasta is amazing. Buy it ! you WILL NOT feel regret. And yes, it smells awlfull when you first open the bag, but you will be over the smell once you start eating it with you tomato/basil pasta ( that's how I like it )Very happy with this vendor too. Got it super fast ! Thank you !!!!!!!!!!!

The only negative to this product is that it isn't more widely available, I live in Europe and had to order from the States.  The noodles will fill you up and help maintain your weight if used correctly (I.e no heavy sauces added etc)
I have really enjoyed these noodles.  I have to watch my carb intake, but I miss pasta.  These noodles fill that void.

So, we just got our shipment in today (super fast by the way).  Our first reaction was "eww they're in liquid, and they look like white worms!"  So I came here to read the reviews. Something I should've done first I guess.  I had no idea they came in liquid--I assumed they came dry, as all pastas do. I also didn't know how small the packages are! I rate it 3 stars because of my personal taste.  I still think it's a good alternative for people who need it, but I won't reorder.  I've been using the shiritaki noodles that are Soy/tofu based and I like them a lot more.  These are a bit too strange for me. It's plant cellulose it seems.  The texture is of an acquired taste, a bit gelatinous, a bit like cartilage. They're transparent and could be used in an asian soup quite well.  I'm probably going to do this with the remaining bags I got.  It's a different way to eat soluble fibers, but it makes a strange noodle.  I really love the Tofu ones though, So if you can eat soy I'd got for those instead.

Not very pleased with this product.  First thing the writing on the package is so small, I could not read it.  Therefore I did not have a good idea of how to prepare on use these noodles.  Upon delivery since it as a hot day and the noodles are packed in water, they were very hot, not sure if that makes a difference but I would feel better if these were package differently.

column9: Miracle Noodles - Yuck!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Stinky & Yucky Noodles
column10: OMG! definitely not what I expected!  The smell alone is enough to turn you off!  smells like really stinky fish!!!  I should of just bought one pack just to see what they are like!! column9: Rather starve than have to eat this!
column10: Seriously, although I could barely drag this very heavy box to the curb, the thought of having to eat them spurred me on--hideous odor and the consistency ofsomething rotting.  Repulsive is about the only word I can come up with---save your money!

I had great hopes that this was the answer for my pasta cravings.  Wrong!!!  I bought a big box of 15 packs of noodles.  I did have great hopes with all the wonderful reviews I read.  I rinsed and rinsed and rinsed and rinsed some more, but the smell was terrible.  I would gag from just the smell of them.  Needless to say they all went in the trash.  Even my dog wouldn't eat them and he will even eat dead stuff off the road (road kill) so you see he is not picky. Don't do like me, just order one pack until you see if you like it.  That was very expensive to throw away.  I tried several ways to make it work.  I thought I would never get the fishy smell out of my sink even after bleaching it, there was that fishy smell.  If you love the way fish smells this is for you but be aware of all of this before you order!

i bought these noodles after seeing them on dr oz! everone on the show said they taste good and have no callories . and they said these noodles pick up the taste of what ever you mix them with, ok here is what i have to say first these noodles are very expensive and although they do indeed pick up the taste of what you mix it with, it smells like fish and the concistency is that of worms!! you really cant bite though them very rubbery! i bought the angel hair and there is nothing angle about it. it is thicker the regular spagitti . i was worned by my friend not to get them ,but she is italain and of course there is no pasta replacement for her . well i should have listened.

As someone who has to be vigilant about food intake, I am always looking for substitutes for items I can't eat.  As such, these noodles were great!No, it is not real pasta.  And yes, you have to rinse the noodles to remove the fishy smell.  And the texture is a liitle weird.  But up until trying these, I probably have had 3 servings of pasta in the past 10+ years.  I rinse (alot!), cook like regular noodles, then add low-fat parm cheese, garlic powder, basil and butter flavored spray.  I've also added grilled chicken.  The savings in calories is tremendous and for me, well worth the difference in taste.  YMMV.

column9: Different, not unpleasent, but not a treat either
column10: I bought these because I'm a sucker for low calorie carbs. I just loves my rice, noodles, pasta, etc.and thought these would be a great substitute.  These are a no calorie substitute, but like substituting tofu for meat, the taste is in the myriad of ingredients you cook them with. They have no taste on their own and a rather obnoxiously slimy texture. The fishy smell you get when you open a package quickly dissipates with rinsing in cold water, they firm up a little with a quick parboil, but on their own they are BLAH. I have stir fried them and boiled them for soup with veggies, garlic, sauces, you name it. They aren't worth the effort. I will continue to stir fry and boil veggies, but I probably won't bother with these "noodles" again. A Tofurkey will never be a turkey and these will never satisfy a noodle craving.

This had such high reviews I was expecting much better. I can't describe the consistency except by saying jelly like and not the good kind of jelly. The smell is very fishy and if you wash them you can get rid of most of the smell. However, I do not care for them at all no matter if they are zero calorie.
I bought these because I'm a carb aholic.. I wouldn't want them as a steady diet.. Cut the up to about an inch long mixed with sauce...not bad...My huband hated them.
Really wish I read the reviews first. The smell was more than I could take. I don't like fish and it really had a strong odor. Could not bring myself to eat them.
I was not very happy with the pasta.  It was more like bean sprouts with no taste. Did not even resemble pasta
Ordered these after watching a TV Shopping Channel presentation. Much better price on Amazon. I found the taste to be very disagreeable, and will not be ordering them again!

These noodles made me very ill.  As far as taste, they do NOT absorb flavor at all.  The sauce just sits right on top and does not penetrate the noodle.  Also, the texture is very strange.  In any case, I would have continued to eat them if they had not made me ill.  The seller refused to take back the four packages that were left.  I was very unhappy with this purchase.

I had a really difficult time choking these down. It'd be great if they made noodle 1/2 from this and 1/2 from a grain. Still b half the calories and actually edible. i guess if your desperate and not too picky of an eater these could work for you.
These are the worst noodles I have ever eaten. No taste and feels like you are chewing on a rubberband, I would rather be hungry.

I was so excited to find these noodles.  When I opened the package the smell of old fish smacked me in the face.  I hoped it would get better after cooking them, but it didn't.  The texture was like chewing plastic.  Not real sure why you would eat these.

If you don't mind substituting flavorless, rubbery "noodles" for real noodles then these are for you. The consistency almost induced gagging. I'd rate them zero stars if that was an option.I'll stick with real pasta, in moderation.

If you follow the directions on the bag the smell should not be an issue after cooking. The texture is not unlike some rice noodles I've had at Chinese restaurants. In my opinion they are pretty tasty depending on how you season or sauce them. I will buy more in the future.

I followed the simple directions on the package and added the noodles to a stir-fry that I made. The noodles took on the tastes of the ginger, garlic, sesame oil, and soy sauce that I used in the dish. They were wonderful! I didn't find them rubbery or fishy at all. I highly recommend them!
Pasta-esque with no refined carbs! Hallelujah! Good texture, takes on flavor of sauce, quick shipment. This is a great option for adding to an Asian-style dish. Will re-order.

column9: I'd give it zero stars if that was an option.
column10: It's like eating a somewhat chewy rubber band. I couldn't get it to absorb ANY flavor.  I soaked it in various sauces for a couple of days in the fridge and it still had no flavor.
I was looking for a low carb food to substitute for pasta.  I read the reviews and thought I would try it.  This was horrible.  The smell is aweful and the taste and texture made me gag.

I wasn't looking for taste comparable to handmade Italian pasta. I was really just looking for noodles I could use in Asian soups and the occasional spaghetti-type dish. I've used these noodles for both and they turned out great. And by great, I mean they didn't add any funky flavor, they're weren't slimy or mealy, they had the texture of real noodles. In fact, they didn't have much flavor at all, and I'm fine with that as they soak up whatever flavor is around them. And they have no calories. That's a miracle.One thing--remember to rinse them in a colander or strainer first because they smell a little funky right out of the package.If you're on the fence on trying these noodles because you're worried they're going to taste weird or have a nasty texture, they really don't. Go for it.

I am amazed at how these noodles taste like whatever you want them to taste like. I like pasta but have never really craved it because it is SO heavy to me. I feel like napping after eating regular pasta and feel SO bloated. These are just what I needed to help me get through my HCG diet. They are so filling, yet light and very tasty. If you rinse them well, boil them for one minute then drain for a minute or so on some paper towels they are terriffic!!! You can really make some great dishes with these. Spaghetti, chicken noodle soup, just mix with veggies, whatever. I think they are wonderful and I will always have some on hand. They are very very filling and have no calories, fat, carbs...nothing!

This noodle works the best with my low carb diet. I always have a hard time thinking of what I can eat when I am on my low card diet. I can be satisfied because I am eating noodles and I will be sticking to my low carb diet. The noodles taste great. Easy to cook.
I purchased these after seeing it on the Dr. Oz show.  They are horrible gross I will never buy again.

column9: Miracle Noodle Shirataki Angel Hair Pasta
column10: Great product! Takes on the flavor of whatever it's cooked in. Doesn't get mushy. Stays nice & firm. Simple to prepare. One package is only enough for 1 person.

These noodles are wonderful!  Rinse well and they have absolutely no taste or odor. I've made them with Tomato Sauce and then with Olive Oil & Garlic, both ways they are delicious. They seem to absorb the flavor of whatever you put on them. Trust this fussy Italian, this "pasta" is really good. I just signed up for auto delivery, that's how much I've enjoyed them. Great for Diabetics, Weight Watchers-it's a free food, Gluten Free... you can't go wrong. Again, follow the directions and you will love this product!

First off, I read the other reviews here and elsewhere, and was worried about the much-talked about smell. Well, I got my order, and even sent a an order to my mother. The so-called smell was pretty mild. Once the noodles were thoroughly rinsed in a colander (preferably in hot water) they were just fine and ready to cook. Now, if you try making spaghetti, or any Italian dish, these noodles will fail you. They are not Italian pasta. They are made for soups, stir fries, and basically Asian cooking. In case the name didn't give it away - let me advise you that these noodles originated in Japan. I stir-fried these noodles with my own mix of vegetables  in minutes. They were awesome! This is the absolute best way to have them. Since April I've lost close to 50lbs by moving to a more vegetarian diet, and these noodles have made my meal planning even easier. I would strongly recommend them - but for people interested in making Asian pasta dishes (Lo Mein, Stir-fry, soups, etc).

Do not buy these!!!!And if you think you can ignore all the negative reviews, just because you so sorely wanted a pasta substitute, you'll be extremely disappointed. What's amazing is that even many of the 4 and 5 star reviewers admit to the things tasting horrible. But still, because they're labeled as 'noodles', some people will maintain a willingness to force them down.....such is the lure  of Pasta! I suppose you could freeze fecal matter and sell it as ice cream and  some people would choose  to eat it if they desperately craved ice cream and wanted to believe the packaging.These are shaped like noodles.All resemblance to any type of real noodle ends there.Horrible smell....as noted here,gags many people.Smells like a fish that rotted in a beaker of benzeneHorrible texture....like a scary foreign body in your food.No flavor (beyond the obnoxious smell) They don't really absorb any flavor either. The sauce just coats the outside, and in eating, any  sauce  quickly departs the  noodle surface and you're left with this disgusting mass of  slimy rubber  worms in your mouth. Even well rinsed, the weird fishy smell remains in your olfactory memory throughout the meal, thereby  eliciting a constant, low order,  gag reflex as you try to chew these things.Somehow I pushed the order button twice...so I'll be throwing out $60 worth of 'food',. Not sure I want them in my garbage can. I may have to drive them straight to the local land fill.I didn't expect greatness from a zero calorie noodle, but I really hoped these things would  at least be a palatable substitute.....not even close.Proving again; there's no such thing as a free lunch.

NO RETURN!  NO REFUND!  The texture of all of the Miracle Noodle products is like eating plastic fishing worms.  I read the reviews and tried every way possible to improve the experience of eating this stuff.  5 minutes of rinsing, par boiling etc.  When you buy this item you are stuck with it.  Amazon.com will not stand behind the quality of your experience.  Don't take a chance of losing $80 like I did.

column9: If you don't like fishy foods, Do Not Buy these!!!!
column10: I was skeptical when I saw reviews that said they tasted reminents of fishiness, but then I read further from reviewers that talked about strategies to get rid of that smell/taste.  I can tell you that I very thoroughly rinsed them in warm and cold water for 5-10 minutes, I then boiled them for another few minutes, rinsed, drained and blotted with a papertowel to take awayany and all water...and guess what the noodles were still extremely fishy and disgusting tasting!!  Save your money. Period.

column9: not gross but can't get over the texture
column10: This wasn't entirely disgusting.. The flavor itself wasn't too bad, it soaked in the flavor of the stir fry.  However, I just cannot get over the texture.  I kept feeling like I was eating hookworms since they were long, clear and rubbery. *shudder*  Won't be able to eat the other bags.

I purchased these noodles thinking they would be a good replacement for pasta.  I had hoped that I could recommend them to my weight loss clients.  Unfortunately things just did not work out.  First of all, the liquid they are packaged in smells horrible!  Does not set the stage for an appetizing meal.  The texture of the angel hair noodles which we tried was very rubbery. Even with my favorite marinara sauce, I just could not force down a full serving.  My feelings were echoed by the 3 other people in my office who tried them.  Even my husband who will eat almost anything, found the noodles unpleasant to eat and suggested that we NOT offer them to our clients.  If you have texture issues with food or you are buying them thinking they will replace pasta, forget it.  Despite the fact that we all eat a mostly vegetarian diet, these noodles gave us terrible gas, bloating and diarrhea the day after we ate them.  On a positive note, the company was very nice and allowed us to return unopened bags.

First, I never ever ever leave reviews on products.  I either like them or I don't, but I figure since I order them blindly, I have to only myself to blame if I don't care for it.  This, however, was EXTREME!  I saw the noodles on an episode of "The Talk" with a guest chef talking about how great they were..no carbs, no calories, great taste.  Wow!  I ordered 18 packages of the stuff without hesitation!  I was so excited, I even paid for the extra shipping cost to get it here faster!The product arrived on Thursday and I was so excited. When I discovered these noodles in 2006, I was really excited.  But, I had no idea how to cook them in a way that'd make me want to actually eat them.  The liquid they're packed in stinks, they have a very strange consistency, and they have no flavor.  It took me about a year to figure it out.Drain the noodles and rinse them really well.  Place them in a microwave safe bowl and microwave them (I use the potato setting).  After the first round, drain them in a colander and check the texture, do they still have water in the noodles?  If so, put them back into the microwave and zap them again.  This process removes all of the liquid, and gives the noodles an actual pasta texture and consistency.  And, it allows them to reabsorb whatever sauce you're pairing them with to give them flavor.Once they're ready, you can combine them with ingredients to throw in the oven for an amazing tuna casserole, or throw them into a reduced pasta sauce for an amazing dry spaghetti, or add them at the end of cooking a phad thai.

column9: very good if you handle it correctly
column10: It smelled of dashi/kombo broth when opening.  We drained it in a colander, then put it in a large bowl of water and swished twice, then drained it in a colander.Then boiled it in water for one minute.  Put it back in colander and PATTED IT DRY so attached water would not dilute sauce.  Then COOKED IT in tomato SAUCE for 30 seconds.It was slightly al dente.  It did not upset my stomach.Capitalized words are essential for success.

I gave these noodles a try and although they are not the tastiest they still get the job done.  I am amazed at the nutrition label.  Calories?  Zero.  Total Fat?  None.  Cholestrol?  Absolutely not.  No sugars, no protein, no guilt.  I have been trying to lose weight for quite some time with different diets and these noodles are getting the job done.  They do have a scent when open but that goes away once you rinse under cold water as the cooking instructions states.  I wouldn't recommend eating these noodles by itself.  Instead, add to a pasta sauce, a salad dressing or soup and it'll taste fine.  They absorb the sauce very well. Although the fishy smells washes off with proper rinsing and boiling the texture of the noodles is nauseating. I was literally gagging as I tried to swallow them. When you chew them they break a part like some odd watery substance. I have used the noodle in several recipes and truly impressed with the versatility.  I started with stir fry and was satisfied with the taste but found the leftovers fantastic.  The flavor of the sauce soaked into the noodle and wow.  I used them in a chicken Tetrazzini and again they took in the light flavor of the sauce and very satisfying.  The most appreciated (by my sister) was as an extention to spaghetti noodles.  She has been just been classed as Diabetic and a 1/2cup of pasta just does not look right so used the noodle as an extender.  I did soak the noodle in flavored water(powdered garlic,onion and water) while making the sauce just to bump the flavor and it worked very well.  So I guess you could say five stars is just fine with me.

If you want a noodle without the guilt, well, this ain't it.  Better to limit your "real" noodle intake and enjoy it than suffer with this.  I've tried Tofu Shirataki Noodles from the local health food store which are a bit better, but nothing replaces the real thing.  These are rubbery, no flavor really, and don't digest well.  Save your shekels.

Ok these things are pretty amazing if you are on a low carb diet and want the pasta "experience."  They are quite versatile.  WE have used them in Italian dishes, asian, and indian/thai.  They absorb flavor well, I think just as well as regular pasta.  The package of 6 angel hair bags is great, but I have to admit the bags are quite small.  Really an individual portion for most appetites.  The price I think was a bit high--17 per package--when I bought.  At 14 bucks/6pack its a better deal...just as good as you'll find at your local asian grocery.For you paleo types out there, it went well with "italian sauce" (ie, ground turkey sauteed with onions in tomato sauce).  But frankly it goes even better with Asian dishes.  Open bag, drain, run hot water over them, and throw in wok with a bit of oil and tamari.  add chicken or whatever you eat and its delicious.  Added them to coconut curry last night=amazing.  But the all time best was adding them into our Pho that we got from local restaurant.  We asked them to hold the noodles and give extra basil/bamboo shoots, etc.  they thought I was crazy, but its pretty darn good.I dont miss pasta at all.  These come a lot closer than other options like spaghetti squash. Get them!

I must say that for me these noodles are perfect. To be clear I am a guy(lazy, messy, tired after work etc who does not like to cook much and also was diagnosed with a gluten allergy).  I would highly recommend these noodles to anyone who trying to avoid gluten and at the same time those trying to lose some weight. They are an excellent source of fiber. I am not however a huge pasta guy so the taste or lack thereof is not a huge factor. I usually order from Amazon or asian food grocer online (Both are fine). FYI I eat these noodles nearly every day since they make good leftovers.How I prepare them:Rinse them in a stainer under HOT water for two minutes(kills the smell)Pasta sauce out of a jar brought to boilDump in the noodles.I also add a few spices and grill up some chicken a few times a week.These noodles can be made in under 5 minutes as I just mix it with pasta sauce that I get from a jar. It is quick and lets face it 0 calories. Add some sauce and a piece of chicken and we are talking about a 200-250 calorie meal. There are some better ways to make these I am sure but I really just want something quick and low calorie. I hope this helps.

column9: HERE'S THE REAL SCOOP ON SHIRATAKI!!
column10: Okay, so I heard about the amazing Shirataki noodle and decided to give it a try.  After MUCH research and deliberation I decided to try both the "miracle noodle" (zero calorie, glucomannan, no tofu) and the House Foods (40 calorie per bag, tofu and yam flour) varities.  BOTH arrived today, so I decided to try both and give an unbiased review.#1 - Anyone who says these noodles have a repulsive odor, has never eaten fish before.#2 - anyone who says these noodles have a repulsive texture, has never eaten ramen, or udon noodles before.I put a small pot of boiling water on the stove, brought to a boil.  Opened the bag, put noodles into a strainer, and rinsed 10-15 seconds under cold water.  Then I put the noodles in pot of boiling water.I purposely sniffed the bag.. and yes.. it has a medium to mild "fishy" odor, nothing worse than salmon.  If you don't like this, then don't sniff the bag.  The "miracle noodle" had slightly less of this odor.I purposely sniffed the boiling water after about 1 minute, and yes, it had an odor, not so much fishy anymore, as almost plastic-y.. kind of hard to describe... again, don't sniff the steam if this bothers you.After 3 minutes of boiling (for the House foods brand), and 2 mintues (for the miracle noodle brand), I poured into the strainer again, and rinsed with HOT water for 10 seconds.  I then drained, and put back into the small pot, and added half a flavor packet from a pack of ramen noodles (chicken flavor).IT TASTED JUST LIKE RAMEN!  I was very excited.  The noodles (as other reviews state) have no flavor on their own, but take on asian flavors nicely.  As for being a "spaghetti substitute," these would probably do the same as if you put ramen noodles under some spaghetti sauce.. not quite right.. but not the fault of the noodles, just not the intent of an asian noodle.As for the texture, these noodles actually get FIRMER as you cook them, instead of softer (like regular noodles).  If your're a fan of "al dente" pasta, then this is for you.  YES < they are a bit firm, but not hard like rubber bands (like other reviews have said).  And not slimy in the slightest, I don't get why people have said this (again, felt just like ramen noodles in my mouth).  I love al dente pasta myself, and found the texture preferable to normal ramen noodles.  The "miracle noodle" is slightly firmer, and more transluscent (like more tradition ramen noodles).I ate one bag of each, and loved every bite of both.  This was also about 4 hours ago, and I felt full this whole time (not uncomfortably full, just not hungry).I'm VERY glad I took a chance on this.  Perhaps if you have a picky pallet, this isn't for you.  But if you like Ramen noodles, then I'm telling you give these a try.  One bag (of either) is about the same volume as one packet of Ramen noodles, but at a fraction of the calories (or zero in the case of miracle noodles).  I plan on experimenting with other spices, such as bullion, and asian "flavor packets" found at the grocery store.Hope this helps!!

It definitely helps to try these out not expecting a perfect pasta replacement. These are way more like the noodles you find in instant cup soups. And yes they did have an odor when first opened, but nothing terrible, and it was gone after a few min. of washing them in cold water.Some have said they can't work as a substitute in spaghetti, and maybe that's true if you're expecting an exact replica for a flour based pasta spaghetti dish, but I did try it, and I was happy with the results. I followed the advice of rinsing them then patting them dry, I did 2 packages of them at once. While that was going on, I was boiling water. I am a stickler for calorie counting and portion control nowadays, so I pre-measure and freeze most of what I eat. I had a measured portion of low cal. spaghetti sauce in a ziplock bag I was heating up in the water, but put it in too soon, as the bag broke and I ended up with spaghetti sauced water. So I made use of the accident to flavor the noodles. I boiled some pearl onions in the spaghetti sauced water, then added the noodles. Let that all cook for about 7min then heated up a second pouch of spaghetti sauce. I strained the noodles, put them in a bowl with the onions and now heated sauce and added some diced tomatoes and a couple shots of hot sauce. I wanted the tomatoes to cook a bit so I further nuked the lot for a few min in the microwave. Then topped it with a slice of fat free american cheese. It was actually pretty good. The noodles were on the chewy side, but not in a bad way. And they do soak up whatever you flavor them with. So as long as that part is good, the whole dish should be good. I think with these noodles anything spicy will work best. Which is why I added the hot sauce, something I wouldn't do with reg. pasta. I'll probably try a hot asian dish next.But it's really nice to know I can eat twice the amount of the low cal/carb pasta I have been using which was 175cal a serving, and actually cut the calories of the dish down to basically just the 40cal in the sauce and 25 cal in the cheese!!!
This product arrived in a timely manner and the product was what it said i would be.  I will be ordering this again.
