For this review you're going to get two opinions.  Darshan1 and chocolate enthusiast extraordinaire, Darshan's Mom.Darshan says:  As an amateur chocolate consumer, I found this fairly similar in taste to Hershey's Special Dark at first, um, chomp, but after a couple chews, I noticed it's a fair amount creamier and much more satisfying than Special Dark.  I favor milk chocolate (I think Cadbury milk is my favorite) so this was a little bitter for me (it actually is a little stronger than Special Dark), but compared to some 82% stuff that my mom sometimes has where I feel like I'm going to choke for the bitterness, this was quite good.  A very good compromise (in my opinion) if we were going to split a chocolate bar for dessert. I like the fact that it's "Fair Trade" chocolate since a lot of cocoa harvesting involves some harsh child labor practices, and since it's one of the few fair trade brands that I can get at the nearby regular grocery store instead of having to trek to a gourmet store, I'd probably start buying their milk chocolate variety.Darshan's Mom says:  Newman's Own organic dark chocolate satisfyingly combines the creaminess of milk chocolate with the taste of a somewhat mild, but luscious, dark chocolate.  Since it's merely 54% chocolate, the heavenly, bitter tang of 75% to 8o% chocolate is missing.  However, the rich smoothness of the product almost makes up for that.  Being a confirmed chocoholic, I've taste tested chocolate in France, Belgium and Switzerland, the holy trinity of European chocolate according to a local chocolate store owner, but, in order to be perfectly fair, of course, I've forced myself to sample chocolate in Germany and Italy as well. I've made pilgrimages to American restaurants famous for their chocolate temptations, visited a cocoa plantation in Tobago and prepared numerous chocolate desserts over the years.  So, I think I know chocolate.  Yes, for those of us who crave deep, dark chocolate, Newman's Own comes up a little short, but it is surprisingly delicious nevertheless.  Another plus, it's organic.  If it's priced well compared to the better-known European chocolate bar brands, it could easily become one of my top choices for everyday enjoyment.

This chocolate is perfection.  The texture is so smooth and melts in your mouth not too fast and not too slow.  Dark chocolate but not too dark, seriously just perfect!  And it's organic, which makes it even better!  Would buy this in a heartbeat.

What I mean by its neither here nor there is that it is somewhere in between a dark and a milk chocolate. The result is that it lacks the intensity, bitterness and depth of dark chocolate yet is slightly creamier, yet it also lacks the smoothness and sweetness of a milk chocolate. So it really is not my favorite at all. Plus, it has a strange aftertaste that I have difficulty describing. All in all, its very decent and much better than an ordinary Hershey's bar yet is just not satisfying enough that I would want to get it again. I do appreciate the fact it is organic and like the size and thickness of the bar, but I just didn't enjoy it that much.

column9: Dark Chocolate for Milk Chocolate Luvers
column10: This chocolate, unlike many dark chocolates I've tried, has more the sweetness and smoothness of milk chocolate. There is very little bitterness. The cocoa level is 54 percent, and is organic, making it a less guilty indulgence.This chocolate goes well with Pinot Noir!

column9: If You Enjoy Dark Chocolate You Will Enjoy This
column10: Regardless of a food brand's mission statement, it all comes down to taste. I don't drink organic milk because of a concern for cows, but because it tastes so very very good. And I wouldn't buy this chocolate if it tasted more like chalk. Well luckily, it tastes very good for dark chocolate. Even my wife, who while liking chocolate in general does not like the straight stuff, says that this is the best dark chocolate she's tasted.For what it's worth, I sampled some Starbucks in house chocolate last week, and it was noticeably more bitter than this.I would prefer thinner bars, these are a bit hard on the dental work to bite off, but in general a quality product.

This chocolate bar was so good.  Dark chocolate is my favorite kind of chocolate and this bar didn't disappoint.  To me it tastes like a Dark Chocolate Hershey bar.  This chocolate bar leaves a good aftertaste.  I tasted the chocolate for a good half hour or so afterwards.  It kept making me want more.This bar is 330 calories, a little more than I wanted in one sitting so I divided it into 3 separate servings.  This was easy to do because it's like 6 little squares put together so I just broke them into 3 different bars.I highly recommend these chocolate bars.

column9: Dark Chocolate for Beginners (misnamed but tastes good)
column10: Perhaps they should have given this bar a different name, maybe "Dark Chocolate for Beginners". It is a "Dark Chocolate" bar but with only 54% cacao. It is still more than typical milk chocolate (in the 30s), but it may confuse fans of dark chocolate. This is more of a bridging-the-gap type of a chocolate. For someone coming to this from the off-the-shelf mass-market milk chocolate, this is not as "bitter" as typical dark chocolate, so if you want to eat healthier chocolate, this may be an option. It is also sweet, sweeter than most of the dark chocolates (60%) I recall trying out, and it does not have the "bitter" taste.However, for someone coming to this from the 60% and 70% and 80% dark chocolate, this may come as a surprise, as it is sweeter and it doesn't have the high percentage of cocoa one would expect. Newman also has a 70% "Super Dark" chocolate Newman's Own Organics Super Dark (70%) Chocolate Bar, 3.25-Ounce Bars (Pack of 12) but I haven't tried that so I can't really compare. However, the choice of a name (70% being called Super Dark) is a hint that these are perhaps intended more for the mass-market grocery store consumer, not the dark chocolate connoisseur.Nutrition-wise, the whole chocolate bar (2.25oz or 64 grams) has 330 calories and it provides one-third of the RDA fat calories and two-thirds of the RDA saturated fat calories. There is 0% cholesterol, 0% trans-fat and only traces of sodium (5mg). Also good is 4g of fiber and 3g of protein, but a jumping up and down 28g of sugars. It is candy after all :-) The cocoa is Rainforest Alliance certified.The bar is made in a way that can be broken in six (probably uneven unless you are careful) pieces, so theoretically you can break it into six servings, which significantly lowers the calories and fat intake. More realistically, one-third of the bar is a reasonable compromise for one person per day, bringing it down to 110 calories with 10% RDA fat and 22% RDA saturated fat. (the numbers are based on the standard 2000 calorie diet found in most of the food labels).

Scharffen Berger's Extra Dark chocolate is much smoother.  Newman's tastes like it has some powdered milk in it.

I can't tell the difference between organic and non-organic chocolate just based on the taste of it.  I highly doubt many people could.  But the taste is really great.  Not as bitter as some dark chocolate is, and it melts really well in the mouth - not waxy at all like a cheaper version might be.This is really good chocolate, period.

I shared my chocolate bar with 2 friends. We all agreed that we liked it. I'm just starting to get into dark chocolate. I've been a long time milk chocolate lover. This bar is only 54% cocoa so it wasn't too bitter or overwhelming for me. I really liked the taste and texture and will buy this chocolate.What my friends said:"The dark chocolate was smooth with very little bitterness.  If you let it melt on your tongue for a few seconds then sipped a 20 year old single malt, it was quite dignified , just like Paul Newman himself." -- Fred"The chocolate was rich yet very smooth and delicious, just like Paul Newman himself."  -- Jackie

column9: Serious Chocolate for the Kid in You
column10: Yummy! This delicious quality chocolate bar makes me feel like a kid.  Who cares if it is good for you.  Its full flavor is neither bitter nor too sweet.  Just a nibble will "fix" your craving.  I feel better that antioxidants taste so good.Highly recommended.

I just LOVE dark chocolate! The highger the cocoa concentration, the better is my motto. While this bar's concentration is higher than a lot of readiliy available drug/grocery store picks it really doesn't shine for me. There are so many more easily purchased choices out there that are truly delicious. Highlight of this bar? It's Organic and that's important to a lot of people today. Low Point? It has a really waxy consistency that borders on the artificial. Mouthfeel is important to me...if I'm going to "spend" calories eating dark chocolate, I want it to be the most amazing taste experience available. The overall taste is not bad, there is just better to be had. I recommend that Newman's Own go back to the drawing board on this one. Oh, and it's kind of an odd sized bar. Larger than an "individual" bar, but smaller than the average multi-serving bar (in case anyone is interested!).

column4: Y. R. Wu "The will to win is nothing without ...
column9: Smooth, not too sweet.  Very good though a bit simple for hard core chocoholics
column10: Summary: a very good "starter" gourmet dark chocolate for those who aren't into strong flavors...We eat a disturbing amount of chocolate around our house, whether it's Lindt, Ghiradelli, Sees, Cadbury, Toblerone, Scharffen Berger, Godiva or even Hershey's, we've had it.We tend towards the very dark chocolates, although i do have to say we had some Lindt in the 90% range which was just a bit too sharp.  I'm also a espresso aficionado.This chocolate has a very smooth texture.  It's well tempered and starts out quite firm in the mouth, then melts to a very smooth consistency.  It's fairly sweet for a dark chocolate - not as sweet as a Hershey's special dark, but more than other dark chocolates in this range.  54% cocoa gives a much stronger taste than Milk chocolate and here it still has a very creamy finish with no sharp aftertaste.  Still, I found it simply "chocolate" without any accompanying flavors you tend to notice in the stronger chocolates.If you like your coffee black or like cappuccinos then this might be for you.  If you drink Turkish coffee or espresso then this probably won't have enough punch for you.

I eat a lot of good chocolate like Valrhona, Domori, & Green & Black. Newman's Own is in no way on par with better chocolates, but it is better than average. They tried hard to make it something special but I won't be buying again. There are much better chocolate bars out there.

column9: Ethically responsible and organic, but there are other brands to try to figure out what tastes best to you
column10: I received 1 bar via the Amazon Vine program to review. Let me just say I love chocolate in any form, but dark chocolate is probably 4th down on the list of favorites.  That being said, I find most dark chocolate is either too bitter for my liking, often leaving me with a slight pucker in my mouth and/or a chalky after-taste.  Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate was a pleasant surprise on the taste front.  Yes, it's dark chocolate, but no bitter aftertaste.  It's smooth and just sweet enough to remind me of bittersweet chocolate, more than dark.The reason for 4 and not 5 stars has more to do with the price of being environmentally aware.  Perhaps that explains the price hike on this bar of chocolate versus some others?  I love that Newman's company puts a portion of its proceeds back into helping others, and that too may explain the price hike, but I don't have to like it.  Not when other brands are just as tasty and cost much less.Similar chocolate in quality and taste: Dagoba Dark (59%) Semisweet Bar, 2.0-Ounces Bars (Pack of 12) focuses too on being environmentally friendly.  My suggestion if you like dark chocolate and want to help the planet, you consider Dagoba, Newman's Own Organics and Endangered Species Black Panther, Extreme Dark Chocolate (88%), 3-Ounce Bars (Pack of 12) for your own head to head taste test to determine your favorite.If you're going to be purchasing your chocolate with the environment and natural ingredients in mind, you should also figure out which one tastes best to you.

column9: It is Dark Chocolate and therefore its a fine choice...
column10: If you are primarily a milk chocolate lover then Dark Chocolate can take some getting used to as it does have an initial taste that leans to more bitter than sweet.  But, that is not to say that it isn't good or that you won't grow to love it.  Besides its the dark not milky that is so good for you.  Plus, this is organic which makes it even better for you.  Paul Newman's Own is always a good choice brand wise and I feel that this product is no exception.

column9: Delicious taste and profits go to charity
column10: While I can't say that I ever ate a piece of chocolate I didn't like, this chocolate bar is up there with the best of them.  It had a nice rich, sweet flavor and disappeared pretty quick at our house when I left it on the nook table to share.  I like to support Newman's Own products as they donate all of their after tax profits to charity. Plus this chocolate bar was also organic, so what is not to like? If it wasn't fattening it be the perfect food.

column4: Jeff Wignall "The Joy of Digital Photography"
column9: Chocolate Excellent, Newman's Own Great, But Vine Only Sent 1 Bar
column10: This is great dark chocolate. It is 54% cocoa which might make you think it could be bitter but it is not at all: it has a very light and enjoyable sweet taste. It also has a very silky texture. I have had almost every expensive dark chocolate out there (me a chocolate addict? Big time!) and I have to say this is one of the nicest surprises--a very nice chocolate, not too sweet, still tastes like dark chocolate but none of the "too dark" taste you often get from expensive chocolates. Also, it's organic.You have to hand it to the folks at Newman's Own, they not only find great products, but they do wonderful work in the world. Paul Newman left a legacy that is far larger than his films: he left the world with a dose of great humanity.That said: The Vine newsletter said this would be 12 bars, I got one. When I wrote and asked why, I got a typical runaround from some "customer service" employee (I think they need to rename this people something that better reflects what they really do which is to, as we said in the 60's, shine you on) who gave me the company line. In other words, our mistake, tough luck. But I take this Vine program seriously and put a lot of time and effort into reviewing products and I think if Amazon is going to ask Vine members to review things fairly, they should treat the people who do the reviewing fairly.But the chocolate, out of this world good. And Newman's Own? Perhaps the best organization on earth.

column4: Gina Pera "Is It You, Me, or Adult A.D.D.?, a...
column9: My new favorite dark chocolate bar, organic and "slave-free"
column10: I tend to prefer darker chocolate -- 65-70%.  So I was expecting this 54% bar to be sweeter or creamier, thus not entirely to my liking.I found this bar neither waxy nor chalky, as some of the darkest chocolates can be. Neither is it quite creamy. Rather, it melts very slowly in my mouth, leaving none of the bitterness of some dark chocolates and none of the filminess, either. I guess you'd call it a clean finish!Neither my palate nor my reporting skills are entirely sophisticated when it comes to chocolate. I can't pinpoint the flavor as being like that of any tropical or tree fruit. And, like most people, I have my preferences and so my opinion is highly subjective.What I can say is that I like this bar very much and will be interested in the other bars in this Newman's line.  I also like patronizing this brand, as they do so much good work through its non-profit efforts.  I also like the fact that it is organic and that, as best I can determine, this is slave-free chocolate.  That is worth paying a few cents extra for, in my opinion.
Has a nice texture and not too bitter, but I would not pay more for it compared to other dark chocolates.

I had high expectations of this chocolate as I've enjoyed other Newman's Own products.  However, this dark chocolate left much to be desired.  It didn't have a very "cocoa" taste- I could barely tell it was dark chocolate.  In fact, it was just bland in general.I buy dark chocolate nearly every week from other brands and I'm used to it having a more distinct smell and flavor.

column9: Great Tasting Dark Chocolate - I'm a fan!
column10: As I get older I prefer darker chocolates to the more sweeter milk chocolates I liked as a younger person.  Now I find it hard to get tasty dark chocolates that are made with the quality you would expect for the price.  Dark chocolate in high percentages - 50 to 70% cocoa (or higher) are usually fairly pricey.  If you are planning to look for organic on top of that, then expect to pay even more.  I was very excited to try Newman's Own Organics Chocolate - not only is it a trustworthy brand name, but Amazon's prices make it the perfect fit for my dark chocolate cravings.  I feel a lot less guilty about buying high quality, thanks Newman's... thanks Amazon.

column9: Good dark chocolate, if you like that kind
column10: I don't eat that much dark chocolate -- or of any kind, for that matter -- but I do have a sense of what dark chocolate should taste like: slightly bitter, and not very sweet.  Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate Bar fits that bill.  I wouldn't exactly call it "mild" in flavor, but it's not as overwhelming in taste as some other dark chocolates that I've tried.  As with most good organic foodstuff, the taste is as good or better than the non-organic versions.

This particular chocolate bar was "perfect" in my opinion, since I often find dark chocolate bars to be "too bitter." Instead, this one seems somewhere in the middle, between the REALLY Dark chocolate and the light chocolate. It is smooth, and enjoyable.While the information lists a bar as a "single serving," I consider one square (there are 6 in a bar) to be adequate to meet my desire for chocolate, and still maintain my girlish figure. ;-)Background for those who care about organics, fair trade, and sustainability:Nell Newman co-founded the Organics line back in 1982, and it split from Newman's Own in 2001. The company has a serious focus on organics, and is a member of the Rainforest Alliance, ensuring that the chocolate is not only grown organically, but also in a socially and ecologically appropriate manner. Newman confirms that all chocolate is purchased at fair trade prices.Since the Rainforest Alliance recently issued a joint statement with Fairtrade and UTZ Certified, you can be assured that this chocolate was not produced by slave labor.For most people considering purchasing these bars, this is not an issue, however, I try to be conscious of social issues, and researched this information for those who find it important.

I'll admit that I am spoiled by really great chocolate from my local chocolate shop so this bar was a bit of a disappointment.  It was hard, waxy and not very flavorful.  Not even quite as good as that chocolate bar from that big factory in PA.  On a personal note, as a Vine reviewer, I only received one bar instead of the entire pack.  Unless you're really into organic, you can buy better chocolate at your nearby superstore.

I consider myself something of a chocolate connoisseur, I love it and have tried many different types and forms of chocolate at quite a few "tastings".I had hopes that this chocolate would be divine.  It wasn't.  It tasted waxy and strangely, not all that chocolate'y.  It was also shockingly small after seeing the caloric content -300+ calories in a bar barely the size of my iPhone!Since I work on a system of "worth the calories or not" when it comes to sweets...I immediately placed this chocolate bar in the "not worth the calories" category, and that is why I can't recommend this product.  Seek chocolate cravings elsewhere!

Like most dark chocolate this bar is not sweet nor creamy; however, it doesn't have one of those "I just gotta have it" tastes to it either.  It comes scored in six squares so you can break a piece off when you're having one of those "I could rip the curtains off the window if I don't get some chocolate," days.  If you are purchasing it because you prefer organic, then you won't hate it, but I'm not really in love with it either.

This 54%-cocoa dark chocolate bar from Newman's Own is tasty enough. Picky chocolate lovers might find it too sweet, but it whacks the craving as far as I'm concerned. I just find it way too hard. It's a quarter inch thick, so it's a solid chunk of chocolate when you bite into it or break off a piece. I've been putting it in the microwave for a few seconds to soften it, but I can see disaster looming there!
This was a good but not incredible chocolate bar. A little too much sweetness masked the chocolate flavors. I've definitely had better but overall its quite tasty.

This is very nice chocolate with a strong, dark-chocolate flavor. The finish is also very nice with a hint of cherry flavor. We compared it favorably to Calibut and Ghirardelli dark, among others. The only reason it loses one star is due to initial waxy texture.

I love dark chocolate and, in fact, prefer it to the sweeter milk chocolate.  While this was a perfectly satisfactory bar of dark chocolate, it didn't stand out as exceptional in any way.  I'm disappointed that, as of the writing of this, there is no price listed for this product.  My guess, based on the branding and the organic nature of the product, is that this is going to be priced above the average for this size chocolate bar, which would make it more expensive than I'd be willing to pay for a product that was really just average in quality.

This is good chocolate and I probably would have eaten as much of it as I had.  The only dark chocolate that is better in my experience was some from Switzerland I received for a Christmas present.  The fact that Newman's Own is organic is a nice touch and for some reason makes it seem okay to eat more of it.I don't think you will be disappointed.

I pretty much love any kind of chocolate (other than white chocolate which I can't stand). I enjoy milk chocolate as well as dark chocolate so that may explain why I liked this so much. It seems to me that it is in the middle, between the two in flavor. It doesn't have the totally creamy, sweet flavor of milk chocolate, but doesn't have the bite sometimes associated with dark chocolate (and no aftertaste I sometimes find with dark). Some folks may find that being in the middle equals bland but I found it delightful.The bar itself it a bit bigger than an iPhone and bigger than a Hershey's chocolate bar, but it's not huge. The bar was scored into 6 squares and I ate 3 yesterday and 3 today. I found that amount completely satifying and felt no real desire to eat the entire bar in one sitting -- which is a VERY good thing.The organic nature of the bar also appeals to me since I am trying to be more aware of the chemicals I put into my body. I eat my share of junky food, but am trying to eat more fruits and veggies and this organic bar fits in with that.For anyone that enjoys chocolate, this bar is very, very good!

column9: Good dark chocolate, but not great
column10: It's hard to be critical of dark chocolate. Like pizza and sex, when it's good it's great and when it's not good it's still good. Both of the adults in our family tried this and we're both dark chocolate fans and we had the same "good, but nothing special" reaction.So, this is a good dark chocolate, not great. At 54%, it's one of the lower concentration "lighter" darks out there. I'd probably be a bigger fan of their "super dark" but my guess is it would still pale in comparison to other dark darks from Ghirardelli, Endangered Species, etc.If I'm going for a natural eco-friendly choice, I'd stick with Endangered Species. If I want a premium brand I can find anywhere, Ghirardelli has Newman beat there too.

column9: good dark chocolat but a bit sweet.
column10: This chocolate is good, but it tastes more like a candy chocolate due to its sweetness.  It has a good mouth feel and texture but for "dark" chocolate it tastes a little to sweet.  Packaging is good, and the sample I got was well preserved, not old or dried out like some chocolate bars you get in the store.Overall as a candy or treat this is good, environmentally responsible chocolate.

column9: 54% Cocoa Selection That Split Our Household On Taste--Try One Before Making A Big Investment!
column10: So, I don't really know how to express my feelings over a chocolate bar.  In my household, there is no other choice besides dark chocolate--that's all we do.  Whether it's the conventional Special Dark or the ritzy high end selections, we've tried it all.  I was excited to check out Newman's Own, an organic variation weighing in at 54% cocoa.  When we go upscale, we tend to venture into the 72% range, so I was interested to see the difference.Me:  I liked the bar.  It was appropriately sweet (but perhaps not dark enough) and had a smoothness I enjoyed.  Spouse:  Didn't like it as much as I did.  Not enough cocoa content, rather generic in conception.  Value:  While we split over quality, we agreed that the price tag on this chocolate was probably a bit high.  We've had better alternatives for less--in some cases a lot less!  Obviously, no one is going to hate a chocolate bar--I'd just recommend that you sample one before investing in a large quantity.  Make sure it delivers the bang you require for your buck!3 Stars from my spouse, 4 stars from me--product at 3 1/2 stars.  But since I write the review, I get the round-up!

While I prefer German chocolate, this was excellent--not too sweet, the way I like it.  Most American candy is way too sweet.  This was just right.  The "organic" label will appeal to some, but I simply thought it was a quality candy bar.

I love Dark Chocolates so does my daughter, But Newman's Dark Chocolate bar does not have enough coco to make it a true dark chocolate.It tastes like any other milk chocolates that I have tasted before nothing much better, I know these are organic chocolates, But what is so different from others? I do not think you can make chocolates with just inorganic materials!If you love Rich Coco taste you will surely love this Lindt Excellence Extra Dark Chocolate 85% Cocoa, 3.5-Ounce Packages (Pack of 12)Having said, Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate is okay but for me it was on the sweeter side, I love chocolates that tastes slightly bitter...
Rich and smooth, with slight crumbly texture. It has a nice balance of dark rich bitterness with a satisfying sweetness. Very creamy mouth feel. An excellent dark chocolate. Very easy eating.

column9: Not the best chocolate but still quite good
column10: Though I like the organic idea I do not like that much organic food suffers in taste.  So it is very pleasant that this chocolate is available.  I would not compare it to some of my favorite premium chocolates but it is certainly as good as most of the mass market chocolate bars.  I prefer dark chocolate that is more bitter than this but I know my tastes are not the norm so most people will enjoy it more than I.  A good idea for a more healthy treat.

column9: Bland Dark Chocolate Flavor; All Profits Go To Charity
column10: The Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate Bar offers a 2.25 ounces of smooth but unimpressive dark chocolate flavor.  It's of medium taste quality, in my opinion, like it's missing something.Packaged in a small brown and black wrapper, this candy bar is created using 54% cocoa, which has proven to be beneficial for cardiovascular well-being, reducing your risks of blood clots, heart attacks and strokes.  On the downside, this bar contains 330 calories, which compared to a regular candy bar without healthy cocoa ingredients, is a high fat content.  When compared to other bars packed with healthier cocoa, the Newman's Own Organics dark chocolate bar does compare in that regard.Newman's Own gives all of it's profits to charity, and the company motto is "Shameless Exploitation in Pursuit of the Common Good."  They are a company that does the right thing and sets the standard by which other companies should follow.Just for the chocolate, I'd probably pass.  But if I have to have chocolate, and I do have to have it, I'd choose Newman's Own Organics over another brand that doesn't use good business practices and donate their profits to charity; right up there with supporting mom and pop stores and shopping local grocers instead of buying at the nearest big-box super center.So it's not just a chocolate bar.  It's a chocolate bar that pays it forward.

column9: Too restrained for dark chocolate lovers
column10: This is a fairly high quality confection.  The flavor is smooth, round, and fruity, almost raisin-y.  However, I am a dark chocolate lover, and dark chocolate lovers won't be seduced by refinement alone.So I consulted my spouse, a light/milk chocolate lover, and we both agree that while tasty, Newman's Own Organics dark lacks that subtle, almost spicy bitterness that brings out the complexity and assertive flavors of chocolate at varying cacao levels.  Now obviously 54% cacao isn't going to register on the palate like 70%, 75% or 90% cacao, but there can still be that "snap" to chocolate, which is often compared to notes in coffee or chili pepper, even at the lower percentages.  I can still, for example, perceive that note in many grocery store brand chocolate morsels, although the overall quality of those will not match the Newman's.  By comparison, the Newman's has a waxiness that reminds me of Dove or Cadbury's.I will say that this is probably a safe choice for company, where a little something sweet is desired that won't be too much for less-than-diehard fans of the dark stuff.  It's agreeable; just not distinctive enough to kill for, which is pretty severe criticism where chocolate is concerned!

column9: The lighter side of dark chocolate
column10: We have a bit of a dispute over these bars in my house, so I can say with some authority that they are right for some people, not for others.  At 54% cocoa, these are darker than milk chocolate but much more mild than many of the dark chocolates you can get.  I personally found them lighter than I like in a dark chocolate and a little waxy.On the other hand, my daughter is a huge fan of dark chocolate, and gives this the thumbs up.  If you like your dark chocolate on the light side, you may like these too.At 2.25 ounces, these are about the total size of a retail candy bar, and a smidgen bigger than some. They're short and wide, divided into 6 nicely stamped squares. For those into that sort of thing, they're made from organic ingredients and support Paul Newman's charitable works.

column9: Possibly the best dark chocolate ever
column10: Ok, so I am a little biased. I adore the late Paul Newman, his family, his enterprise, his charity, and all of his products. But I also love me some dark chocolate! I take my chocolate tasting very seriously and wouldn't give it high marks just based on sheer good will. This is some seriously good stuff! Even though I love dark chocolate, I am not what one would call a chocoholic. I have restraint. I typically have a bar in my cupboard, then after dinner break off a piece or two. I savor it, then I leave it at that. Tonight I tried a piece of this delicious confection had to eat half the bar all at once. It was SO GOOD! What I love about it is it's creamy consistency. You usually find that in only milk chocolate, whereas dark chocolate usually has a sharp, almost bitter taste to it. You don't get any of that bitter taste in this bar at all - and yet it's a true dark chocolate. How do they do that? There are lots of subtle undertones of flavors, and it makes for an amazing dessert. And of course coming from Paul Newman, it's heaven sent.Bonus too that they took such great care in choosing the best fair-trade organic chocolate. That's a big deal because if you look at most commercial chocolate sources, it makes the diamond industry look tame. This makes Newman's Organic a truly guilt-free delight. Enjoy!

column9: Great, but even darker might be better for my taste
column10: Very goo bar but a little sweet for my taste... I like my chocolate even darker. I compared it with similar bar from Trader Joe's with the same 54% cocoa, although the Trader Joe's bar is a huge one pounder. The Newman's bar was slightly smoother, perhaps just a little more waxy and sweeter. Big plus for Newman's Own is that it is organic and rainforest alliance certified.  Next, I'll need to move up to the next level of dark from Newman's Own. Maybe that will be the perfect bar for me. I know I like the Trader Joe's 70% bar better than this one but the darker version of Newman's Own might be even better.

For those wanting dark chocolate, this simply is going to do the trick.  It's 54% cocoa solids and really quite sweet.  In terms of texture, it's a bit grainier than average.  It's not shiny, but kind of matte, and melts pretty reasonably.Each 2.25 oz (64g) bar has six large-ish squares, making portion control a little challenging.In terms of flavor, this definitely earns a solid three stars.  It's really not bad at all, like a very reasonable cocoa.  It's so sweet that it tastes a little like a really high end milk chocolate at first, with a good finish for a milk chocolate.  All in all, for a dark chocolate this is better than Dove (less "smooth" because it's grainier, but definitely a better finish), but can't hold a candle to a good high end dark chocolate like Lindt.In terms of organic chocolates, Green & Black makes a darker, smoother, better finishing chocolate, and the bars are bigger, too.

This was a really nice flavored dark chocolate.  My family of five each tried and enjoyed it, even my teenage son who doesn't normally enjoy dark chocolate.  As a family we agreed that it is really good chocolate.  However if Hershey's Dark Chocolate is cheaper, we would still by the Hershey's as we all agreed its very comparable in taste.  That said, if organic is something you are looking for in your chocolate, you can't go wrong with Newman's Organic Chocolate Bar.

I happily accepted a review bar as I am a fan of Newman's Own chocolate, usually buying the orange flavored version of this bar Newman's Own Organics Orange Dark Chocolate Bar, 3.25-Ounce Bars (Pack of 12).  (All Newman bars are available in both 2.25 oz and 3.25 oz sizes.)With only 54% cocoa, this bar is not particularly dark tasting, for people who are extra-dark chocolate fans.  To my taste, it is somewhat sweet (not bitter) and almost creamy.  For those wanting a darker chocolate, Newman's does have a 70% cocoa bar: Newman's Own Organics Super Dark (70%) Chocolate Bar, 3.25-Ounce Bars (Pack of 12).I prefer this bar (and its various-flavored versions) to the higher cocoa content bars as an everyday treat that I can have a bit of here and there and enjoy a silky chocolate flavor and yet not feel over-caffeinated afterwards.

My sample bar of chocolate arrived today and I quickly opened it to sample so I could write my review.The chocolate is so delicious that I had difficulty resisting the urge to finish the whole bar in one sitting. I love dark chocolate, and Newman's 54% cocoa is an excellent balance between sweet and bitter.  The melt point is just right for eating. The chocolate is very smooth.Being certified organic is not that important to me, but if you are looking for a great tasting bar of chocolate, this is a good one.

column9: Creamy, Tasty, but Not Too Chocolaty
column10: This chocolate is very creamy and delicious either raw or melted. It is only 54% cacao, which is either very good or not so good, depending on your preferences.My wife and I love dark chocolate, and try to make our chocolate desserts (such as brownies, ganache, mousse, and chocolate buttercream frosting) as chocolaty as possible. This chocolate might not have enough punch for us, compared to theGhirardelli 60% and 70% cacao (bittersweet) chocolate that we usually buy. This chocolate is not as intensely chocolaty as either of those, and is sweeter and more creamy. I enjoy milk chocolate (which has much less cacao than dark chocolate) more than my wife does, and liked this chocolate more than she did.This is a very good start if you are just getting into dark chocolate, though, or are already sure of what cacao level you prefer.

This organic chocolate is absolutely delicious...so smooth and creamy.  There is a rich, deep chocolate taste and excellent texture...not waxey or grainy at all, with just the right amount of sweetness.  Chocoholics...this is the one for you.  Fabulous!

Smooth and rich and so yummy!  What more can you say about good chocolate?  Well, it is also organic.  When I received this candy in my mail, I couldn't wait to open it.  I broke off a piece and put the rest of the bar in the freezer.  I will enjoy another piece later with a glass of wine.

a solid bar, most bars this solid are flaky when you snap them, but not this one.  there's a tart taste,  so you know you're eating dark chocolate, and a creamy aftertaste probably because of the cocoa butter, and a longer lasting tartness on the tongue.  after a few bites i was missing maraschino cherries, and with some reflection, desiring a manhattan, with a cherry, to drink along with the chocolate.  according to the ingredients, my taste buds were on to something, chocolate liquor went into the mix.  i found the bar to be a great treat for adults.sugar 28gtotal fat 22gcalories 330

I honestly wasn't sure what to expect with Newman's Own Organic Dark Chocolate.  I happen to love dark Chocolate but realize it is for some an acquired taste.  Also, the term "organic" can sometimes mean something more natural but less satisfying either because of a harsher flavor or a strange texture.  Neither is a concern here.  This chocolate is not only satisfying for a dark chocolate lover like me but its rich creamy texture makes it an excellent choice for a quality chocolate for those who normally find dark chocoalates too strong.  This is not a quick fix bar to gobble down at lunch or on the run but one to savor with an after dinner beverage.  For a first entry into the chocolate market, I think they have a winner!

I am not a chocolate connoisseur, but I've tasted enough varieties to know some of the differences. I like dark chocolate but still prefer it to retain some sweetness, which can be a tricky balance. (Ever try 95% dark cocoa chocolate? It's like paying $5 to eat a stick of chalk.)This chocolate bar is labeled as 54% cocoa, which is an interesting choice. It has a nice aroma, and the color is somewhere between milk chocolate and one of those European dark chocolate bars. Most importantly, it tastes great. There is a smooth consistency, and it has a really nice blend of sweetness and bitterness. I shared the bar with a couple of other folks, who had the same impression. We give it 3 thumbs up.

column4: Nicki Heskin "Editor, Early Childhood and Bre...
column9: Yummy... but smaller than you average chocolate bar
column10: I found this chocolate bar to be truly delicious.  It has a perfectly respectable ingredient list.. all organics, essentially evaporated cane juice, chocolate liquor, cocoa butter, soy lecithin and vanilla, all USDA organic certified).  The cocoa is listed as "Rainforest alliance certified."The chocolate is only 54% cocoa, so it is not bitter or overwhelming like some dark chocolate.  This would be a nice bar for someone wanting to make the move from milk chocolate, but not liking the super-high-cocoa-content bars.One thing to note is that this bar is smaller than most that I see on the market.  I though that was just the angle of the photo and didn't think much about it, but it actually is smaller.  It comes with scores for 6 square pieces that are a bit larger than I might otherwise give myself, although even with that, I'll admit that I planned to eat one piece and ate two instead!  The chocolate is creamy, and nicely satisfying.  Probably not the bar for a super-serious-chocolate lover, but a nice quality bar for someone wanting to support organics and find something a bit nicer than average, but widely likeable.

column9: Excellent - NOT bitter at all and very rich!
column10: I'm a huge chocolate fan. It's my favorite sweet. I like all types - and this one is really scrumptious. It's rich and creamy without that bitter aftertaste I associate with so much dark chocolate. It's not exactly melt in your mouth but neither is it extremely hard and crunchy. It has a nice texture and I found it very pleasant.It is rich so I don't think I could eat the whole bar at once. I wish it was breakable in smaller chocolate squares - as it did not break off evenly for me. I love organic products and chose to buy them whenever I can and money allows. Everything is better with chocolate!

column9: has what I want from a chocolate bar
column10: While I'm not a chocoholic, what I want out of a chocolate bar is the following: It doesn't give me a migraine (I got my first migraine ever after eating a Dove Bar in the 80's, and I've eaten chocolate from chocolate bars that have been followed by migraines); it's delicious; I feel good immediately after eating it; it's priced right. With the exception of the migraines, this is all subjective, and whether or not consuming a certain food will result in someone getting a migraine is obviously unique to the individual.Chocolate prices have been rising lately (I'm writing this on Feb. 23, 2011), due to a 12% rise in the price of cocoa coming from the Ivory Coast, which is the largest producer of cocoa beans in the world. Other than that the chocolate for Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate Bars are from cocoa grown on Rainforest Alliance Certified farms, I do not know which country these farms are located in, but I imagine that the rise in the wholesale price of cocoa beans affects the entire retail market for chocolate. Non-gourmet chocolate bars are presently priced at under a dollar per ounce retail (e.g., 38 cents an ounce for one type and size Hershey's Dark Chocolate bar, 58 cents an ounce for Lindt), while one type and size of a gourmet Godiva Dark Chocolate bar sells at present for $1.58 an ounce. It looks like the Newman bars are selling for around $1.44 an ounce (I say "looks like" because the retail price depends on the size of each bar, how many are in a pack, etc., etc.). So for gourmet chocolate, that's an acceptable price, IMO.I received one 2.25 ounce bar to sample for review purposes and I found that I could only eat two of the six squares the bar is scored into at one time (and per day) before I felt sated on chocolate. Chocolate and dark chocolate in particular may or may not have some health benefits (you know the drill, what's supposed to be good for us is constantly changing), but I buy dark chocolate bars and eat them one or two squares at a time (per day) because I enjoy eating a little chocolate and in case there really are health benefits. Given my fairly modest chocolate consuming habits, I think I can afford Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate Bars, and so they meet all of my standards for what I want out of a chocolate bar. The taste is quite rich and that suits me fine, as it means that for me, a little bit goes a long way.

This chocolate bar arrived today, and I didn't wait very long before trying it! :) What can I say, I can't resist chocolate. And I liked it!It's 54% cacao, so it's not going to be the most intense dark chocolate experience you've ever had. But it's quite tasty, and if you think the darker chocolates are too bitter, this may be exactly what you were looking for.It probably won't make me break up with my usual indulgence, Ghirardelli's squares, but I'd definitely consider a dalliance from time to time. Mmm, chocolate.

column9: dark chocolate even a milk chocolate lover can like
column10: I have a sweet tooth.I'm not afraid to admit it and normally I only enjoy milk chocolate for my cocoa cravings.  But this dark chocolate could make me change my mind.Now admittedly this bar is only 54% coca, which is not that dark by most standards, but still gives you that rich deep cocoa taste.The bars are 2.25 oz and segmented into six squares per bar.330 calories per bar, 200 from fat.  22g of fat.It is USDA organic, and made with Rainforest Alliance Certified cocoa.And most importantly the flavor......really quite good.  Sweet, but with a bit of that dark chocolate bitterness.  Very smooth and not grainy at all, which lends to a lovely texture and mouth feel as it melts on the tounge.All in all I enjoyed it would love to have some more.  A nice high quality starter dark chocolate, as a lover of milk chocolate I may be falling to the dark side soon.

Delicious dark chocolate bar. Not too bitter, as some dark chocolates can be, but neither is it too sweet. I thought I tasted something a little different in the mix, but the ingredients don't list anyting out of the ordinary. According to the package, the ingredients are Organic Dark Chocolate (Organic evaporated cane juice, organic chocolate liquor, organic cocoa butter, organic soy lechtin and organic vanilla). The cocoa is "Rainforest Alliance Certified" organic, which the Newman's Own Organics has been associated with for years.Another thing that's nice about Newman's Own chocolate is that the company backs its claim that their cocoa beans come from farms and plantations that do not mistreat their workers or engage is slave-labor practices.

I am a HUGE fanatic of dark chocolate. I was excited to try Newman's organic dark chocolate. It's 54% cocoa, which should put it somewhere between not too sweet but not too bitter. It's a small size bar (2.25 oz), and 330 calories. Frankly, if it was larger, I'd feel much guiltier eating it!The chocolate is not very sweet, but not bitter. Actually, it really doesn't have much flavor at all, which was surprising. Compare this to a Dove Dark Chocolate, and the difference is very obvious. Dove is creamy with deep flavor. The Newman's is dry, almost chalky consistency without much flavor at all.Overall I was pretty disappointed in this chocolate. I love that it's organic - just wish it was tastier.

column9: Good, Albet Average Dark Chocolate Bar
column10: A good, not too sweet dark chocolate bar that reminds me of Hershey's Special Dark bar. The difference being that Newman's has less of an after taste. But the biggest difference is that Newman's Own donates 100% of its profits to human services, health, education, arts, and cultural organizations including Hole In The Wall Camps for seriously ill children. On top of a decent organic chocolate bar, you are making the world a little better place. Wonderful.

column9: Not My Cup of Tea... Err, Bar of Chocolate.
column10: I used to hate dark chocolate. I didn't care for its dryer texture or bitter taste. Then I was diagnosed with gestational diabetes and chocolate pretty much became a no-no. Through careful experimentation though, I discovered I could occasionally enjoy a square of dark chocolate with higher cacao percentages because they have less sugar. I began to appreciate the flavor of chocolate without the milky sweetness and have since been a big fan.Keeping that in mind I'm always trying new brands and blends in search of the perfect dark chocolate bar. Unfortunately, as much as I love Newman's Own as a company and many of their other products this chocolate was just not for me. It's too sweet and the vanilla taste came through strong. It melted into a watery consistency in my mouth and almost had an alcohol-like tang to it. Once I'd noticed that tang I checked the ingredient list and sure enough it's made with chocolate liquor which some may like but I personally don't care for when I reach for dark chocolate.At only 54% cocoa this is pretty low on the spectrum of darker chocolates and with it's texture would be a great introduction to dark chocolate for someone who doesn't like it usually. It kind of reminded me of an oversweetened version of Lindt Lindor Truffles Dark Chocolate, 60-Count Box's centers. If you like organic and fairtrade chocolate this is certainly not a bad place to start but I would recommend trying Theo Classic Organic (70% Cacao) Dark Chocolate, 3-Ounce Bars (Pack of 12) (or any other Theo chocolate bars which are my FAVORITE Organic and Fair trade chocolate products) if you're looking for something similar but with a higher cocoa content.

To me, dark chocolate is the only kind worth eating. I've always loved it. I'm aware that many people don't like the flavor. I really think this Newman's Own Organics dark chocolate is a great even for people who normally prefer milk chocolate. It's 54% cocoa, which truthfully is a great balance between sweet and bitter. I personally prefer even more cocoa content, up to 70%, but 54% is a good compromise for those looking for a more traditionally sweet candy bar.Like any dark chocolate, if you're expecting creaminess you won't find it here. The chocolate is hard and not easy to break into squares. That's just the way dark chocolate is. But the texture is great - very consistent. Its flavorful and the 2.25 ounce bar is a perfect size if you're looking to indulge.Newman's Own makes generally fantastic products, pretty much everything I have tried - from their perfect Italian salad dressing, to their crisp pretzels, to this dark chocolate bar - is awesome. They use quality ingredients. And with the millions of dollars they've donated to charities, it's a way to support good causes.

Maybe it is because this chocolate only contains 54 % cocoa (vs. let's say the 70 % Lindt) but I found the taste disappointing. This might be premium chocolate, and it might be organic and Rainforest Alliance-certified. But the flavor still is surprisingly bland and cheap - a tad too sweet and creamy, with a bit of a waxy texture in too thick a bar. This is just a run-of-the-mill dark chocolate and nothing to entice the palate with.

column9: An American Chocolate to be Proud Of
column10: I wasn't expecting much when I bit into this bar, because I'm usually disappointed by American chocolates. Not here. This lovely chocolate has super creamy mouth feel, great dark reddish brown color and most importantly, a clean, classic chocolate taste. Compared with with other premium brands of comparable cocoa content, this bar is a little sweeter and is less bitter.It is important to me that Newman's Own sources chocolate grown on Rainforest Alliance Certified farms, another reason I can feel good about buying this chocolate in the future, which I will. Recommended.

This 54% dark organic chocolate by Newman's Own is passable.  It is very dry, as are the higher percent dark chocolates, but not as flavorful as others, such as the Lindt or Godiva brands.  Although I enjoy many Newman products, I would not buy this chocolate, I enjoy either of the other brands much more.

How can you not love Newman's Own Organics anything let alone Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate?!? These candy bars are so tasty.  They melt nicely in your mouth and just a few blocks really satisfys my need for chocolate!  I love the fact that it is organic, but I really love that it is fair trade as well.  No slave labor in this delicious chocolate candy bar.

Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate (54%) comes in a 2.25 oz bar that packs a great chocolate taste with a hint of orange in the undertone. It is creamy and very satisfying for those moments, minutes, hours, days when nothing but chocolate will satisfy your craving.  Really good quality.  The 2.25 ox bar contains 330 calories, 200 of which come from fat.  While this sounds dreadful, one square of the bar was so satisfying, I was able to leave the rest for another day.

column9: This is what I like in a chocolate bar
column10: This dark chocolate bar is 54% cacao, with a solid chocolate taste--not overly sweet as some bars are, but not at all bitter. The chocolate melts nicely in the mouth without the waxy texture that some cheaper bars have. While the nutrition label lists this bar as one serving, for me it is two generous servings at 2.25 ounces of flavor. It is also 330 calories (200 from fat) which also makes me want to split it into at least 2 servings or share with a friend. It is easily broken into six substantial squares, so that makes sharing easy. Half a bar is a very satisfying treat. If the price is not too hefty, this is a bar worthy of satifying a serious chocolate craving.

column9: Smooth and rich dark chocolate, tastes great, worth trying
column10: I love all types of chocolate but especially dark chocolate. I would consider this to be one of the best dark chocolate bars that I have tried so far. It is very smooth and rich without a bitter aftertaste. These bars are 2.25 oz. and each has 330 calories. For the size of the bar I would consider that 330 well spent calories. The size is just enough to satisfy you without being too large and excessive.These chocolate bars are 100% organic. I don't buy a lot of organic products but it is nice to know that this product is 100% natural.  Each bar contains 54% cocoa which is dark but not the darkest that I have tried. My personal opinion is the darker the chocolate the better it tastes for the most part. These are definitely worth trying.

I have always enjoyed Newman's Own products including the doggy treats but this chocolate didn't do it for me. Could be my aging taste buds but we all taste differently and this didn't excite me. Wasn't a bad taste just kinda bland, not exciting.

column9: nice dark chocolate, but too sweet for my taste
column10: I am a lover of dark chocolate.  Unfortunately, this chocolate will disappoint true dark chocolate lovers.  Its waaaay too sweet!  Its not bad chocolate - its creamy, its rich, its got good cacao flavor, but they put too much sugar in it.  I prefer the very complex, slightly bitter, very dark (71% cacao) Dove Silky Smooth Dark Chocolate instead.  Also, the Newman's chocolate is broken into six relatively large 1.5 x 1.25 inch squares - IMO just a little too large to just put one square in your mouth and allow it to melt away.  The Dove is broken into 1 x 1 inch squares - the perfect size to melt on your tongue.  Even the wrapper on the Dove is better as it is true foil and easily allows you to keep the remaining chocolate wrapped up tight.  The Newman's comes in gold paper meant to look like foil, but its only paper - it does not close well.  Overall, disappointed.

I received a sample of one Newman's dark-chocolate bar through the Vine program. I live in a part of the country where it is warm in the winter and the bar arrived slightly melted. I put it in the refrigerator to return it to a solid state--and I can imagine the shudders of chocolate connoisseurs since chocolate is not supposed to be refrigerated. It causes "blooming," a grayish discoloration of the shine on the chocolate. The chocolate actually did discolor, but that didn't matter to me personally, because I love cold chocolate bars which are crunchy to the teeth and smooth to the tongue.I could go into all the ways that Newman's Own is a great company (it is), the fact that the ingredients in this chocolate are organic and healthier than those in a regular chocolate bar (they are), and that there's a lot of solid research that dark chocolate is good for your health (it is), but since several other reviewers have already covered all that and done a great job, I'll stick to the main issue:How does it taste?In my opinion--and I love chocolate--this bar tastes great. And particularly great for dark chocolate. Many regular dark-chocolate bars are, for my personal preference, rather too bitter. The bitterness that is supposed to be there as an essential part of the flavor experience of dark chocolate is present in this Newman's Own bar, but not to the extent that the bar doesn't offer a sweet treat.As for the texture, to me it felt quite smooth as it melted on my tongue. The aftertaste is excellent. It tastes just as good as the initial bite of the candy.What about the price? I wrote Amazon about the price today, and they wrote back it is going to cost $25.85. The suggested retail price appears to be $35.88 for 12 bars which comes to a little under $3 per 2.25 oz. (64 gm) bar. The Amazon discounted price comes to about $2.16 per bar, which is cheaper than any other source on the Internet is currently selling it.How does it compare to it's conventional, U.S. competitor, Hershey's Extra Dark Chocolate Bar? The Hershey's bars are larger, weighing in at 3.52 oz., and they come in a pack of 14 selling for $31 on Amazon. That's $2.21 for a larger bar. I haven't tasted that bar, but the reviewers who have claim much the same thing I am for this bar for the Hershey bar's taste, that it has great flavor with no bad aftertaste.In the end, since the taste is at least as good as its conventional competitor, the choice for a consumer as to whether to choose this product will probably come down to two main things: a desire to support the company selling it and/or the fact that this bar is organic and has a healthier sugar in it. As for myself, considering those two things, I would personally choose this bar.

column9: As good as any other dark chocolate, but slightly less bitter
column10: Serving size: whole bar (64g)Calories: 330Fat calories: 200 (22g fat, 34% DV)Saturated fat: 13g (65% DV)The fact that all the ingredients are organic should account for some credit. Otherwise, the product tasted similar to any other dark chocolate we have tasted in the past. Slightly less bitter.We weren't thrilled or ecstatic after eating this chocolate, but we have nothing bad to say about it.

Taste is subjective, obviously, other reviews have detailed the product. I'll just add my subjective evaluation. It tasted good to me and I was not bothered by the texture. I prefer a darker chocolate and, at 54%, this bar was sweeter than one that I would buy for myself.

column9: Excellent quality dark chocolate, just the right sweetness.
column10: The Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate is one of the best dark chocolate bars I've ever eaten. My son felt the same way about it too. The flavor was excellent and it was neither overly sweet nor was it bitter like some dark chocolate candy. I would definitely buy this product after trying the sample from Amazon Vine.

column9: Fancy, creamy, and not too bitter!
column10: Newman's is a brand that I'm used to hearing on fig bars, prunes, and other things much healthier than chocolate, so I wasn't sure how good their chocolate was going to be.  I was very pleasantly surprised to find that not only was their chocolate very fancy, but it was also very smooth and not as bitter as other dark chocolates.The packaging, as you can see from the picture on the description page, is very ornately designed, and the bar is the same.  It is divided into sixths, and on each sixth there is an engraved N.The taste, which I was very surprised at, wasn't bitter like Hershey's dark chocolate tends to be, but it wasn't too sweet.  It was just the right bittersweet mixture!  Also, on top of this, it had a very creamy texture, much like milk chocolate would.In one 2.25 ounce bar, there are 330 calories, so I wouldn't necessarily describe this as a healthy snack, but all of the ingredients are organic, making it more nutritious than your average chocolate bar.Overall, it is a deliciously different type of dark chocolate bar that I recommend to all chocoholics (like me).

column9: Yes, you can have it all
column10: Note: by "all" I did not mean *my* chocolate.Newman's own organic dark chocolate is really fine chocolate, more like that you would expect to find at a chocolatier than at a grocery store!  There are things about it which are, in my experience, fairly unique.  It is a dark chocolate with the mouth feel and texture approaching milk chocolate.  It is not chalky, bitter or grainy.  There are ways in which the texture approaches truffles. I am guessing that is  because they use cocoa butter instead of some other oil or fat, like most commmercialy available chocolates.  It is 56% dark; not as dark as some, but in my opinion it strikes a nice balance bot6h smooth and dark.It is made from high quality 100% organic and Rainforest Alliance certified; good for you and the planet.  If that's not enough, Newman's own donates 100% of after tax profit to charity, a product you can feel good about no matter how you look at it!I would say without reservation that htis is the best organic dark chocolate that I have had (and I have had quite a few)!My only real issue with it is that mine is gone and I will have to order some more.

Although it says "dark chocolate" it is 54% so it is really on the mild side.  If you are into dark chocolate, go with something a little stronger as this one is pretty weak.  It is more for those who are into milk chocolate, but want a bite of dark chocolate with it.  All in all, this bar is yummy though so it is good for all chocoholics.

column9: OK, But A Fairly Low Percentage of Cocoa Solids
column10: I've been a fan of Green & Black's Maya Gold, Organic Dark Chocolate with Orange & Spices, 3.5-Ounce Bars (Pack of 5) for many a year, so I was delighted to be offered Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate Bar, 3.25-Ounce Bars (Pack of 12) for review. (There is currently no link availble to the Pack of 12 2.25 ounce bars) I've been anxiously waiting for my package to arrive, as I had discovered a few recipes on the Newman's Own site, one of which is for a Chocolate Angel Cake that sounded just delightful - and a great way to use up some of that chocolate! Imagine my surprise when that Pack of 12 turned out to be a single 2.25 ounce bar!As a result, I really cannot comment on this particular product other than to say it has a nice, smooth chocolate taste, though it is fairly low in cocoa solids. Any other properties that Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate might have as a candy or confection coating or baking ingredient will remain untested. Strictly as a chocolate bar, this is one I can take or leave. Green & Black's - long involved in the organic, sustainable rainforest movement - will remain my go-to dark chocolate bar.

I don't usually eat bars of plain chocolate but I found myself going back to this one, breaking off piece after piece.  It was smooth and not at all bitter.  There was no strange after taste, which I've experienced with some other dark chocolates.  I had planned on saving some to share with my husband but I'm not sure it will last that long...

column9: Not As *Bitter* As Most Dark Chocolates!
column10: I really like NEWMAN'S OWN ORGANIC DARK CHOCOLATE BAR. It's not as bitter as some dark chocolates like Ghirardelli Chocolate Squares Dark Chocolate 60% Cacao, 5.25-Ounce Packages (Pack of 6) but that's due to the lower cocoa content, 54% vs. 60% and higher in others, so it can be a good or bad thing depending on how you like your dark chocolate to taste.For me, this is just right; not sweet like milk chocolate and not bitter at all! My only complaint would be that I wish the bar was scored so that the pieces would be a little bit smaller. Right now the bar is somewhat scored into six squares, but those are pretty big squares, so you have to break them in half to let it sit comfortably in your mouth and let it dissolve.That's really the best way to eat dark chocolate: put a small piece in your mouth and let it dissolve slowly . NEWMAN'S OWN DARK CHOCOLATE starts melting almost immediately into a chocolate cream that coats your tongue and the roof of your mouth, so that you get that wonderful taste just enough to satisfy a sweet craving.I highly recommend it to those who love chocolate, but want to skip the milk chocolate and find that other dark chocolates are too bitter. NEWMAN'S OWN DARK CHOCOLATE will satisfy that craving without making you go overboard.

column9: Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate Bar
column10: I am a big fan of the Newman's Own products, and especially the Organics line -and a decent fan of dark chocolate as well :), but I would have liked this bar more if the cocoa content was higher than 54%.  I found the taste to be comparable to some other 65-70% cocoa bars (not too sweet-not too bitter).  The bar size is approximately 4.5"x2.75"x1/4" thick, and easily divided into 6 sections. Good tasting overall.

column9: Tastes Like Chocolate, Not Like "Health Food"
column10: The dark chocolate flavor of this NEWMAN'S OWN ORGANICS DARK CHOCOLATE BAR is mild, compared to dark chocolate bars manufactured by specialty candy makers (for example, See's Candies).  But the flavor is quite good, especially for a "commercial" candy bar designed for general sale in grocery stores.  Unlike many health food store "organic" products, this "organic" chocolate bar leaves no unpleasant aftertaste.The bar (approximately 2.5" x 4.5") breaks into six large snack pieces. One bar (one serving) weighs 64 grams, has 330 calories (200 fat calories), and 22 grams total fat.  There are 5 grams sodium, 37 grams carbohydrates, 4 grams fiber, 28 grams sugar, and 3 grams protein.The label warns that the bar is manufactured on equipment that may have been used to process other products containing peanuts, other nuts, milk powder, wheat, soy and egg (although the bar itself contains none of these).  The bar is 54% cocoa (Rainforest Alliance Certified).Because I'm a big fan of "Newman's Own" products, I was eager to try this offering from the "Newman's Own Organics" line.  It did not disappoint.

column9: Disappointing on a number of levels
column10: My wife and I independently taste-tested this product. My wife is a regular consumer of dark chocolates while I tend to prefer milk chocolate, and/or chocolates with fillings. After trying it out, we both decided that we would not purchase this product in the future, though for different reasons. Here are our independent reviews:My wife: I am confused by the labeling of this product. It is called a 'dark chocolate' but has a 54% cacao content. Most dark chocolates that I buy have upwards of 65% - 75% cacao. When I first opened the package, I noticed a smoky aroma. I eat a lot of dark chocolate, including raw chocolate, but I never noticed such a smoky aroma before and found it pleasant. My first bite was disappointing. It is a bit too sweet for me, and is certainly significantly sweeter than the dark chocolates that I buy. It is smooth, which I like. While I appreciate the fact that Newman's own is producing an organic, minimally processed, chocolate I will not purchase this again.Me: From my first bite I knew that this chocolate was not for me. It had a distinctly waxy feel that I usually associate with inferior chocolates - this was an immediate turnoff. There was absolutely nothing distinctive about this chocolate - no fruity notes, no particular bitterness, nothing that sticks out. While this chocolate is better than a lot of what constitutes the mass market, I cannot recommend it.

I started this review process on a bad note: I was under the impression that I was destined to review "Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate Bar, 2.25-Ounce Bars (Pack of 12)." In fact, I received a pack of one. You can see the problem right off, particularly since I had recruited three other tasters to help me evaluate the product and then had to tell them they each only got a quarter of one bar.The bar is smaller than most other organic chocolate bars on the market (at least in my market), so I'm hopeful it will be a bit cheaper. (Many run from $3.50 to $4.50 apiece.) It has a somewhat lower percentage of dark chocolate than my favorite brand, as well.Like all of Newman's products, this is a perfectly fine product, and the charitable donation included with each purchase is always a winner.

column9: A great organic chocolate option - dark chocolate for people who don't like dark chocolate?
column10: THE QUICK TAKE:  Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate is a great chocolate option.  At 54% cocoa solids, it's just over the edge of dark chocolate.  So it makes a nice change for those wanting dark chocolate that isn't so dark.  And, it's sustainably and responsibly produced - making it as guilt-free as chocolate gets.  The price at Amazon varies and can be high, so you'll need to look at the current price and your other options to decide what works for you.TASTE AND TEXTURE:  To have a little fun, we did a taste comparison to some other chocolate we had in the house.  The Newman's Own Dark Chocolate compared well to other premium and organic chocolate we had. It's decidedly darker, less sweet and firmer than a milk chocolate, with a very nice texture both to chew and on the tongue.  And it has some really nice subtleties to the flavor.  But it's not nearly as strong as what aficionados would consider a "dark" chocolate.  So it's a good option that might just hit the (bitter)sweet spot you are looking for in chocolate.PRICE:  These bars are relatively expensive.  That's to be expected for a premium chocolate that's organically produced.  We're lucky enough to have a lot of options for locally for organic chocolate.  Newman's Own is an excellent product, but you will want to compare it to the other options available to you.PRODUCTION: There are two important aspects that make this chocolate as guilt-free as chocolate gets:First, organic production.  Newman's Own has one of the largest organic chocolate sourcing operations in the world, which is highly commendable.  So you and your family get great tasting chocolate without consuming other things you don't want to eat; and, you also get the knowledge that the producers are working to minimize the impact of your consumption on the places where the chocolate is grown.Second, responsible sourcing.  Far too few people know that most of the world's cocoa production is tainted by child labor and often forced labor - or, in plain terms, slavery.  If that's news to you, Google chocolate slavery for some eye-opening information.  Or have a look at some of the Amazon listings, such as Bitter Chocolate: The Dark Side of the World's Most Seductive Sweet.All of that is a lot to fit into a chocolate bar - but Newman's Own has done that, and more, and offers you a lot of excellent options in chocolate.  If this one doesn't suit you, there are several more on Amazon.

This chocolate is only 54% cocoa solids. Given that many of the better bittersweet or dark chocolates have 65-80% cocoa solids, that gives a lot of room for other ingredients, which in this case is sugar.  Although being organic, you get the high falutin sounding "evaporated cane juice", which is, of course, sugar.  Although the chocolate flavor is good, this bar is on the sweet side.  So if you are looking for something stronger or with a sharper edge, you should avoid this one.  However, if you have a sweet tooth, and want a good fruity chocolate flavor, this chocolate would be to your liking.

I'll keep it short: I like chocolate, especially good chocolate.  While this bar may be organic, with great texture (not waxy), the flavor seems to have been left out.  It's labeled "dark chocolate", which it is, but it's also very, very bland.  I ate most of the bar, just broken into pieces, trying to decide if it's something I'd use for baking.  I wouldn't.  I'm not a big fan of Ghiradelli, but I'd use their chocolate in baking before I'd use this.  If you're looking for a mild dark chocolate bar with great texture, this is for you (not as bitter as Hershey's Dark).  But if you're looking for a good, strong-flavored, dark chocolate - keep looking.

This bar is billed as 100% premium organic chocolate, actually, dark chocolate 54%.  My passion is dark chocolate.  It's 2.25 ounces totaling 330 calories, and they are absolutely delicious.  Bottom line, however, this bar tastes more like the richest, most creamy, milk chocolate bar you will ever eat versus true dark chocolate.  There is no slight to outright bitter edge characteristic of dark chocolate, yet the bar is not overly sweet.  By rights this bar should lose a star regarding the dark chocolate issue, but it's just too good overall.

This was pretty bad for dark chocolate or any other chocolate for that matter. The consistency was sort of like chalk, extremely crumbly and way too sweet/milky to have that great punch that dark chocolate has. I would like to say that the overwhelming sweetness was due to the lower cacao percentage that I like, this comes in at 54% where I prefer around 72% and up. But it is just way too sweet. I ended up breaking it up and making a small batch of muffins and not a soul noticed.

Overall, this is a nice chocolate bar with the benefit of being organic and rainforest certified.  The chocolate dissolves quite smoothly and evenly - we compared it against a number of other dark chocolate bars we purchased from Trader Joe's and other places, and it dissolved more smoothly than any others.  It isn't as bitter as many other dark chocolates, and hence, it may appeal to some people who don't really like other dark chocolates.  The appearance of the bar was great - it had clean, dark surface, and there were no white blemishes or other marks that sometimes mar chocolate bars.  The bar breaks with a nice "snap," and the aroma is quite nice.  Overall, both my wife and I found the taste to be excellent.On the downside, the bar has fewer cocoa solids than the other cocoa bars we tasted - 54% cocoa solids.  Most of the others we sampled had 70%-80% cocoa solids - a couple were even higher.  This _could_ be important to some health-concious consumers, because many studies examining the health benefits of dark chocolate have defined "dark" to mean 65+% cocoa content.  That should be taken with a grain of salt, because some recent studies also have found merit to chocolates with lower cocoa content, but the majority of studies to date have focused on dark chocolate.Another possible concern related to this chocolate could be the price.  A twelve pack of bars comes in at $25,85 (possibly plus shipping); Trader Joe's has a number of bars that, although sometimes not as tasty, are certainly not as expensive.In sum, for taste, aroma, and presentation, this is a really good chocolate bar.  The negatives are price and a lower cocoa solid content.

I don't usually like anything other than milk chocolate. But I do know that the benefits of dark chocolate are good, so I thought I would give this a whirl and I'm really glad I did.Much to my surprise I found this to be an altogether pleasant experience. This chocolate has a rich, creamy texture when allowed to melt slowly in your mouth. It also was wonderful just to down-right gobble, but I don't recommend it. (Gobbling that is) This product is just too good to gobble willy-nilly!It had no unpleasant bitter aftertaste that I've come to expect with certain darker chocolates. I sometimes like my chocolate to be a bit on the softer side, so I also tried the candy a tiny bit melted and found that it was even better. There is no waxy taste to this bar and it melts well, it is rich, creamy and full bodied. And I had to really restrain myself from gobbling this up in one sitting.I'm not one who likes European chocolates; I have a love of Hershey's and always will, so this product is right up my alley, and if I find myslef looking for something a little different...this will be it from now on.

This is nothing like the Newman's Own chocolate I've had in the past! I don't know if they are changing all their chocolate products, after trying this I hope they are!Usually I'm not too crazy about dark chocolate & find that even the lesser percentage dark chocolates are still too strong for my liking.  This simply is not the case with this Signature Series bar!  It melts nicely in the mouth & isn't too bitter or too sweet.  The flavor is very well balanced & very satisfying.  After the first sniff & taste I thought I'd devour the entire bar; it was so good!  However, I enjoyed about half the bar & was amazed that my chocolate craving was soothed!Imagine that - chocolate left for another day!Last, I'd like to mention the ingredients because to me they are very important.  I would like to think that if you are considering Organic Chocolate, you care about the ingredients too.A big problem I have with the majority of Organic chocolate is the soy lecithin.  Ever notice that it's hardly ever organic?  Soy is a huge crop & I believe something like 80% of of it is GMO!  Big time Bad!  Thankfully this bar is ALL Organic:Organic evaporated cane juice, organic chocolate liquor, organic cocoa butter, organic soy lecithin, organic vanilla.  The Cocoa butter is Rainforest Alliance Certified.(A few Organic chocolate bars on the market contain NO soy lecithin!  Even better!)

column9: Good Product, but it is merely organic, not gold.  Are we worthy?
column10: Newman's Own Organic Dark Chocolate Bar is good if you like semi-dark and mildly sweet chocolate that is a little harder with a slightly higher melting point than that of European chocolate of similar expectations. I liked the chocolate very much but I did not find it to have any superior qualities to Hershey's chocolate. The product is sold in a pack of 12 bars but my sample from the "Vine" program consisted of only one bar. I am not sure if my opinions would have changed given a larger sample, but my confidence and enjoyment of the review would have been significantly greater by having a larger sample from which to provide a better comparison of quality and quantity with competitive products. I am certain that the people running the Vine Program at Amazon fully understand the importance of having a reasonable sample in quantity and that such quantity that reached the reviewers may have been less than what was originally planned to be a sample of sufficient size. In other words, "Who ate the chocolate?" is a question that should be investigated by an independent party and that those with chocolate remnants on their fingers and lips should no longer be allowed to participate in management of the Vine Program.In summary, Newman's chocolate is good, but in my opinion nothing special that could justify the cost. But, the Newman products are supposed to be of higher quality with the excess margin being used to support worthwhile causes and I have no problem with a product such as chocolate where an inflated price provides excess margins to do some good that might otherwise may not have not been done.

column9: Another home run for Newman's Own
column10: I really enjoyed the (alas, all too small) sample of Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate provided to me by the Amazon Vine Program.  Make no mistake, it's a serious, rich, and elegant chocolate, perfect for those times when you want something better than the goodies on the rack next to the register at the supermarket.  But more playful adjectives, like "yummy" and "scrumptious" also came to mind while enjoying it.I don't eat many sweets and desserts these days, so when I do I make sure it's the good stuff.  And this complex, nuanced (yes, yes-- and yummy, too) dark chocolate certainly qualifies.
