With this new addition to its product line, Newman's Own continues its reputation for delicious, healthful, and environmentally responsible food products.

Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate bar is a tasty, fairly creamy chocolate bar.  One bite will satisfy your mid-afternoon chocolate craving and hopefully help you make it through the rest of the day.  Of course, any bite of chocolate around that time would probably do the same, so why choose this one?Its socially responsible.  The cocoa beans are grown on rainforest certified farms. From their website, "The Rainforest Alliance Certified(tm) seal guarantees that the cocoa in our Signature Series was grown on farms that meet comprehensive standards for sustainable farming, protecting soil, waterways and wildlife habitat as well as the rights and welfare of workers, their families and communities."Its organic.  Newman's Own is certified by Oregon Tilth.  If organic foods are important to you, Oregon Tilth certification is your guarantee that high standards have been met.Its simple.  Organic evaporated cane juice, organic chocolate liquor, organic cocoa butter, organic soy lecithin, and organic vanilla.Its yummy.  54% cocoa means its intensely chocolatey.  There is a hint of sweetness, but it retains the bitterness dark chocolate fans like.  Not too creamy, not too dry.Compared to a few other dark chocolate bars, Newman's Own stands up pretty well.  I did a little taste test with the following: Organic Dark Chocolate with Almonds - 3.5 oz Bar was the best, but it had an unfair advantage with the addition of almond bits. It was a little creamier than Newman's Own. Organic Dark Chocolate - Regular, 59% cocoa, 12 Units / 2 oz was almost indistinguishable from Newman's Own. Same texture and very similar flavor, perhaps slightly more intense. Trader Joe's Fair Trade Swiss Dark chocolate had 71% cocoa so it had a drier texture.  I even tried one by Ikea, which was inexpensive and chocolatey, but actually my least favorite.  It did not appear to be fair trade or organic.Overall, a good solid organic fair trade dark chocolate bar.  Dark chocolate fans will like it, milk chocolate fans might be converted.

column9: Very good and smooth, not as smooth as the best.
column10: Excellent chocolate. Very good taste and good mouth-feel (smooth and good melting point). It isn't the best chocolate we've had, but certainly in the top 10%. This was dark chocolate and tasted accordingly, so you have to be into that.

I love dark chocolate , when I first started I wasn't picky, I always grab the Hershey special darks when they are on sale and stock up, have  tried a few expensive ones and found many to be to bitter for me. But I really like the newsman's own, I love it's organic, I try to eat organic when possible. This chocolate is not as sweet as the Hershey brand and I like it more, it tastes thick and delicious without to much sugar and yet not bitter, a winner in taste now if they could just work on the price.

column9: Rich, decadent, silky, and 'feel-good' in content, origin, and manufacture.
column10: "Silky" is the word I kept coming back to as I tried this chocolate.  It's smooth, rich, and ... well, "silky" is just the right word.  Everything about this chocolate is decadent, but also feel-good insofar as it bears the 'organic' and 'rainforest certified.'  What does this mean in a practical sense to consumers?  From the Newman's Own site: "The USDA Organic Seal assures that at least 95% of the ingredients are organically certified." and "The Rainforest Alliance Certified(tm) seal guarantees that the cocoa in our Signature Series was grown on farms that meet comprehensive standards for sustainable farming, protecting soil, waterways and wildlife habitat as well as the rights and welfare of workers, their families and communities."Seals and certifications don't mean much in the mouth, however, and that's where this chocolate excels.  It's rich without being excessively bitter.  Smooth without lacking depth and substance.  It's easy to eat (and that comes from someone who struggles with chocolate, at times), and it's a very accessible dark chocolate.  A very adult alternative to the over-sweet milk chocolate one might find in a more pedestrian alternative.I don't know how better to celebrate this product than to just list the ingredients: Organic Dark Chocolate (organic evaporated cane juice, organic chocolate liquor, organic cocoa butter, organic soy lecithin, and organic vanilla).  This stuff is as feel-good as it is taste-good.  Can't wait to try the other varieties.

column9: Yum, could have used a bigger sample though
column10: Vine sent me this to review - I LOVE chocolate, especially dark chocolate so I was quite excited.  Now if you order this product you will get a pack of 12 - I got 1 so my only option was to simply consume it.  And I enjoyed that oh so much.  It had a harder texture than your hershey's special dark, but had a very similar flavor and sweetness.  It was very very tasty.  I would have liked additional bars to try things like baking with to fill you in on things like does it melt well in chocolate chip cookies or to make chocolate covered strawberries... I will have to guess on this as I didn't have enough to do that experiment.  Due to the harder nature of the chocolate I believe it would work well in cookies but not so much on strawberries.I like the idea of my chocolate being organic - I like where Newman's is going with their product line... I hope that they keep the word "Organic" meaning something other than just another sales pitch tactic.Anyway - if I'm in the market for Dark chocolate - I would pick this up without a second thought.

column9: Not for those who like a smooth taste
column10: First of all, I love dark chocolates tried a wide variety of them.For Dark chocolates to taste good - they typically need to made from the finest ingredients and manufacturing processes - else they are going to taste bitter and rough - leaving an unpleasant taste.I had high expectations about Newman's own Organics, but utterly disappointment.As you slip a square of the chocolate into your mouth - it feels smooth and good - ....  When you are done with 3/4 of them, thats when you realize that there is something kind of an aftertaste/not so smooth taste about this.  I do not get this feeling when I try a Lindt or dark chocolate truffles from Central Market/Whole foods.Overall - they are made of pure organic ingredients - but for whatever reasons - the cocao/manufacturing ... - the taste did not go over well with me.
Good taste, but more sweet than I expected. Also, the texture could have been a little creamier.  But overall, it hit the chocolate spot.

column9: My sweet tooth isn't quite that sweet
column10: Wish I could have rated this higher.  I respect the Newmans and their philanthropy and appreciate the fact the product is premium organic ingredients.  I was looking forward to trying this 54% chocolate bar.I eat a little dark chocolate daily and found this was too sweet for my taste. (To be fair I have had the same problem occasionally with a couple of other brands I've tried over the years.)I usually buy Green & Black's 85% Dark Chocolate or Endangered Species 72% Dark Chocolate. Someone who is used to milk chocolate might like the Newman bar better than I did.As for comparing nutrition facts, all three bars use different portion sizes...so I didn't find it worth the effort.  Newman's 2.25 oz. bar is considered a single serving.  Green & Black's 3.5 oz bar is considered 2.5 servings, and Endangered Species 3 oz. bar is two servings.

Like all chocolate, this organic chocolate bar from Newman's Organics is very high in fat content.  It is a guilty pleasure.  It is simply some of the best organic chocolate that I've ever tasted!  I'm not the biggest fan of chocolate, but this is absolutely fantastic.  Best of all, it is made with organic ingredients.  No pesticides or artificial ingredients are used in making this product, so while it may not be healthy the ingredients are still better for the body.  Highly recommended.

I love chocolate and was really disappointed by the weak, almost non-existent chocolate taste of this bar.  Since there are no milk solids in dark chocolate, it is supposed to provide a deeper pronounced chocolate flavor.  However, this bar doesn't provide much in the way of chocolate flavor. There's no immense pleasure derived as the chocolate melts in your mouth which makes the bar not worthy of its caloric content.Break off a piece and hold it against the roof of your mouth and run your tongue over the bottom of it.  It feels sort of waxy, and it takes a bit of work before the chocolate flavor starts to come through, and when it does, it's nothing to really appreciate.  Flat tasting is a good way to describe this bar.I wouldn't buy this, and I don't recommend it.
The dark chocolate is not too sweet and not to bitter.  Delicious and organic.  What's more to say?

I didn't get to each much of the bar I received, as my husband purloined most of it, sadly. But what I DID have was absolutely silky-smooth and delicious, without the harshness that some dark chocolates can have. (I'm actually more of a milk chocolate girl, but I LOVED this.)My husband particularly liked it because he's very concerned about the ethics of cocoa plantations, so he felt like this was something he didn't have to feel guilty about eating. We'll definitely repurchase!

column9: I'm interested in the health properties of dark chocolate
column10: After reading a number of articles on its possible health benefits, I became interested in finding a good organic dark chocolate to "take" instead of red wine (to provide polyphenols in my diet) and aspirin (for its blood-thinning properties). I appreciate the opportunity to review this 2.25-ounce 54% cocoa chocolate bar.One of these bars is divided into six squares. Two squares equals .75 ounces. According to a study published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition, half an ounce of dark chocolate was enough to boost antioxidant activity and reduce oxidation of LDL cholesterol. (I could not find the percentage of cocoa in the chocolate used in this study.) If these bars were divided into 8 instead 6, two sections would be closer to a half ounce serving, and this would bring the cost of a daily "medicinal" (:-Q) dose of chocolate down some. If these bars are priced comparably to the other organic chocolate bars in the Newman line, however, the .75-ounce serving of two squares will still cost less than a can of soda from a vending machine. If I'm not drinking red wine and taking aspirin, that's not going to break my bank account.Milk chocolate fans may not like the taste, but I like this chocolate a lot. It has just the right amount of bite in the finish without being bitter, and it melts slowly enough but not too slowly on the tongue. I'd like to also try the 70% cocoa bar to see which I would prefer. I'm after the health benefits more than the "sweets" aspect.Being Rainforest Alliance Certified, I can eat this chocolate without guilt, knowing no child slavery or destructive growing practices are involved with its manufacture.

column9: Expected more from Newman's Own than this!
column10: First off, I like dark chocolate, I really, really like dark chocolate and I also like the Newman's Own products/foundation. However, I did not like this one. In fact, I spit it out. I don't think I've ever done that before..It is much closer in taste to a milk chocolate, but even at that lacked any real flavor. There was no depth to this at all, none. It was bland, yet too sweet for dark chocolate, lacking any real chocolate experience at all.If you appreciate dark chocolate, I recommend you check out Chocolove products, or Endangered Species brand. I've never been disappointed in either of those brands.

I've tried my fair share of different milk & dark chocolate brands. In the end, there are two simple categories for me in the affordable chocolate range:(1) Cheap, too much factory taste/feeling, not really worth the calories - Hershey's, etc.(2) Memorable, usually more expensive but when you bite into it you agree it's worth it - Green & Black's, Lindt, etc.I'll eat from either category depending on my budget and level of chocolate neediness. My impression of this Newman's Dark Chocolate is it is priced as if it belonged to category #2, but tastes more like it belongs in category #1 (I suppose high end of category #1). Still, I would skip the Newman's and buy something from category #1 to get something that tastes like category #1 and save some money.

column9: Okay, but even Cadbury is better.
column10: Sorry, I know it's organic, I know it's Newman's Own, I know it comes in a wonderful expensive package and all... but I'd rather actually taste Cadbury dark chocolate, or the dark chocolate made at my local candy store.Nice packaging, nice "real" cocoa flavor... but it doesn't make me want to eat more.I'm not the chocolate connoisseur some are, but this didn't really get my motor goin'.

I generally like items from other Newman's product lines as they always seem to have a great, borderline decadent flavor.  So I was genuinely surprised at how disappointing this bar was.  I love dark chocolate and when given a choice will always choose it over milk chocolate, but I found this bar to be bitter, almost burnt tasting, and the texture was exceptionally gritty.  To be fair, dark chocolate isn't going to have the silky texture of milk chocolate, but that doesn't mean it should crumble in your mouth.  All in all a very disappointing experience.

column9: Better than no chocolate, but not as good as one might hope
column10: Unlike the other members of my family, I'm not a chocoholic.  I'm a take it or leave it consumer and in general, I go for the good stuff.  This sample bar was my introduction to the Newman's Own Organic Chocolate line, and in order to get a variety of opinions, I shared this taste with several co-workers.My immediate impression was that the bar had the nice, crisp snap of well-tempered chocolate, and also that it had a lovely texture, melting quickly and smoothly in my mouth.  The "dark" chocolate bar has a slightly smoky flavor, but only 54% cocoa, which is less than what many may be looking for in a dark bar.  (Newman's Own also has a super dark bar with 70% cocoa.)  All of us felt that this bar was sweeter than we would have ideally preferred, more akin to bittersweet chocolate than a true dark chocolate.  It was suggested, for that reason, that it might be a nice high-quality bar for baking--though as noted previously, it is not a standard baking bar size.The other thing that all of us noticed was a very subtle orange note to the flavor, to the point that we searched the ingredients for an explanation.  The ingredients of this organic bar are very simple and straightforward.  In fact, there are only five, none of which would explain this undertone.  And it wasn't a problem, overt, or unpleasant; it was simply commented upon.  Further perusing the Newman's Own offerings, I see they produce a dark chocolate orange bar, and I have to suppose there is some minor cross "contamination" of the flavors.  Mystery solved.A quick survey among my cohort revealed that there was only one of us who really cared that the product was organic.  Yeah, the rest of us are Philistines.  Based on the high price point and the low percentage of cocoa, even though we'd enjoyed the treat, none of us was inclined to purchase the product again.  Your mileage may vary.

I love dark chocolate so Newman's own naturallly appealed.  It has a clean taste, but lacks the depth and complexity tthat you expect from a premium dark chocolate.  I do like that it is not overly sweet -- know it would be great to bake with.

Chocolate is by definition a Good Thing, dark chocolate doubly so.  And organic, Rainforest Alliance Certified dark chocolate?  Very nice.  It has a good flavor.  At 54% cocoa, it's not nearly as dark as some of the other bars on the market, and so is rather smooth on the tongue (I will dispute that it's waxy as one reviewer reported.)  It's true that it's not silky the way really fine chocolate is, but it doesn't purport to be.  It's the sort of chocolate you could find at your local supermarket.  High end there, but nowhere near the price or quality of a bar of Vosges organic dark chocolate.  Nor should it be compared to something like Vosges or even Godiva.  It's a good, affordable organic chocolate bar that has some good credentials in the environmental department.The bar is smallish, but I also debate the assertion that it's too small to share with a friend.  There are six good-size squares in this package, which are more than enough for two assuming that no one is being a glutton.  (That said, I admit I ate the whole bar myself today, but if there'd been anyone else here I'd have shared.)  Yeah, more is better when it comes to chocolate, but it's by no means necessary.Enjoy this chocolate bar for what it is.

I am not a chocolate connoisseur but I occasionally buy a bar of Hershey's Special Dark to enjoy and this tasted very much the same.  For me, that's a good thing.  For a gourmet chocolate aficionado, maybe not so much.

column9: i love your movies, paul, but not your dark chocolate
column10: first off, the size of the box this bar of chocolate arrived in was ridiculous. it could have fit at least 50 bars or more. c'mon, amazon, you can do better.now to the real review, which i should qualify by saying i prefer my chocolate 70% dark. this is only 54%, which i failed to notice when i requested this vine product. that said, this tasted too much like milk chocolate. milk chocolate in a bland, mass-produced, thoughtless way. this is just boring chocolate. it's ersatz chocolate. basically, once you've gone dark, you can't go back. and this, for me, was back.

column9: Don't Be Afraid Of The Dark
column10: When the bar of NEWMAN'S OWN ORGANICS DARK CHOCOLATE arrived on our doorstep, it was a race to see who would devour it first. My daughters, my husband, our cat, and even our guests all lined up for a square of this delicious treat. But we had only one bar! So bit by bit, I doled out hunks of My Precious until the line had dissipated and only one hunk remained. So yes, I was the good hostess and the last to pop God's Gift to Chocoholics into my mouth.I should pause to say that I am not normally a huge fan of dark chocolate, but I will eat it in a pinch. This was not a pinch, but there I was, savoring a mouthful of truly delicious cocoa. What I generally dislike about dark chocolate is the bitter aftertaste, but with NEWMAN'S OWN ORGANICS DARK CHOCOLATE, they have managed to create a pleasantly sweet flavor that both mitigated the bitterness and complimented it. I was surprised. I really liked it. Even afterwards, after I had allowed it to melt in my mouth and slide down my throat, the pleasant flavor lingered. I found myself scanning the others for remnants of their squares, but alas, they too had eaten every crumb.The packaging announces that NEWMAN'S OWN ORGANICS DARK CHOCOLATE is organic and 54% cocoa. Oh and it's "premium." Ordinarily, I'd consider that to be advertising puffery, but I'm here to tell you that this chocolate *is* premium. And delicious.Nutritional facts (which are absurd to list on a bar of chocolate!):  Serving Size: 1 bar (although a stack of bars is highly recommended.)  Calories: 330 (but they're tiny chocolate calories, so they don't really count.)  Total Fat: 22g (you know, that may sound like a lot, but it's METRIC. See? Practically calorie-free.)  Trans Fats: ZERO. (And trans fats are a kind of fat, so in a way, it's fat free!)Whew! All that science has made me hungry! Why did I only get one bar?  I definitely need more NEWMAN'S OWN ORGANICS DARK CHOCOLATE!!!!!

column9: Smooth organic chocolate with a semi-sweet taste
column10: I love dark chocolate, so I was excited to try this Newman's Own Dark Chocolate bar.  First, I was impressed that the bar, which is smaller than other specialty chocolate bars but still a generous six squares, is just a single serving size.  At 330 calories, 22 grams of fat, and 28 grams of sugar, it is still an indulgent treat, but if you choose to share the bar (as I did), you can satisfy your sweet tooth without feeling too guilty about it.I definitely enjoyed the taste of this bar as well; I found the chocolate to be rich and smooth.  At 54% cocoa, it is definitely not as dark as many other dark chocolate offerings out there--in fact, I found the taste to be a bit sweeter, more reminiscent of semi-sweet chocolate than true dark chocolate.  Although this was fine by me, some dark chocolate lovers may be disappointed.  So, unless you need your dark chocolate to be of the extra-dark variety, I would definitely recommend this product.

column9: Don't Go Out Of Your Way For This
column10: This was a surprisingly bland bar of chocolate.  It was not sweet, lacked the deep flavor of dark chocolate and had an almost waxy consistancy.  There was nothing special about it.  It was also too small to share with a friend.

If you are used to waxy mass-produced chocolate, Newman's Own Organics might take a little getting used to. This is the real deal, 100% premium organic dark chocolate. The texture is a bit different from the run of the mill waxy chocolate that most people are accustomed to, but the flavor is very good and the rich dark chocolate melts in your mouth! Ingredients are: "Organic Dark Chocolate (Organic Evaporated Cane Juice, Organic Cocoa Butter*, Organic Whole Milk Powder, Organic Chocolate Liquor, Organic Soy Lecithin, Organic Vanilla). *Rainforest Alliance Certified(Tm) Cocoa." I enjoyed this dark chocolate but not everyone may appreciate the texture. Give it a try and see what you think!

I found this bar rather lacking in chocolate flavor.  At 54%, it might be possible that I am used to a higher cocoa content (60%+).  While some other reviewers have mentioned the mouthfeel as "grainy", I found it more chalky.  It melted well in the mouth without any grainy feel, but when chewed, became a rather gummy mass of chocolate.  It wasn't awful by any stretch of the imagination, but it was a little strange.  If you don't like dark chocolate, you would probably enjoy this bar--it seemed more like semi-sweet chocolate to me.  If you like dark chocolate, however, prepare for disappointment.

column9: Good... but would go with a larger size
column10: This chocolate bar had a really nice taste to it. Wasn't bitter like some dark chocolate I've had before. Nice taste, I thought it was smooth, my only complaint would be the size as it seemed smaller than normal size bars and I would like more! Which really isn't much of a complaint.

I thought this was a pretty good bar with just the right amount of chocolate and sweetness, but I felt the bar could have been a little smoother, as I had a slight bit of a grainy texture from it.  Not enough to turn me off, and YES, I did finish the bar, but if it were just a tad smoother I would have given it a full five star rating.Overall, not a bad bar, but I prefer some of the others on the market that have less of a grainy texture.

When reviewing one of the Newman's Own products, it's always tempting to let one's opinion of the goals of the organization temper one's review of the product. I try to avoid that as I figure that the reader can decide those issues and is reading this to see what a reviewer thinks of this particular product.I like this product, but got it to try as part of the Vine review program and I don't know that I'd actually buy it because there's no price info available yet, so you can't compare it.On the upside, I like the taste. Until the last few years, a 54% chocolate was considered 'dark' and I like dark chocolate of about this percentage (up to about 60%). I think it's robustly chocolate, without the bitterness of the extremely high chocolate you see these days. This bar seems a nice balance of chocolate and sweet.One the downside, I find it just a bit on the grainy side. It's subtle, and didn't stop my enjoying it, but I noticed it compared to other high-end brands of chocolate bars. It's just not as smooth.Would I buy this compared to others? It's hard to tell without being able to price compare, but given that I don't consume enough chocolate for the price to really matter, probably not.

Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate Bar, 2.25 oz.I'm a firm believer in the Newman's Own corporate objectives and enjoy many of their fine products. I appreciate the facts that this chocolate, according to them, "is formulated with some of the finest Certified Organic chocolate we've ever tasted, made from cocoa beans grown on Rainforest Alliance Certified(tm) farms." While the New Organics Dark Chocolate is very good, it has a slightly grainy texture which, for me, spoils the mouth-feel a little. A small point, I suppose, as it is excellent chocolate with a 54% cocoa content. I certainly recommend it for its rich chocolate aroma and taste.

column9: Yummy smooth dark chocolate that is also good for your health!
column10: Fuzzy Wuzzy's Summary:**** Recommended with warm fuzzies.I just received my single 2.25-ounce bar this morning and it was a good thing that I already ate breakfast as I nibbled (instead of chomped) on this with my morning coffee.  I have always liked all of Newman's line of foods, because they taste good and are made of high-quality ingredients, and because his foundation donates hundreds of millions of dollars to charities throughout the world.  (And I love his movies! :-)  Paul Newman walked the philanthropic walk in helping to make the world a better place.This 54% cocoa dark chocolate bar has an all-organic ingredient list that is free of artificial sweetener and extraneous additives and fillers, which is all too common in chocolates, candies, and foods these days.Note that, at the time of this review's writing, the "Ingredients" and "Nutrition Facts" listed on Amazon's site for this dark chocolate bar are actually copied from another "Newman's" chocolate bar, Newman's Own Organics Milk Chocolate Bar, 2.25-Ounce Bars (Pack of 12) , and so this information that is currently listed on Amazon's site for this dark chocolate does NOT apply to this product; it refers to Newman's Milk Chocolate.  Hopefully, Amazon will correct the listings in these two sections for this product.Amazon's "Ingredients" listing: Organic Milk Chocolate (Organic Evaporated Cane Juice, Organic Cocoa Butter, Organic Whole Milk Powder, Organic Chocolate Liquor, Organic Soy Lecithin [An Emulsifier], Organic Vanilla), Natural Coffee Flavor.Actual Wrapper's "Ingredients" listing: Organic Dark Chocolate (Organic evaporated cane juice, organic chocolate liquor, organic cocoa butter, organic soy lecithin [an emulsifier], organic vanilla).Wrapper's "Nutrition Facts" listing (with Amazon's corresponding "Nutrition Facts" listing, that actually apply to Newman's Milk Chocolate bar, in parentheses):Calories:  330 (340)Calories from Fat: 200 (190)Total Fat:  22g 34%DV (23g 35%DV)Saturated Fat:  13g 65%DV (12g 60%DV)Monounsaturated and Trans Fat: 0g (0g)Cholesterol:  0g 0%DV (5mg 2%DV)Sodium:  5mg (30mg)Total Carbohydrate: 37g 12%DV (37g 12%DV)Fiber:  4g 16%DV (1g 4%DV)Sugars:  28g (33g)Protein:  3g (3g)Vitamin A:  0% (2%)Vitamin C:  0% (2%)Calcium:  2% (20%)Iron:  10% (15%)So Newman's Own Organics Milk Chocolate Bar has more vitamins, calcium, and iron due to its use of milk, while the dark chocolate has more fiber and less sodium.  Many people do not consider chocolate to be a high-fiber food, but dark chocolate (not milk chocolate) ranks among the top-20 for high-fiber foods.  Dark chocolate is loaded with flavonoids that act as antioxidants, keeping your heart healthy and reducing oxidative stress.  Flavonoids also balance hormones in your body, and they activate endothelial nitric oxide synthase levels in your body (biochemical gibberish that translates to "helps regulate your blood pressure" :-)  Studies have also shown that dark chocolate, perhaps due to its increased fiber content, makes you feel more "filled up", giving you more of a feeling of satiety compared with eating milk chocolate.At the time of this review's writing, Amazon had not yet priced this chocolate. But even if it was priced higher than other dark chocolates offered by the larger candy factories, I would still buy this because I believe in Newman's cause and charities.  I also love dark chocolate that is combined with nuts and/or berries, such as the Chocolove dark chocolates, and I hope that the "Newman's" dark chocolates line also eventually includes those.I love dark chocolates with cocoa content that goes to 77% and beyond, but these are not as sweet and have a subtle bitterness compared to dark chocolates with lower cocoa content.  The 54% cocoa content of this Newman's bar strikes a happy balance of sweetness that will appeal to those who are more accustomed to milk chocolate's sweetness.  This chocolate is not as sweet as some of the other 54-55% cocoa dark chocolates out there because many dark chocolates add higher amounts of extra sugar to their bars.  The flavor of this chocolate is nice, but with a slightly fibrous texture; just don't expect it to be as sweet as some of the more-sweetened dark chocolates on the market or else you may think that this tastes a bit bland compared to them.  Likewise, some people think that heavily-salted food tastes better than lightly-salted food.  The "evaporated cane juice" used as a sweetener in this chocolate is a healthier alternative than the processed sugar that is included in many chocolate bars (including the Belgium-made Chocolove bars that I love).  Both refined sugar and cane juice come from sugar cane, but cane juice is less processed and retains more nutrients.  So enjoy this smooth rich dark chocolate "health food" guilt-free, but in moderation.  I certainly will enjoy eating the rest of this chocolate bar while watching my DVD of Cool Hand Luke (Deluxe Edition)

I got this chocolate for free on the Amazon Vine program, and for free chocolate, it was pretty good. But if I'd paid full price for it, I wouldn't have been happy. It was overly sweet and the texture was a bit grainy. I'll stick with Green & Black's when I want organic dark chocolate.

column9: I expected a lot more from the Newman's Own brand.
column10: I have tried a couple of products from the Newman's Own line and, while I didn't necessarily think they were better than their competitors' products of the same type, they definitely held their own.  I sadly did not find this to be true with the Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate Bar.When it comes to reviewing edible products, I find it helpful to compare and contrast with a similar product from another brand.  Because I love Dove Dark Chocolate (though I try many different kinds of dark chocolate), I used the Dove Silky Smooth Dark Chocolate Bar as comparison (though I prefer the Dove Promise individual bites, it was easier to compare bar to bar).The Dove Dark Bar is 33 grams and the serving size is the entire bar.  The Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate Bar is 64 grams, nearly double the size of the Dove Bar, and still 1 serving is considered the entire bar.  Now, I am as much of a chocolate lover as the next person (probably more, in fact), but there is no way I need nor want to eat to consume 64g of chocolate in one sitting (especially sub-par chocolate).In most nutritional areas, especially fat and sat fat, the 33g Dove bar and the 64g Newman bar are almost equal if you consider that one is double the size of the other.  Newman's only clear win over the Dove bar is on cholesterol, having 0mg even though it is double the size of the Dove (which has 5mg cholesterol).  For those watching sugar, the smaller Dove bar has 17g while Big Daddy Newman has 37g.With the health business out of the way, let's get down to brass tacks--taste and texture:Texture.  I am accustomed to the smooth, creamy texture of Dove dark chocolate--I find its mouth feel luxurious.  My initial thought on biting into and chewing the Newman was waxiness--quite nasty at first but, once I got it chewed, it had a nicer mouth feel.  It is not creamy like Dove, but it loses the waxiness once chewed.Taste.  The only thing particularly pleasant to me about the Newman bar was the finish...the very last taste as you're swallowing it.  That has a deep rich dark chocolate taste and, despite the 37g of sugar in it, is not overly sweet, which is nice.  As for Dove, the entire process of biting into it, chewing it and swallowing it is enjoyable, so there is no contest.In summary, if you have your heart set on contributing to Newman's Own because of the good work they do, or you must have an organic chocolate bar, I suppose this will do.  But it is not, in my opinion, any competition for ANY other brand of good dark chocolate I have tried.

Wow! As with virtually all Newman's Own products, this is the best. I've tried just about every brand, including a number of organic chocolates, and this beats them all. Naturally, such and assessment is subjective, but I'd suggest that in a blind tasting (i.e., without the suggestion of a brand name), Newman's Own chocolate would always be at or near the top of every list. Do yourself a favor and get some--it's good for you, too! You won't regret it.

column9: Could be a bit more flavorful...and less expensive!
column10: Like most health-conscious people, I appreciate the idea of organic food, and Paul Newman's Own is one of the most respected brands on the market. That's why I wanted to try this chocolate bar.I'm not a big "chocoholic," but I do enjoy a taste of decadence on occasion, and this was one of those occasions.To make a long story short, I tried it and liked it, but it didn't taste nearly as good as Lady Godiva or even my old cheapie "standby" Hershey bar.Sure, Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate Bar, 2.25-Ounce Bars (Pack of 12) is  flavorful, but to my taste buds it seemed a little harsh... Oh, how do I describe it? I guess what I'm trying to say is that the texture wasn't creamy enough.In all fairness, I must confess that I often enjoy chocolate while drinking green tea; you know, a generous chunk of chocolate romancing my palate, followed by a sip of hot tea to mellow and enhance the taste sensation. Well, that proved to be what did it for me. Yes, I loooved it when savored in that mannerI shared it with a friend who is more of a connoisseur than I am, and he loved it...straight from the stylish, golden wrapper.Another drawback for me is the expensive price. This 2.25-oz. size isn't available yet, but I found Newman's other same-size bars on Amazon for $26.88 per box of twelve. That works out to about $2.50 per candy bar (plus postage). Ouch!Needless to say, I would rather spend my hard-earned money another way. Sorry, Paul. I dearly love you and enjoyed many hours of quality movie time with you, but I'll stick to buying your salad dressings. Meanwhile, I'll get my chocolate kicks from my old friend, Mr. Hershey. Even Lady Godiva is out of my budget.With the small amount of chocolate I digest, it's not going to kill me. :-)Reviewed by Betty Dravis, February 24, 2011Author of "Dream Reachers" (with Chase Von) and other books

column9: If you don't like dark chocolate, you will love this bar
column10: I love dark chocolate, but I found this bar too bland for my tastes.  It has one note of flavor and not very interesting.  Funny thing is, when I handed the remaining squares out, everyone who usually only liked milk chocolate loved this bar.  So if you like milk chocolate, but would like the benefits of dark chocolate, this may be the perfect compromise.  However, if you like the bracing complexity of dark chocolate, you may find yourself giving this chocolate away.I usually really like Newman products and like supporting their business, this is the first item I will not be repurchasing.NOTE: The bars are as tall as an iPhone and a little wider than one -- just a heads up if you think this is a large bar, it is not.  You will want to note the weight of the bars if using for a recipe.

column9: I didn't think I would fall in love with it, but I did.
column10: So, I'm a guy.  I like chocolate, sure, but I am not into dark chocolates.  I even used to date a chick who was into wine and tried to get me into the whole dark-chocolate-with-wine thing, which I never got.  I got into wine, sure, but dark chocolate was never anything I really cared for.So when I got this, it was with much hesitation.  I don't even LIKE dark chocolate, why on earth would I want this?-I cannot explain what this bar did to me.  I took a small bite and was hooked!  It's just wonderful.  How do I describe this - it was ultra smooth without any of that bitterness which I detest in dark chocolate - not even a hint!  It was pure excellence.  I did see other people here mentioned that it seemed "grainy" and I can say I felt none of that.  I thought it was gorgeous.  I literally could not stop eating it.  And that never happens - I am very much into food but it's rare that anything grabs me like that.  I did put it down halfway through - and I was transformed from a guy who hates dark chocolate to a guy who now knows what real dark chocolate is.  I put it down because I was on my way out the door - but you can bet that as soon as I got home, I ate the rest.  It was just so fine.  I would absolutely get this again, and I look forward to a time when I can buy this for someone else, so they too, can experience the luxury of this fine dark chocolate.
This chocolate was a bit less sweet, more bitter, and harder than I usually enjoy.  For the price and the small bar size, I would prefer Dove dark chocolate.

Its hard to describe taste especially since I'm not a connoisseur of chocolate but of the brands that I have tasted, this one sits in the middle for me, not of the highest taste pleasure sensation but a great deal better then others I've tried.  I love the Newman's Own Brand and every product I've tried from this brand has been excellent.  I think this one might be best used for baking rather than eating straight out of the package.

column9: Pretty good chocolate, very small serving
column10: This Newman's Own Organic Dark Chocolate is a good bar.  It has a rich dark chocolate taste, a good texture, and a nice mouth feel.  My only complaint is that it is a very small bar, so it's not outstanding enough to justify the cost.  There are better dark chocolates out there.

column9: Good quality but not my favorite
column10: I'm a big fan of chocolate and of Newman's Own products, so I was very excited to try their chocolate. This bar is 54% cocoa, which I consider somewhere between milk and dark chocolate (but more towards dark), and this is right in my personal sweet spot. This is high quality chocolate with a complex flavor, but it was not as smooth as I usually like. My favorite chocolate, the Scharffen Berger 41% extra rich milk, is obviously much more of a milk chocolate bar, but I have had 60% cocoa chocolate that was smoother than this 54% chocolate. I do recommend that you try this chocolate because I think it would appeal to many chocolate lovers.

There is a immediate taste corresponding to the chocolate content. Although my preference is for chocolates with a bit higher content--60% or more--it is close enough. It is rich with some sharpness, but does _not_ have a "burnt" taste that several other brands have. It melts nicely in the mouth to a smooth texture, without becoming overly buttery. And it has a good aftertaste.

column9: Not All Great Dark Chocolate Bars Hail From Europe
column10: I've always been a fan of Newman's Own products and this dark chocolate bar did not dissapoint. I like my dark chocolate bars to have a bit more cocoa (70% at least) but for those who shy away from the bitter flavor, this bar offers a good balance with a hint of sweetness the higher cocoa bars lack. You won't mistake this for a Hershey bar by any means. The product is certified organic and uses Rainforest Alliance Certified cocoa so you can feel good about what you are eating. A great bar at a very reasonable price that holds its own against the more expensive offerings from Europe.

We enjoyed the full and rich chocolate bar. We ordered the product on Amazon Vine and received the order promptly...as we do with all of our Amazon shipments. We enjoy organic foods and this certainly is a welcome item on our list of organics.

NOTE: Guest review from my chocolate-loving friend LW:I almost missed the 2.25 oz. bar at first, wedged as it was, in its brown and black wrapper, alongside the inflated-to-full-size plastic air cushion in its Amazon book box. But once I'd extricated it and opened it, it was substantial. All 22 grams of fat (13 saturated) of it. Sorry, I looked. But not to worry -- that's for the whole bar. With a modicum of discipline, you can easily spread that shame across six nights by breaking off one generous carefully scored square each night (bigger squares than the one on your hotel pillow). That's all you need at a go anyway -- the taste is very rich with a subtle liqueur-like finish -- just what you'd hope its 54% cocoa content would deliver.[Bar provided as part of Vine review program might have been smaller than bars available here for sale.]
I split this bar with my wife.  She (as it seems most women are) is the expert on chocolate.  Nonetheless, both she and I really like the taste of the bar and will be ordering more.

Satisfying.I love that this chocolate is organic. From the first to last ingredient.I love that the first ingredient is dark chocolate.I love the taste. Intense, rich with a hint of sweet.The one thing I didn't love was the meltability on the tongue factor. I don't know if the bar is so thick that this slows the process. I broke it into a smaller chunk and it sat on my tongue awhile. Not that that's awful..it's chocolate for goodness sake... I guess I could say it's slow to melt. Chewing didn't hurry the process.Allergies or Vegan? The standard disclaimer appears. "This product manufactured on equipment that may process products containing peanuts, other nuts, milk powder, wheat, soy and egg." However the only listed ingredient on that list is the organic soy lecithin.Overall tasty. And pretty much what it promises.
I usually am a fan of Newman's products, but this chocolate left me cold.  Just didn't taste creamy or chocolatly. Sort of tasted chalky.  Ick

I am not a fan of dark chocolate. I was a little hesitant at first but it was silky, smooth, and the right amount of sweetness. My boyfriend on the other hand is a chocolate freek. He agreed and ate the majority of this bar. I love Newman's Own products. I honestly would purchase this just because he donates so much of this proceeds to charity.

column9: Organic but does not taste like dark chocolate
column10: I am a chocolate lover and it was the first time I tried an organic dark chocolate. It tastes alright but it does not seem to have the same smoothness and bitter taste which come with the typical dark chocolate.  It is also a little pricey for over $2 dollars a pack. I would prefer the Ghirardelli Dark Chocolate over this.

I will say upfront that there are very few dark chocolates that I like. I'm a fan of Ghiradelli, and Lindt, but not most of the others I've tried. The Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate was tasty, but the texture wasn't as smooth as some of the others I've tried. I'd say it's better than most (say, Hershey's Dark) but still needs tweaking to be as good as Lindt.

This is one great dark chocolate bar!  It is organic and when comparing this to a nestle special dark I can definitely tell the difference.  The Hershey's tastes more sugary and artificial.  While this chocolate bar isn't cheap it does taste great!

column4: Shawn Kovacich "Author and Creator of numerou...
column9: Give Me A Hershey Bar Any Day of the Week!
column10: I admit that I am not a big dark chocolate fan. I first noticed that the chocolate does not have that sharp bitter taste that most dark chocolate has. Then again, it doesn't really have any taste. By the time I was done eating the chocolate bar, I kind of felt like I ate some wax. From there it did not agree with my system. It might be organic and dark chocolate, but give me a Hershey's bar any day.Shawn KovacichAuthor of the Achieving Kicking Excellence book and DVD series.

I didn't find anything remarkable about this candy. It's not more tasty, it isn't smoother, and it generally just isn't any better than other dark chocolates. I passed bites around to my office mates and everyone came back with the same reaction. Newman's brand is known for being a cut above everyone else; this isn't anything to write home about.I do appreciate the environmental aspect, though.

Not smooth enough or distinctive enough in flavor to compare to many high-end chocolates and with more chalkiness/waxiness than I expected, this simply was not a big enough step up from mass-market semi-sweet chocolate to be that interesting to me as a purchase in the future, even after getting this (single-bar, not pack of 12) free taste test from Amazon's Vine Reviewer program.  Not terrible, just underwhelming.

column9: Very Tasty, But Kind Of Small.....
column10: I've never eaten Organic Chocolate before, and I often find Dark Chocolate to be somewhat bitter, so I was very interested to taste Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate. I found the taste to be surprisingly sweet and smooth, and I enjoyed it very much. The actual amount you get per bar seems very small for the price, however........But it is a fair-trade product, so that knowledge does go a long way towards justifying the price.

column4: Bonnie Jo Davis "Loves to read and review books."
column10: I must admit that I have never eaten an organic chocolate bar so I was excited to taste Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate Bar.  Unfortunately, I found the taste to be bland.  The texture is nice and I liked that it didn't melt in my hand while I was eating it but this bar has the distinction of being the first chocolate bar to enter my house and not get completely eaten.  Newman's Own is a fantastic organization that donates generously to charity so I feel guilty saying this but I would not purchase or eat this chocolate bar on my own.

column9: Somewhat chalky with a bit of an after taste.
column10: I love what Newman's is doing and I applaud their products.  I must confess that I am not a big lover of dark chocolate and prefer milk.  This particular bar tasted chalky, like maybe it had been available for a while (which, since it was free, may have been the case).  It also had an unpleasant after taste.  I am not sure if Newman's has  a milk chocolate bar, but if it does, I will get one to add the comparison to my review.

column9: Is there such a thing as bad chocolate?
column10: Some might argue that, just as there's no such thing as bad sex, there's no such thing as bad chocolate. (Even the worst of the latter I've ever consumed - in Leningrad, Russia in 1984 - was still edible. My history with the former we needn't discuss.)So, here we have NEWMAN'S OWN ORGANICS DARK CHOCOLATE (NOODC). Mind you, it doesn't contain such poncy embellishments such as almonds, macadamia nuts, cherries, pomegranate, mint chips, bacon shreds, rice krispies, orange peel, caramel filling, peanut butter, raisins, walnut pieces, toffee crunch, coconut, red pepper, coffee beans, cranberries, blueberries, white chocolate chunks, or the kitchen sink. It's just 100% chocolate, i.e. evaporated cane juice, chocolate liquor, cocoa butter, soy lecithin, and vanilla - all organic, of course. (It must be pointed out, however, that vanilla is used by chocolate makers to mask the flavor of imperfectly roasted cocoa beans. Hmm.)At 54% cocoa, NOODC isn't particularly elevated on that scale. Who in a chocolate company determines the what and why of an optimum concentration, I wonder? Probably the (cocoa) bean counters, I imagine.Because I have a taste disorder described more fully in my review of the book Remembering Smell: A Memoir of Losing--and Discovering--the Primal Sense, I can't judge the sweetness of this candy, but only the chocolate flavor and the "mouth feel." Both are pretty much average and acceptable. Is it better than one of my favorite brands, a Cadbury Royal Dark Chocolate Bar, 3.5 oz, 24 count bar? Uh ... no. But, it's infinitely better than that Commie chocolate eaten back in the nostalgic good old days of the Cold War! I mean, without any of the added embellishments mentioned above, a plain chocolate bar has to work overtime to stand out from the rest of that genre on the shelf.Actually, I was more interested in the subtleties of the label. Paul himself is pictured with Nell, his daughter by Joanne Woodward. Nell started the Organics Division of Newman's Own in 1993, and remained at its head when it chipped-off the old block in 2001. Dad still lent his support, though, before he died. I gather it's Nell`s leadership and participation that's inferred in the confectionary's subtitle, "The Second Generation."Again, according to the labeling, the cocoa has been certified by the "Rainforest Alliance." Perhaps I'm being cynical, but it makes me wonder how much Nell's company tips this outfit for the granting of its certification, however legitimate such a ritual blessing may be. Similarly, there's the notation "Certified Organic by Oregon Tilth" - whatever a "Tilth" is.Also, there's the usual CYA disclaimer: "Manufactured on equipment that may process products containing peanuts, other nuts, milk powder, wheat soy, and egg." The potential hazards for allergy sufferers aside, how might those possible contaminants affect the organic quality of NOODC if they themselves aren't organic? Inquiring minds want to know. (Perhaps the "USDA Organic" sticker carries implications here. I'll certainly sleep better at night knowing the guv'mint is involved.)And the fact that a 1 bar serving size contains only 5 mg of sodium means that my wife could chow down the whole thing - minus the single bite I was tossed - without fear of elevating her already borderline-high blood pressure. After all, dark chocolate is reportedly a health food.Would I buy NOODC on at the local chain supermarket without it being at a bargain, club price? Probably not. I've never been convinced that "organic" isn't mostly a marketing ploy to raise the sticker, and NOODC at full price doesn't give more satisfaction than a less expensive bar laden with assorted impurities, toxins, and carcinogens. And both go down equally well with a glass of cold, non-fat moo.

I don't know if I have any of Mr. Newman's products that I didn't like.  This is no exception.  At 54% cocoa the bar isn't overly dark.  Even it color it is fairly light. There isn't the hint of bitterness that usually comes from a dark chocolate bar.I found myself breaking the pieces into quarters.  A piece is about an inch square but smaller is even nicer to savor.  This is not chocolate to feed on but to eat, savor and enjoy.  The feel is wonderful because it quickly melts in your mouth and is just wonderful.The bar is small. It makes you want to savor and eat it slowly.Delicious, just delicious.

I have had a lot of chocolate in my life time, from all over the world. I've have the pralines in Belgium, the smooth satiny rich chocolate of Switzerland (which I consider the best) and spent some time in France trying their orange and chocolate combinations. I do love American chocolate products also! I prefer dark chocolate over milk chocolate, unless in Switzerland where the milk is the most creamiest (and unpasteurized) I have ever had the joy of trying.Newman's Own Organic chocolate bars rival that of my European favorites.  It has just the right amount of "dark chocolate" flavor (54% dark) without being too bitter.  It has a solid texture that quickly becomes creamy as it melts in your mouth. The sweetness is not overwhelming, and this definitely falls into the "dark chocolate" lover's category.I feared that "organic" chocolate would not taste good, since I am not into "organic" this and that.  I hated the "Carob" years when everyone tried to convince me that Carob tasted just as good as chocolate, though it wasn't even really close!  This chocolate is very very good.I don't eat chocolate for my health, of course (unless mental health counts) and this stuff is high on the calories (330 per bar, or 64 grams, or 2.25 ounces.) compared to another brand's special dark chocolate bar, which is 180 calories per 41 grams.The choco-holic in your life (and you know there is one) will find this to be a very delicious treat! The gold foil wrapper inside lets you know you are buying something special!Highly recommended if you like dark chocolate!

column9: Just What it Says - It's Dark
column10: This is so dark it smells and tastes like baking chocolate.  When it melts in your mouth it is smooth and creamy.Organic Dark Chocolate (Organic evaporated cane juice, organic chocolate liqour*, organic cocoa butter*, organic soy lecithin [an emulsifier], organic vanilla).*Rainforest Alliance Certified Cocoa.

The flavor of this chocolate reminds me of Hershey's Special Dark from several years ago (the classic formula), only considerably milder. And it's not just me; the first reaction of those who I shared it with was, where's the flavor? The most charitable adjective I can think of is 'inoffensive', but that's not a good thing. Not something I would ever seek out again. Forgettable.

column9: Delicious, not bitter. Also good for PMS!
column10: I'm more of a milk chocolate kind of person, so I didn't expect to like this, but it's actually very smooth and not bitter.Since dark chocolate is so good for you, and milk chocolate, well, isn't, I was hoping I'd find a dark chocolate bar that didn't have a nasty bitter aftertaste. This meets that criteria!The bars are small, but it's rich and satisfying, and all you really need, even for PMS. I can feel the grumpiness melt away, replaced by mild euphoria and a feeling of peace, contentment, and love for everyone. Chocolate is a miracle drug, and this particular one is high quality, good stuff.DH knows that there are certain times he will need to throw one of these in ahead of him and run past and wait for the chocolate to kick in. He considers these a good investment, and I like the taste, texture and health benefits.I feel much less guilty eating these than I would milk chocolate, or my beloved forbidden white chocolate.I'm very satisfied with this product.

column9: Very Good taste, but texture a bit brittle
column10: I love chocolate, and this bar from Newman's was very good tasting. Nice and rich. The only thing I didn't think was good was the fact that the chocolate doesn't seem to have that soft smooth texture.It is a good size bar (2.25 oz) and the calorie count is 330, 200 fat calories.I would continue to buy this chocolate.

column9: This product illustrates the deficiencies of the term "organic"
column10: I can't give more than a 3 star average for this item, when considering the flavor and taste of this "organic chocolate" bar.Like some other Newman's Own food products that I've tasted, it doesn't offer any special quality, other than that the ingredients are virtually all "organic".  Unfortunately, our local, state and Federal requirements for "organic" foods, are severely flawed, and this product potentially  illustrates this problem quite well.The ingredients in these chocolate bars may meet most standards for organic foodstuffs, but there is an important element missing in the case of chocolate, that most people don't understand.I have read several articles recently about the high lead content of much of the chocolate that we consume, and for a period of time this problem was presumed to be that the cocoa beans themselves were (are) contaminated with lead, due to the leaded gasoline  in the engines of the farming equipment used in those countries that grow cocoa beans.However, some articles mention that lab analyses show that raw cocoa beans themselves have a relatively low amount of lead in them, compared to the final, processed chocolate products (and compared to other similar food products).  Some observant writers have then suggested that the high lead concentrations in cocoa products, are probably due to lead in the air near and over the drying beds, where the beans themselves are dried.  The reason for this contamination would be similar to the original theories, since there is likely high lead content in the air around these drying beds, for the prior reasoning (the lead in the gasoline used on the cocoa bean farms is emitted by tractor and other vehicle exhaust,  and then these contaminants attach themselves to the drying cocoa beans).At any rate, if the price of Newman's Own organic dark chocolate is as high as I suspect it is,  I would recommend buying a cheaper brand of chocolate bar ("organic" or not), since there's no way to know whether Newman's Own chocolate has less (or more) lead in it, than other brands do.

column9: Standard decent health food chocolate bar
column10: If you go to a health food store, you'll always find bars like this near the checkout counter.  They are high end chocolate bars that use all organic ingredients and fair trade cocoa.  They all taste pretty good and sometimes they go on sale so you don't have to pay an arm and a leg for them.  Newman's Own tastes very similar to any number of high-end organic chocolate bars.  They have about 40 percent more calories than you'd get with a Hershey's, but they also taste better.  I wish the squares for breaking off pieces were smaller, because this is really nibbling chocolate, not something you'd eat a whole bar of in a single sitting.I wouldn't say these are special or extraordinary chocolate bars.  They're perfect decent, though, and if I had a hankering for chocolate and they were on special, I'd buy one at a checkout counter.

Received only (1) - 2.5 oz dark chocolate bar,and we were expecting (12 bars) as stated in advertisement, so that was a disappointment to start with.  My husband and I shared the 2.5 oz bar, and we both felt that the quality was just average.  It was good, not too bitter, but not the best dark chocolate I've taste either. Based on the price, we would probably not purchase these in the future, as there are cheaper choices that are of the same quality, in my opinion.

I have a major sweet tooth, and my favorite dessert is chocolate. I can't get enough of the stuff. This made Newman's Own Organic chocolate a natural choice for me. I wasn't sure what to expect since I haven't had a lot of organic chocolate, but I really liked this bar. It was thicker and harder than I'm used to (that's what she said), and I generally prefer my chocolate soft and creamy. However, the thickness means you get a lot in every bite. I wouldn't call this chocolate creamy, exactly, but it has a smooth texture. I liked the way it melted in my mouth. One thing I noticed is that tiny flakes remained as the chocolate melted; this gave it a pleasant texture. The bar was also full of flavor, almost too rich to finish in one sitting. It was sweet, too, but not too sweet (it's 54% cacao, in case that's not in the description). I really prefer the sweeter milk chocolate, but not everyone does, and this was good dark chocolate.As for nutrition, it could have been better. There are 22g of fat and 330 calories. I worry more about saturated fat, and there were 13g of that here. There were 28g sugar, about average for candy, and 37g carbs. However, I think the slightly high numbers here are due to the fact that the bar is bigger than most. It looks smaller than a Hershey's bar when you get it, but like I said, it's thick. I don't think it's meant to be eaten in one sitting. It's divided into six pieces, so it's easy to eat a little at a time (or is it?). It's 2.25oz/64g. I don't know if that's a lot, but other consumers might. All the ingredients are organic, of course, and cane sugar is better for you than processed sugar, anyway. Besides, we all know that chocolate is full of anti-oxidants, and dark chocolate doesn't have so much sugar.This chocolate is certified organic by the USDA and Oregon tilth. It also uses Rainforest Alliance certified cacao, which should please the environmentally conscious. The wrapper is all paper, easily recyclable.I found the packaging attractive, too. The background is brown with pinstripes, and the logos are in black and white and bordered in gold. It has a classy look. The information about the product is easy to find; it says dark chocolate in big letters on the front, along with the cacao percentage. The ingredients are clearly listed, as are the nutrition facts (though I wish the important stuff had been in a table for easier reference). Also, the organic labels are prominently displayed (except for the Oregon Tilth one, which is easy to miss). If you want to find out more about the company's organic program is listed. The address is also printed and easy to find in case you want to contact the company. Finally, there's a picture of the founders on the back (which seems like an attempt to make the company seem homey), and it kind of looked like American Gothic. I found this amusing. The overall presentation is a good one, and it's attractive enough to make a nice gift, I think.So all in all, I thought this was a great chocolate bar. It's rich and smooth, and you get a lot for your money. It's certified organic, and it's environmentally sound, too. Great for health and environment conscious chocoholics!

In the last year or so I've really developed a taste for dark chocolate. I've liked dark chocolate for years but I started eating a bit more recently. I've tried several different brands from the store. All were at least good with some being a little better than others.So. While not scientific my personal taste experience says this dark chocolate bar taste terrible.If you are looking for that silky smooth deep rich dark chocolate flavor that sort of infuses your whole body starting with the tongue and culminating in a very pleasing feeling in your nogging look elsewhere. My God.On the other hand, if you are really into organics and go out of your way to eat all things organic then perhaps this is your chocolate bar. 54% is not a very dark bar and I think it shows in the taste of this bar. The taste could also be due to the organic nature of the bar. That being the case, if you prefer that organic experience, that taste that organics typically have I don't think you'll be disappointed.For everyone else, the flavor is off with strange undertones. Not inedible just not very tasty.The bars are fairly small at 2.25 ounces. That isn't really a knock since moderation in all things is a good habit.
This is a delicious chocolate bar.  But for the additional cost, I was expecting something extra special.  It tastes no better than a standard Hersey bar and has a very slightly rubbery texture.

With all the organic, single-origin, Fair Trade, 80% + dark chocolates available even in discount stores, I am not quite sure why Newman's Own brand wanted to get in the chocolate business. Anyway, this is a very light-weight entry into the fray, and at only 54% pure chocolate (in the Vine sample I received, anyway), a quite weak entry at that. It tasted okay, but definitely too sweet and lacking the earthy bitter-sweet taste of the more cacao bean-heavy chocolates available. Not much different than a decent Hershey dark chocolate bar, and likely much more expensive.

I was excited to try this chocolate as I'm such a fan of Newman's Own products in general.  It was good, but I found it a little disappointing.  It has a rich chocolate taste, but the texture is a bit too dry for just eating (which is what I intended to do with it).  It might work well for baking, but I haven't tried that yet...probably would work to chop up in pieces for cookies.

I really don't know what else to say except that it's moderate - not too bitter, not too sweet. The texture is not rich or exceptional in any way. It seems to be just a conglomeration of the ingredients listed on the package, so I would choose (or not) to get it based on whether you like that list.

I am but a simple man!  Complexities of taste and aroma are probably lost on me.  If I tell you, in a fake French accent, about the complexity of the flavor, it's probably because I'm trying to get your phone number.I did like this, though.This was a bit sweeter and creamier than most dark chocolate I've had, which can edge towards the bitter (aw we-we).Consequently, I liked it a lot.I decided to make Smores out of it.This turned out to be A Good Idea.  Probably offending lots of chocolate aficionados, who are even now fainting while someone waves a fan at them; I'm just sayin', next camping trip?  Box of these.  Far superior to Hershey's.As for "organic", I confess I appreciate things made with sugar.  I don't really buy into the horror stories of high fructose corn syrup, I just think sugar tastes better.  Kinda like those horribly overpriced sodas made with sugar.  THEY ARE SO GOOD.  But I digress.This is a great chocolate bar.  It has that dark chocolate flavor, yet it's creamier and more on the sweet side than most dark chocolates. I thought they really found the sweet spot.So to speak.Now about that phone number...
I really enjoyed this.  It tasted like a cross between milk chocolate and dark chocolate.  It was really creamy and rich.  I am somewhat of a chocolate snob, and this is some good stuff.

I am not a big fan of dark chocolates (Milk Chocolates for the win!), but these tasted surprisingly milky. For the price Amazon is selling them though, I would definitely suggest you to stick to your convenient stores' Hershey bars.

Chocolate is one of the few luxuries accessible to anyone. Researchers say that it even boosts endorphins in the brain, those feel good chemicals that decrease pain and heighten mood. But most of us love it for the sheer sensual taste and texture. Lesser quality brands can give the impression of eating brown bees wax, and while preferences and tastes vary, quality chocolate can make your eyes roll back in your head and for a few seconds your whole existence becomes only taste buds and ecstasy. So where does Newman's Own stand on the chocolate experience scale? Again, that's subjective. But my opinion as a chocolate lover is that it's one of the best I've ever tasted. The first thing you notice is that it immediately begins to melt in your mouth.  In fact, I tested the theory with one square of the bar, and it did completely melt without making a single bite in a minute or so. The flavor is very rich, creamy and flavorful without being the least bit bitter. It's made responsibly using organic materials and I like buying Newman Products knowing that they give all profits to charity and in the 26 years of their existence have donated over $300 million to worthy causes. How does it compare in regard to value? At around $2 per ounce it's about half the price of Amedei - No 9, the chocolate bar judged as the best in the world by the Academy of Chocolate. Be aware that it is a chocolate bar and not in a decorative box for giving as a gift. But for a small slice of heaven in the privacy of your mouth it's a great choice.

Newman's Own is my favorite brand and I try all of their products.  However, this one is a failure.  The bar is bland and I guess 54% cocoa is not enough.  I am sure as chocolate bars go, this is nutritious, but frankly, it is hard to find a nutritious chocolate bar.  If you want nutrition it would be best to go and  get an apple.  When I want chocolate, nutrition is not even on my mind.  Decadence is.  This bar is not decadent enough.  Keep looking.
Newman's Own organic chocolate is pretty good. It may have a little waxy taste than other dark chocolates, but it has a nice consistency.

As a true connoisseur of chocolate, I was interested in this new dark chocolate bar from Newman's. In truth I've always thought the Newman chocolate bars to be overly sweet and not particularly rich tasting. I thought from the hype that this new line of products would be different but I sad to report that is simply not the case here. In fact these new gourmet bars taste much the same as the standard line of Newman's own chocolates. There is still the problem of being overly sweet and considering how dark these are supposed to be, they don't have that deep rich dark chocolate flavor and texture that I am always looking for.n summary I just want to be clear and say that if you are looking for that killer concentrated rich dark chocolate flavor I'm sorry to report that you won't find it here.

The newmans own organic chocolate was very good.  Although it is dark chocolate, it had a rather milk chocolate smoothness and flavor to it.  If you are a fan of Dark Chocolates on the bitter end of the spectrum then you would not care for this chocolate necessarily.Overall, I felt that the quality was very good, it was pleasant to eat.  It had, perhaps, a slight aftertaste that reminded me of oranges.Good stuff, if you like mild dark chocolate, you wont be disappointed.

I am a big fan of Newman's Own Dark Chocolates. I've tried all the "percentages" of dark chocolate, and this is another good one. I like the texture of the chocolate: solid, but still creamy--and NOT crumbly (which I hate). The chocolate is mild, yet very flavorful and without any bitterness. Another solid chocolate bar from Newman's Own!

column4: Glenda Boozer "Live, live, live! Life is a ba...
column9: It's dark enough, it's sweet enough, and it's organic
column10: Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate Bar has a good mouth feel, a rich flavor, and just enough sweetness to eat on its own or to use as part of a snack. It's perfect for pain au chocolat, where a lesser chocolate would not be sufficient for such simple treatment.The taste is chocolate, pure and simple: very pure, and very simple. Try it alongside your current favorite; it should hold its own.

Good dark chocolate. Don't know if it's any better or worse than equivalent chocolate bars or non-organic chocolate.I guess I can say it didn't leave the kind of burnt or unpleasant aftertaste that I've noticed some other name brand chocolates occasionally do. So, there's that.For me, it was just generally some pleasant dark chocolate.

This bar reminds me of the semi-sweet chocolate used in baking.  The chocolate is neither instense on chocolate flavor nor very sweet, nor very smooth and creamy.My wife the dark chocolate aficionado in the house prefers a more instense dark chocolate - usually in the 70% + cocoa range.  Myself, the milk chocolate fan prefers a more smooth, sweet, and creamy chocolate.  In comparison, we bought a bar of Hershey's Extra Dark (60% cocoa) and it was both more intense and sweeter.  We both preferred it to the Newman's bar - surprising result for me considering I prefer milk to dark chocolate.I suppose those that prefer a semi-sweet, not overly creamy, medium intense chocolate this might be the ticket.  For us this  chocolate, though not bad per se, isn't what we are looking for when we want something to indulge in.

I love dark chocolate but sometimes the bitterness is a bit much. Newman's Own had a nice balance and flavor. I love the Newman's Own brand and their commitment to raising money for charity and using Organic ingredients. I'll happily be buying this product again. Highly recommended!

The smell is divine before you even unwrap this dark gem! It's rich tasting, without being too sweet. Dark chocolate often tastes bitter to me, but this was just the right balance. It's a decent-sized bar, but rich enough that it satisfies the chocolate monster for two people!

Great tasting dark chocolate bar by Newman's Own.  Paul Newman's company generally makes good food with natural ingredients and this tastes like another winner.  A nice, soft sweetness with no indication of bitterness, Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate Bar doesn't taste like the typical store bought, processed dark chocolate bar.  Fresh tasting with real chocolate/cocoa and is very satisfying for a bar its size.

column9: Dark chocolate for those who don't like dark chocolate
column10: I was intrigued by the tide of enthusiasm surrounding dark chocolate.  Apparently, chocolate can be healthy.  Well, it can also taste terrible too.  Those high cacao bars from far off lands my qualify as health food but they tasted like dirt.This new bar from Newman's Own is a different story.  It smooth but not overly creamy.  Sweet but not cloyingly so.  This is a really tasty dark chocolate bar.  Much better than Hershey's or the stuff you find at the exotic farmer's market.

column9: Smooth and pleasing, a very approachable dark chocolate
column10: I love dark chocolate and I eat it all the time.  For me, the darker the better; however I know that for some people the intense dark flavor I crave is not what they think of as chocolate.  For those people, I would recommend this chocolate with few reservations.My wife who is not as into dark chocolate as I am really enjoyed this, probably even more than I did.  I think for her it was a solid 5.

column9: all around good, but average chocolate bar
column10: I'd suspect most people who try this will like it, at least enough to finish a bar. I prefer dark chocolate, typically with a higher % rating then this has but hey chocolate is chocolate so I wasn't going to turn down trying it. It reminded me far more of a bittersweet (think chocolate chip) then of my typical dark chocolate bars. It wasn't bad by any means but it didn't stand out as amazing either. It's obviously worlds above your typical "candy isle" bar but I wouldn't pick it out when compared to other organic dark chocolate options at a specialty market. For those interested in moving into dark chocolate for health benefits this might be a good transition bar into those with a higher % if you're used to milk chocolates.

This is an acceptable chocolate bar, but probably not worth what they're charging for it.  It's pretty mild on the dark chocolate scale and has a slightly odd texture--definitely not melt in your mouth.  I wound up using most of my trial bar to make hot chocolate, and it served that purpose quite well--better than eating it out of hand.

I am a fan of dark chocolate, but I find some of the 70% and up bars to be bitter. The Newman's Own bar has 54% cocoa. It has a strong chocolate flavor without being bitter or harsh.One 2.25-ounce bar has 330 calories. The flavor is rich enough that when I need a chocolate fix all I need is one square (1/6 of the bar). That's just 55 calories so it makes a satisfying treat without busting my diet.The texture is smooth and somewhat creamy, although not as creamy as Dove dark chocolate (for whatever that is worth).I would definitely purchase Newman's Own chocolate bars again.

column9: Sweet and mildly dark organic chocolate
column10: Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate Bar is much more like milk chocolate than dark chocolate, rather sweet and somewhat milky for a dark chocolate, though it contains no milk. In fact, "organic evaporated cane juice", better known simply as sugar, is listed as the primary ingredient by weight.There are no unusual or notable flavors detectable other than chocolate and a hint of vanilla but the ingredients taste fresh. The tablet is not too thick nor is it too thin.Overall, a good but not notable and rather nondescript 54% cocoa bar for people who enjoy a higher cocoa content than milk chocolate but who don't like the taste of 70%+ dark chocolate.Each 2.25 oz. bar has 330 calories including 200 from fat.

column9: NEWMAN'S OWN ORGANICS DARK  CHOCOLATE BAR - Premium, best in class
column10: This "second generation" of Newman's Own is dedicated to producing products that are certified organic by Oregon Tilth.  (The "first generation" company gives all of its after-tax profits to charities.)  But in both cases, these two companies produce high-quality foods that are usually the best in class on the store shelves.  This NEWMAN'S OWN ORGANICS DARK CHOCOLATE BAR is no exception.  Pricey, yes.  Tasty, very.  The taste is, in fact, a smooth, semi-sweet dark cocoa flavor, with no acidity,  but with a slight roasted-coffee after finish.  This is not an afternoon pick-me-up candy bar.  This an after dinner treat to be shared with a cup of coffee.

Really, the title of my review *is* my review.I'm a fan of dark chocolate.  I like dark chocolate with a bit of bite to it: slight acidity and slightly bitter.  With that as the yardstick, Newman's Own 54% Dark is somewhere between dark and milk chocolate.But oddly enough, I really like this chocolate.  It has a REAL chocolate flavor without being too "earthy", but isn't as smooth and tame as milk chocolate.A small piece works really well with dried fruit or peanut butter as a small but satisfying snack.

column9: Fans of dark chocolate will want to sink their teeth into this.
column10: Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate Bar is a must for any lover of dark chocolate.  I really enjoyed the strong taste of the dark chocolate.  The not-as-sweet-as milk chocolate taste was to die for.  Not a lot of people really appreciate the taste of dark chocolate and those that do will definitely want to try this newest product from the Newman line.  Over the weekend I bought a carton of Newman's Virgin Lemonade (no HFCS) and it was delicious.  So if you feel that you're a connoisseur of chocolate then you'll want to buy a bar of Newman's Own Organic Dark Chocolate today.

column9: Pretty good taste, even better fringe benefits
column10: Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate Bar is a pretty good chocolate bar that has more going for it than just taste. First, it's USDA certified organic. I try to use organic products as much as possible, particularly on less costly products and those where organic matters. Second, the product is Rainforest Alliance Certified cacao. So the cacao is produced using sustainable growing techniques. These are the things about the product that I like best. And sometimes, it's these factors that make the difference between buying product A or B.As far as the taste ... well, it is not the best chocolate bar I have ever tried, nor is it the worst. First, the bar is about 7 mm thick ... moderately chunky as bars go. There is a classy-looking N emblem embossed in each piece. The nutritional panel says that one bar is a serving, but that one serving is going to provide about 330 calories ... actually 1/3 of a bar is a serving for me. The chocolate is not very melty. This is more common in higher cacao content chocolate bars; Newman's Own bar is about 54% cacao, so I was a little surprised. The bar was also a little sweeter than I expected. The chocolate was not unpleasant, but it just seemed to lack a "smack your face" slap of chocolate flavor that you expect in good dark chocolate.So, bottom line time: Newman's own is a decent but unremarkable chocolate bar. It's organic and Rainforest-friendly, and earns the product bonus points in my book.

I eat all types of chocolate, from the cheapest to the most expensive I get as gifts.  Dark chocolate is my favorite.  Recent medical studies are now showing dark chocolate can help prevent heart attacks and strokes, and help keep those individuals who have already had heart attacks from an earlier death.
