Thank you Amazon for stocking this one and for putting this on the subscription account to give me both savings and convenience.  Being a Brit in the states it is tough locating stores that stock some of home's conforts.For those who have never tried this brand of tea - you will love it for the rich blend of tea; somewhat richer and deeper than some of the American versions; but smooth with a dash of milk.I still need my cuppa in the morning and so pleeeeased it is avaiable. Try it as a great alternative to coffee ;-)
This is among the best everyday teas anywhere.  I just have to have a cup every day.

I was a bit suspect at buying this tea due to the very low price. But, the truth is that it's high quality tea at a bargain generic price. We have spent 3 or 4 times as much for bags of less quality. One big bonus is that not only are bags free flowing but the the tea also brews much quicker than other brands. A highly recommended product.

column9: Excellent black tea at a great price
column10: I recently started drinking PG Tips when I found it in the tea/coffee cabinet at the home of the family that I work for. They know I make tea for myself nearly everyday, so they are kind enough to keep tea in stock for me.  Being a young American, I had never heard of PG Tips until now, so I am sad that I have been in the dark for so long. The taste and "texture" of this tea is absolutely fabulous. I brew it for 2 minutes and it makes a perfect cup without any bitterness, but with a bold smooth flavor. I also add a splash of milk and a bit of sugar or honey... whatever is on hand. I am glad this is becoming widely available in the States and I can see this replacing my regular morning cup of Twinings. I can see why this is the "#1 tea in the UK."

Amazon bills this as black tea, which is technically correct but those familiar with Chinese and Indian teas also call this type "white tea." It is the tip end of the tea branches, the very best part. The rest of the plant is not considered choice at all. Basically they pick off the best parts and ship those to England while the USA's Lipton et. al. bag up the nasty leftovers and foist it off onto Americans, which is probably why we consume mostly coffee. If you enjoy a nice cup of tea, give P.G. Tips a try. Each teabag is large enough to brew a small potful, so it works out to be very economical.

PG Tips pyramid bags are the best for convenient brewing, two to a pot.  The 240-count package sits 9 inches tall, too tall for the cupboard where I keep the tea, so I kept one of the 160-count packages from the case I ordered last year and use it as a dispenser.  This tea is not for the fainthearted; it's dark and packs a caffeine punch.  Warm the pot, then brew for five minutes and (unless you're an iron gut) sweeten each cup with a cube of sugar and a dash of milk.  Gentler on the stomach than coffee, and if prepared as above, a healthy alternative.  I like both tea and well-brewed coffee, but find tea easier to manage.

column9: A good strong cup of tea, just the tea I want to drink
column10: This tea has excellent flavor and aroma, perfect for a good, strong cup of tea. PG Tips puts a third more tea in their tea bags than any other tea bags I have found sold in the U. S. The shape of the bag enables the leaves to move more freely in the bag and facilitates the brewing process.

column9: Avid tea drinker here: I will name names!
column10: I have always been a hot tea drinker, and over the past 5 years black tea has become my favorite drink. I purchased my first box of PG Tips at a local store after reading some reviews here. I thought to myself,  "I am sure it's good, but I'm an experience tea drinker and should not expect it to exceed some of the brands I already drink." Given the higher price of PG Tips, as expected, I found it FAR superior to regular Lipton, Walmart's Great Value Brand, and Lipton Black Pearl. It also surpasses similarly priced teas like Twinings, Stash and Tazo. What really surprised me is that it is solidly better (albeit not by huge margins) than more expensive teas like Numi and Mighty Leaf. So what makes it better? Firstly, it's smooth, aromatic and satisfying in a way the others are not. Secondly, as tea begins to cool a bit, the other brands' taste (especially the cheaper ones) begins to become a little off-putting. I find that with PG Tips even as it cools a little, I do not rush to finish the cup since it maintains its taste. I just purchased the 240 count two pack and recommend PG TIps to all tea drinkers.

column9: PG Tips is part of a happy marriage
column10: I first discovered PG Tips when I was researching what kind of tea one of my British characters would have imported to the Midwestern university where he reigned as President. (Dudley, from This Brilliant Darkness This Brilliant Darkness) That was when I discovered that PG Tips was the best-selling British tea. Upon editing, that detail got cut, but I never forgot.A few years later, I was delighted to find PG Tips on the shelf of my local grocery, in the imported foods section. I bought some to try, because I am a tea "whore." I always have upward of two dozen varieties of tea in the house at any given time--a situation that my then-coffee-addicted, then-boyfriend Tim found ridiculous.As soon as Tim tried PG Tips, all that changed.I now subscribe to recieve two extra-large boxes of PG Tips every few months. Tim takes a box to work and uses the rest here. He can't live without it. Also, we are extremely happily married, and he spoils me with whatever I want. Coincidence?  I think not.I have consequently become addicted to K Cups--but that's a different story.For the record, this & Earl Grey are the only teas Tim likes...so me and my 22 other varieties go the iced tea route & don't try to come between him & his Elixir of Life.Thank you, PG Tips, for making our lives complete.

P G Tips tea is a black tea. I am from India and am used to strong tea.. I used to have to use two Lipton bags at least to make a good cuppa, but PG Tips has solved that issue for me. We have a constant supply now and I suggest the name to all my friends.

This tea is stronger than I am used to, so it takes less teabags to make tea. I use about half the usual amount of teabags I used to use to make my Georgia Sweet Tea! I love the flavor of this tea, and it saves money using less.

Of all the teas I have tried, which is quite a lot at this point, PG tips by far makes the best cup of tea, even when compared to loose leaf.My English fiancée is a major fan of it and turned me onto it, and I have been hooked since. If you want an amazing tasting black tea with the convenience of bags, buy this. :)
Do the math; you save so much if you purchase PG Tips packaged like this! My husband has drank this since being a boy. He says it's "the proper tea".  I have to agree!

PG Tips is everything you need for a cup of no nonsense tea: strong (without bitterness), smooth and it stands up to milk and sugar to give you a satisfying tea experience.I know there are many out there (you know who you are) who look down their noses at this brand of tea. Go and be that way, there's more for me!The subscribe and save feature for PG Tips makes it very economical as well.

column9: Great tasting tea at a Great price
column10: PG Tips Black Tea was a very good choice to purchase. I have purchased numerous brands of black teas as I prefer the flavor of black tea over other teas for its stronger flavor. I've always drank Lipton tea iced and use six teabags from Lipton to make 1 gallon of tea. With PG Tips, I find three to four is enough or it's TOO strong but as always taste is based on personal preference. Upon reading all the five star reviews for PG Tips tea, I said OK...going to buy this tea and try it. Coming from England, I expected great flavor and quality and that's exactly what PG Tips was and is. My first impression is it tasted identical to Lipton, I can't really tell a difference between PG Tips or Lipton from the US because it taste exactly the same! The only difference I can tell is I use less teabags for making a gallon of tea with PG Tips than Lipton, why this is I am still trying to figure out. Possibly because they use only the two tips of the tea and a bud? Not sure...but PG Tips is my new tea from England! Enjoy.

I have had my eye on this brand of tea for quite a while, I just never wanted to spend the money on it.  Don't you just love the Friday Deals???  So, since the price was awesome, I decided to splurge.  I do not regret it!  I am now an official PG Tips tea fan!  The flavor is so great... smooth, but oh so flavorful!  I usually drink coffee, but occasionally get on a tea kick.  Let's just say that I could totally quit coffee and switch to PG Tips and not miss the coffee.  When I said that I usually drink coffee...let me go one step further and say that those people that know me, know to stay away from me first thing in the morning until I have at least 2 cups of coffee in my system.  I don't even know how to smile with out having my daily fix.  So, with that being said...that's how much I love this tea..that I could switch from coffee to tea and not miss it.
My friends and I have found that PG TIPS tea has a very enjoyable taste and I would definitely recommend it to anyone that loves that TRUE english tea taste.
If you like strong black tea that goes well with milk and sugar, then this is it.

column9: PG Tips Tea Bags are Pretty Grand
column10: Your cant find a better tasting tea and the price is just fantastic.  I i had storage for it i would order about 50 boxes so i would never run out.

I love this tea. I usually drink it as milk tea and it's delicious. My husband drinks 8 cups of this tea a day, which is good because he never drinks anything besides soda. Helps get him the 8 glasses of water he should be drinking. The tea is officially his favorite drink.

If you want a tea that is easy to get along with and has no tongue-torturing surprises, then PG Tips Black Tea is for you. No fancy oils or spices, just tea the way God and the British Empire intended it to be. I started drinking it decades ago and it's still my favorite. column9: The Best Tea for a great price!
column10: If you're familiar with PG Tips, you know that it is "England's No. 1 Tea". There is a reason for that: while PG Tips is not the cheapest tea in all of England, it is an excellent product. Here in the USA, I have not found a better tea which can be both purchased in bulk and excellent. If you're used to purchasing your tea at an American grocery store, PG Tips will most certainly cost less than a "weak" American tea. Where I live in Wisconsin, some truly awful teas sell for the equivalent of 10 cents a bag! PG Tips is high-quality and low-priced, and that is why it's my favorite tea.

PG Tips is the best tea! It's good hot or cold and the best thing I like about it is that you can brew your iced tea in the fridge. No more boiling water and waiting for it to be cool enough so as not to melt the ice!

While this may not be "premium" tea, it IS very good tea. It has a smooth, not harsh, yet bold flavor. It stands up well to milk or cream and makes a very good iced tea. After drinking this, Lipton's tea just seems so unbearably harsh and acrid. It brews up well, never seeming to become bitter. It works well as a general, all purpose, every day tea; also, blending well with mint or other flavors, like cinnamon, if that's what you like. PG is good black, too. It is a finely cut tea, BUT, so what? It steeps well and tastes great. The tea bags are pyramid shaped, which does seem to brew better, probably because more of the bag and tea is in the water and less is floating.  Also, there is more bag surface exposed to the water.  The material the bag is constructed of is different than the usual bag.  It is softer with a more open weave, so again, water flows through better.  It does not leave a slight taste of the bag, as some other brands do. I searched high and low, for years, and paid way too much for stale PG Tips before finding it on Amazon at a very good price, especially when purchased at subscribe and save prices. I do prefer the loose tea, but occasionally use tea bags, for traveling. There are other teas I enjoy, but this remains on my list of favorites, both for taste and price!
These PG tea bags make a good strong brew and a good cup of tea. If you cannot stand t-bags with string on then these will make you happy.

Excellent British breakfast tea, reasonably priced. Large string free bags, I like to steep them for 5 minutes, just the right amount of tannins to make a brisk flavorful mug, with whole milk and honey. Recommended.
Amazing blend tea.  Powerfully flavorful, for those looking for a 'pick-me-up.'  Not tart, but rather smooth and rich.

This is my favorite tea.  My local Wegmans doesn't appear to be carrying this anymore so I had to find another place to get it.  I need my "PG tea fix" after dinner!  I signed up for auto delivery which saves me money on shipping and I don't have to worry about having to re-order.  Thanks Amazon for carrying items like PG.

Of course it was PG Tips.  This tea is nonpareil.  I couldn't always find PG Tips.  After finding it at Amazon and having a subscription, I have a constant supply at a very good price.
Addicted to tea and this is the perfect solution. PG Tips is wonderful. I know it isn't the classiest tea available, but for the price it is a treasure. A good strong tea.

I have been enjoying PG tips for more than a decade. I first encountered it when I was in England. It is rich and smoothing. I need it everyday so if I had to take a star off that would be because of it addictive nature. ;-) Enjoy your cup of PG tips.

This is my favorite tea from Britain. It's a mix of black and green teas. The bag is the secret. Highly recommend this tea!
I liked the taste of the tea better then the normal brand I drink. Only takes eight tea bags to make a gallon of ice tea.

I've been a diehard Lipton Tea drinker all my life, until my English daughter-in-law introduced me to PG Tips Tea bags with their "Pyramid" style bag. I absolutely LOVE this black tea... hot, iced, anyway one uses tea. It has a robust flavor that eclipses all other brands!

column9: No wonder it's #1 in the UK!
column10: I've seen and purchased this tea in my local supermarket and was thrilled to see this fabulous deal on Amazon!  I really love this tea - I steep my teabags forever (i.e., leave them in the teapot) and this tea never gets bitter - I can understand why PG Tips is the best-selling tea in the UK!

column9: I cannot live without PG Tips!

I ordered a large supply which won't last long for us, so will be ordering more in the future. Thanks Amazon.com from a very grateful Scottish Lass...

My friend sent me a link to Amazon when she saw it on there, and I have a "subscription" now.It's perfect!The tea is great, and it comes to my door, when I want it. Thanks Amazon.

column9: Very good, and a lot of it
column10: If you haven't bought a 240 count package of tea before, let me tell you how much it is.  A lot.  That's how much.  This is the church's morning tea supply for the next few months.The pyramid teabag is very nice.  The bag material appears to be a standard tea bag like the kind used by Celestial Seasonings, but the four corners of the bag were formed into a pyramid instead of a square.  A tea bag, of course, will retain some air as it is steeped.  A square tea bag will float flat on the surface of the water.  A pyramid, on the other hand, floats as an upside down pyramid.  I don't know why the air doesn't collect in one of the corners, but it doesn't.  Bottom line: the rest of the bag, and thus the tea, is submerged, which makes for a (in my opinion) much better steep than a square bag.The tea itself is quite enjoyable, although I am not a connoisseur by any means.  I use one bag in the morning to make about a liter of tea, then down it with a big breakfast.  This tea is not as in-your-face earthy as the last black tea I tried (a Yorkshire blend), and I like it better.  It still has that earth and slightly bitter flavor, but it is a little sweeter than the Yorkshire blend I tried, probably because it is made from the tips of the plant, as the product name states, or perhaps it came from a different and better crop, or some other reason that I do not know.  I am not one to add anything to my tea for sweetening or any other alteration, so I prefer this tea.There's just a ton of it.  Two-hundred forty tea bags in an absurd quantity.

The PG Tips arrived in good order. I have found that I'm using more of the product and would like to receive the same order more frequently than quarterly. How do I change my order frequency? Excellent service otherwise thank you.

column9: PG Tips is the Best Tea!
column10: I love PG Tips and have been drinking it for over 15 years. No other tea even comes close to the delicious flavor. It's full-bodied without being bitter. Another great thing about the tea bags is there's no string stapled to the bag and no little paper bit to fall into the tea. These bags are pyramid shaped and the paper the bags are made of is very strong.I used to boil water in a kettle and pour it into the cup, but after burning up three kettles, I now microwave my tea. Just pop a bag in a mug of water and microwave on high for 2 minutes 15 seconds. The bag does not burst and it tastes just as good as pouring boiling water over the bag in a mug.Highly recommended!

PG Tips Black Tea, Pyramid Tea Bags, 240-Count Boxes (Pack of 2)We have been drinking PG Tips for over 30 years and can vouch for its authentic British tea flavor and outstanding consistency, year in, year out.  We take it with us wherever we go, and are delighted that Amazon sells the 240 count 2-pack for a very reasonable price.  We can share it with everyone!
PG Tips is always a good black tea, British Style that has plenty of body. Like we have had in India. The price was not bad especially with free shipping.

PG Tips is a little more expensive than domestic brands, but it's worth every penny.  I've tried every other brand and none compared.  It's strong enough to add milk and sugar and still taste the tea flavor.  The color is rich and inviting instead of weak and grey.

If you like a good strong, flavorful tea, this is for you. It's a blend of Assam, Ceylon, and Kenyan tea.  I was delighted with the Kenyan tea when I visited there and have continued my preference. column9: PG Tips, warms the heart of any ex-Brit
column10: There really isn't much I can say.  If you've had PG Tips you know the difference.  If you haven't you don't know what your missing.I'm from the UK originally and for years in the States I drank Lipton as it was the only brand I could readily find.  But along came Amazon and restored my access to my favorite tea.If you're used to drinking Lipton, PG TIps has a stronger flavor and if you brew it real strong it can get bitter on you.  However I used to use 2 Lipton bags to get the strength I like and just one PG Tips bag does the job nicely.If you're not sold, wait until it goes on sale or special and at least try one box.  Its particularly good if you brew it in a proper ceramic or china teapot rather than making it directly in a cup.Actually that is one thing to note.  These tea bags don't have little strings so make sure you've got something handy to fish them out with.From an Eco-friendly perspective I also like the fact that you only have the tea bags and the main box they come in.  Only the plastic shrink wrap is not recyclable.  If you drink a lot of tea using individually wrapped tea bags you are going to be generating a lot of unnecessary waste.  Particularly for those teas in plastic envelopes.  At least in Lipton's favor they do use paper wrappers you can recycle.

Being a Brit ex-pat living in the states, I can honestly say, if it wasn't for my PG Tips I would've gone back home years ago!!  lol  My Mum used to mail me my PG Tips, used to cost her a fortune.  When I found PG Tips on Amazon I couldn't miss the opportunity of buying them myself - they are actually cheaper than my Mum can get them!  They arrive on my doorstep every two months.PG Tips have got to be THE BEST t-bags you can find!  A lovely cuppa tea!
need to a/b pg tips and your fav teas, went thru the usual suspects and those brits know a good thing

Moving to the USA from the UK there are a few necessities that you need to have in your new home and tea is one of them.PG Tips are up there in the top few teas regardless of what any other tea maker tells you.Perfect brew in a cupPut one of the tea bags in a cup or mugPour boiling hot water into the cupStir the water and tea bag a little to help the brewingAdd a bit of your preferred milkDunk the tea bag until it meets your tastes (darker the colour the stronger the tea flavour). Some like it milky, some like it strong or without milk.Remove tea bag and stirAdd sugar or sweetners based on preference if you want.A great taste of "home" while abroad.

So, currently a little more than .60 a can.  Considering how difficult this product can be to find in certain geographical locations, this is to many people, quite a deal.  Much better than 3.61 a can anyway.2. The flavor has nothing at all to do with iced tea and I wouldn't describe Cel-Ray as "iced tea like" in the least.  It's much more comparable to ginger ale, or ginger beer.  It's less sweet than 7-UP or Sprite and more spicy or peppery with a mild, light vegetable undertone to it from the celery seed extract.3. While it's LESS sweet than most soft drinks on the market it's certainly sweet, as corn syrup is the second listed ingredient after carbonated water.  Granted they must use a lot less than regular soft drinks but it's plenty and Cel-Ray qualifies as "sweet."  It's also fairly strongly carbonated.  If pouring into a glass, you will see a light greenish-yellow color and a big, substantial head at the top of the glass.If you've never tried this before and it sounds iffy to you, you might want to taste test it first.  But for anyone with fond memories of pairing a Cel-Ray with a pastrami on rye, you already know how great they taste.  If you are a regular drinker of ginger beer or "hot" ginger ale then your tongue is ready for Cel-Ray.  This soda also makes a great mixer for Gin or Vodka.
