Unfortunately, they felt compelled to make it sweeter, so they added sucralose, also known by the brand name Splenda. If you're trying to avoid this artificial sweetener, then don't get this snack. But if you want some cocoa almonds, these are pretty good.

These fantastic dry-roasted almonds offer up all the chocolate-y taste of dipped almonds, thanks to their generous dusting of cocoa powder, without any of the higher-fat guilt.  Nice crunch with a hint of salty-sweetness (or would that be sweet-saltiness?)  We recently served them at a dinner party and everybody couldn't stop talking about how great they were.  Good luck stopping at a small handful!

I was a bit hesitant since they are dark chocolate and I'm a milk chocolate type of guy, I do like almonds though, so I decided to try them.  They're rather good.  Unlike other Chocolate nuts, these have a thin layer of chocolate that gives them a nice balance between the almonds and the chocolate.  Even my wife who doesn't like chocolate likes these quite a bit.

This product wasn't exactly what I thought it would be when I ordered it -- these are not "chocolate covered almonds," they are "cocoa powder dusted almonds."  Woe is me!  That said, I found that I enjoyed the more subtle flavor.Celiac and other allergy notes: Made with modified potato starch.  However, the product is processed on equipment that is also used to process wheat, soy, other types of nuts, and milk.A lot of thought went into product and packaging design.  This is a clean snack to eat, as the cocoa powder stays on the nut and doesn't get all over your hands.  The cannister is designed to fit in a car's drink holder (though at over 1500 calories per can, it's probably a REALLY bad idea to drive around with this so easily at hand), and the lid holds one serving's worth of nuts.  One serving is a satisfying little treat, but the tempation to keep filling the lid back up is nearly irresistible.

I was hesitant about these chocolate covered almonds thinking it's just a gimic.I can say I am hooked !  The chocolate gives the nuts a little something unexpected and extra.  I found myself eating a handful the first time.  I am not a huge fan of almonds but these are absolutely delicious.  They are not really sweet but the dark chocolate give a hint of sweetness and richness that i think plain almonds lack.They are addictive.  It's a good thing almonds are good for you !!  I would highly recommend these as a snack.  I also really like the twist lid.  It makes it so convienent to grab a handful.  yes, these almonds are the perfect snack !

Emerald's Cocoa Roast Almonds make a great on the go snack. I especially like the container as it fits nicely in the cup holder of my car and stroller. It makes a nice take-along snack during the day when running around and not having time for a meal always. The almonds have a hint of dark chocolate flavor. By the time you realize there's chocolate flavor, poof it's gone and you're onto the almond taste. For a person who enjoys almonds and the dark chocolate flavor is a bonus-this is still a nice snack. If you are purchasing this thinking it will be more dark chocolate and less almond, then you will likely be disappointed. I did not give 5-stars only because when I gave the almonds to my children who normally eat plain almonds and other nuts, they did not care for the dark chocolate roast. Hey what do kids know!

column9: The container was emptied in less than a day
column10: I am a lover of nuts in general and almonds in particular. My tastes are also strongly in favor of chocolate, so the combination is one that I like very much. Even better, the chocolate is in the form of very lightly sweetened cocoa powder. As someone who has a slight blood sugar problem, this feature is also one that I applaud. I received the package in the mail and by the end of the next day, I had consumed every nut. They are very good.

Great taste, great snack. Very fresh, tastes good, has a light cocoa dusting of dark chocolate on them. Not messy.  Great for keeping at your desk at work and munching on through out the day.  I really liked the flavor and freshness of this item.  I highly recommend.

Almonds may be the healthiest nut there is.  Indeed, famed psychic Edgar Cayce stated that eating 5 almonds a day will prevent cancer.  So, eating them is a nice, healthy & tasty insurance policy--hard to beat.  Adding the  cocoa makes them far tastier too.  Not overly chocolatie, sweet without being cloying, they satisfy my sometime craving for a sweet.  They go well with some fruit (I tried fresh apricots)--but CAUTION, like a certain potato chip they're hard to stop eating.  I went through half the container before stopping.  I don't think they'll last too long on my shelf.  On the other hand, if you have a big sweet tooth (or maybe all of them are sweet--if you have any left after eating tons of chocolate), they may not be sweet or chocolatie enough for you.  They are for me.  Enjoy!

column9: Get Set for a Nutty Surprise
column10: It occurred to me that sometimes you feel like a nut and sometimes you don't. I didn't feel like a nut when I sat down to try Emerald Cocoa Roast Almonds, but my wife did and so we started undressing the beast.I undid the top of the plastic wrap, she unscrewed the cap, and then I finished the job by peeling off the airtight barrier that sealed the top of the container.And that's when it happened.My wife grabbed the first almond and popped it in her mouth. I could actually hear the crunch of her first bite. She's tough to please and especially cynical about packaged foods that try to appear "new and different."Her eyes lit up. "Whoa, this is good."I grabbed an almond. She was right.She reached for another, and then two or three more. I popped about five in my mouth and went for the full chew. Then she did the same.When we came up for air, we talked about how surprised we were. The almonds were dry roasted and really crunchy. We expected something closer to soggy, like almonds sometimes get. The cocoa coating gave just the slightest hint of dark chocolate, and the sweetness didn't come through until we ate more than one at a time.Maybe best of all was that there was no discernible salty taste.My wife said, "I think they have a winner here." I took another handful before I decided I agreed.In the end, it's just a nut. But, boy, what a nut.

column4: Learning All The Time "It's Never Too Late to...
column10: I thoroughly enjoyed these almonds;  the almonds are fresh and crunchy, the cocoa not too messy or overpowering. The chocolate flavor is subtle, these are NOT milk chocolate covered almonds, and they are unlikely to stave off a true chocolate craving.  They're not really addictive either -- unlike salted nuts - I will plow through salted nuts until they are gone.  Nevertheless, they are still quite filling and satisfying.  A tasty change of pace.

Okay I have to admit it I am hooked on these almonds. The cocoa flavor is subtle, and delicious. The packaging is clever, and easy on the hands. The fact that almonds are also beneficial and good for you doesn't hurt either. The unique lid allows me to keep up with portion control which is a good thing, otherwise I would probably empty the can. These Cocoa Roasted Almonds are like eating an almond candy bar without the guilt.Highly recommended.

This is a very tasty and very good snack.  I absolutely love these.  I am a fan of almonds anyway so it wasn't a stretch when you combine almonds with another one of my favorites, dark chocolate, and you have a winner.The almonds taste fresh and as always they are meaty and filling.  I can enjoy these at about 7 or 8 at a serving which seems to me to be about the serving size at ¼ cup.Although these aren't unhealthy in the sense that there is a lot of junk added they certainly are not a weight loss tool.  At 150 calories per serving and 110 of that from fat you would be in serious trouble if this replaced baby carrots on your menu.All in all a very tasty treat.  I give it four stars instead of five only because of the high fat content even if it is healthier fats.

All of the chocolate lovers loved these nuts!!A great alternative to candy and junk foods. My daughter grabbed them and claimed them as hers, so I's say this was a good deal!!!The only thing one mAY or may NOT care for is this is not a soft, chocolatecovering but a dry, light covering.I think it tastes better as such and my daughter did not even notice.The nuts were very good themselves.This will go over well for the health and for the weight conscious persons.For me, while I liked them, I am NOT a sweet lover and found them very sweet FOR ME. but I still would buy and eat them ...a few daily ...to get the benefits of dark chocolate and almonds.

I was pleasantly surprised by how much I liked these nuts. At first I thought they were chocolate coated and sweet, but that's not the case. They are dusted in dark chocolate powder. That adds flavor but not a lot, if any, calories. A one oz. serving is 150 calories and yields 3 Weight Watcher Points instead of the usual four because of the high fiber count. Good deal. It satisfies two cravings in one serving. A very good way to get your nut goodness with some chocolate too. Enjoy!

column9: Sort of an inverse chocolate bar
column10: I like these more than I thought I would. They're sort of the inverse of a chocolate bar with almonds: instead of a lot of chocolate and few almonds, you get a lot of almonds and a little chocolate flavor. My personal preference tends toward high-cacao percentage chocolates, so the minimal sweetness here was not a problem for me. Also, and unlike conventional chocolate-covered nuts, these will not turn into a lumpy, gooey, mess if you leave them in the car this time of year.

These almonds are one of my favorite snacks. If you're trying to eat healthier but still crave a little sweetness or chocolate, this is the way to go. It can be a little dangerous to your diet if you eat TOO many at once but it makes you feel less guilty than some other snacks. I like that they aren't too sweet or too chocolate-y. You still taste the almonds despite the sweet coating. This is a product that I'll be buying again.

column9: Satisfying Chocolate Taste with the Almonds!
column10: These roasted almonds are coated with cocoa baked onto the outside of the nut. They are made in a way that the cocoa leaves no powder on the hands for no-mess eating, no stickiness, no powder, no mess. These are dry, these are not chocolate candy covered. The cocoa has a strong chocolate taste and is not sweet, it is delicious. The nuts also taste great.This would satisfy a chocolate craving. The great taste of the almonds and cocoa together is delicious!

Imperial is the brand I choose when buying nuts in the Dollar General store because it costs less than the others and the quality is good.  I had no idea they made such a gourmet treat as these Cocoa Roast Almonds but I'm certainly glad they do.  I was wondering if the coating of cocoa powder could be inhaled and cause choking (I've choked on dry cocoa powder dusted on the top of other foods) but they've added some potato start to make the coating stay put.  The dry roasted almonds are of a nice size and quality and the flavor is very good.  I think maybe they could be a bit less sweet and more dark-chocolately but still they're good and once you start eating them it's hard to stop so beware there.  These go great with a glass of Yellow Tail Cabernet Sauvignon.

column9: Tasty, but some Not too Healthy Ingredients
column10: These taste really good...slightly sweet and salty and not at all overpowering. Both almonds and dark chocolate are healthy ingredients and I would love to give this product 5 stars.But, there are also not so good ingredients in the product: artificial flavors and the artificial sweeteners, acesulfame potassium and sucralose. Therefore, I will not be purchasing this product in the futire.

column9: Dark Chocolate Lovers healthy dream come true.
column10: Oh My Goodness. Finally the taste of chocolate covered almonds that are actually good for you. I could not believe how yummy these are. The chocolate is dry covering and baked into the almond. The dark choc doesn't up the calories or fat, infact it is lower than others.These are a great source of protein and fiber. The only warning I would give is to measure out a 1 serving size and put the container away or you may be in trouble, they are hard to stop once you get started.I plan on chopping some and sprinkling over fat free ice cream for a real treat without the guilt.You will not be disappointed with these almonds, if you love dark chocolate or any chocolate for that matter give these a try.Amazon has the best deal on them also. Take these to the beach and on vacation this year instead of unhealthy chips and candy..they fill both cravings, sweet and salty.

Don't expect chocolate-coated nuts from this can.  The cocoa, not chocolate, flavor is more subtle and roasted into the nut, and I like it for that.  As one would expect from Emerald, the almonds are top-quality too.  It's a tasty and healthy treat, but relatively high in calories and especially in fat - which again, one should expect from a whole-nut product.  If you like almonds, they are definitely worth a try.

column9: Good almonds, but where's the chocolate?
column10: These tasty almonds are very (VERY) lightly-covered with dark cocoa powder, but if I hadn't read the label, I wouldn't have noticed.  The thin coating gives off an unknown, slightly muddy flavor that is not unpleasant, but if you're looking for a strong, true chocolate taste, skip these nuts.  (I think they would taste better without the coating.)There are 11 servings in a jar, each with 150 calories, and the lid measures one serving perfectly.  They're good and crunchy and I like them, even though they don't have the chocolate flavor I was expecting.

The nuts taste fresh and have a hint of sweet dark chocolate.  There is more almond taste to it than dark chocolate, which is a great thing.  The chocolate flavor compliments the almonds well.  Great crunch, and has no after taste.  All the almonds are uniform in size and great as a snack anytime of the day.  Each canister is a generous size and is a great value for your money.  I highly recommend you give these almonds from Emerald a try.

I'm in love with a jar of nuts. I'm hopelessly (but happily :)) addicted to these almonds. Heavenly. Adopted a healthy eating lifestyle since Jan 1 (and lost over 40lbs), after having sworn off chocolate and all things 'bad' that taste good, these nuts are an amazing treat!! Same nutritional profile as regular almonds, cocoa chocolately taste that isn't too sweet, and not too bitter. Perfection!

column9: Healthy chocolate snack.  Can it be?
column10: This is a great little snack for those chocolate lovers who want something healthy and a little bonus for their sweet tooth.  The almonds are just lightly coated with cocoa powder. So, it's not the same as having a creamy candy bar. But, you can snack on these for the same amount of calories you'd get with a handful of almonds instead of having a big old fat candy bar.  And, you get all the nutrition of nuts and their good fats with only 1 gram of saturated fat per serving.I'm a chocaholic and true chocaholics don't like their chocolate overly sweet.  These have a hint of a dark chocolate flavor and just a hint of sweetness.  The almonds are nice and crunchy since they are roasted.I gave these four stars out of five.  Some might miss the creaminess of a chocolate bar and these won't completely take the place a of a good piece of dark chocolate.  But,they are great to have around when you just need something to take the edge off of that chocolate craving.

If you're a nut lover this may be just what you are looking for. After all, once you get beyond proper roasting, there isn't a whole lot you can say about nuts other than what you add to them. If you bury them in salt, or immerse them in chocolate, you are getting more flavor, but the trade off is unwanted cane sugar, and/or salt; so these make a pleasant bridge.Extra added flavor with the thin coat of dark chocolate cocoa powder (that doesn't get on your fingers by the way), while only ingesting 25mg of sodium in a single 1/4 cup serving.When I first started to eat them, I thought the dry unsweetened cocoa powder didn't add anything desirable to the flavor, but as I progressed to finishing about a 1/4 cups worth, I began to realize that this could very well become a strongly acquired taste.If I had to be critical of the entire presentation, I would note that the plastic "jar" has a threaded top with 2 half circle single threads partially overlapping each other that results in a not so very snug closure. With very little effort you can snug them at closure and skip right past snug to loose again, so much so that if you dropped the container the lid may pop off, spilling the contents.I am not commenting on the way they are sealed though, they did an outstanding job of that. You have to pop open the plastic seal over the top of the lid edge, just to remove the screw on top, and then once open, there is an internal air tight seal to keep the contents fresh, and they are. Overall highly recommended, especially if you are nuts about nuts.

Emerald Cocoa Roast Almonds are almonds roasted with cocoa rather than covered with chocolate, which makes them healthier and less fattening than traditional chocolate-covered almonds. This is is an advantage if you don't want to have to wear clothing made in Indonesia, a highly laudable goal considering that country's trumped-up 2005 drug-smuggling conviction of a young Australian tourist. What's more, they taste excellent, too. In fact, these are chocolate-flavored nuts for people who care about watching their weight.

The dark chocolate flavor of these airy almonds makes this snack something to look forward to.The flavor is mild. Just enough chocolaty flavor for chocolate lovers but not too overpowering or sweet.  The texture of the almonds seem airy. They are lighter than what I'm used to. It's a nice touch to the flavor. Not too heavy.One 11 oz container holds 11 servings. Each serving approximately 1/4 cup.  For 150 calories per serving this snack also packs 6g protein, 8% iron and an impressive 35% Vitamin E.Overall, my entire family enjoyed this snack and I plan to stash one in my office at work as well as in my tote bag.Excellent snack!

Don't be fooled by appearances--the chocolate taste on these nuts is very subtle. They look to be coated in melted chocolate, but it's more of a delicate dusting, so if you're looking for chocolate-coated candy, look elsewhere. However, if you're looking for a lighter, nutty pick-me-up, you can't go wrong with these.  Highly recommended!

column9: Delicious twist on traditionally salted almonds
column10: I wouldn't normally buy a product like this, but I had an opportunity to try this product out and I was pleasantly surprised.  The almonds are roasted with a light layer of dark chocolate powder.  The chocolate lends a subtly  pleasant taste to the almonds and is a welcome alternative to salt.  It is not overpowering for the almond and leaves a sweet aftertaste.  Delicious.The chocolate is roasted on in such a way that it does not leave you fingers covered in chocolate.The packaging is also nicely done.

As  a dedicated chocolate and almond lover this is exactly the sort of thing that would appeal to me.  And I wasn't disappointed.  The fresh, crisp almonds are beautifully complimented by their coating of cocoa.  They're lightly sweet, too.  Just enough to give you the full flavor of both chocolate and nut.  The only problem I have with them is that they're sweetened with sucralose, which is an artificial sweetener, and which may or may not be good for us.  There doesn't appear to be a great deal of it in the mix -- it's the last listed ingredient -- but for some it might be a problem.As with the Marcona almonds I tried earlier, these nuts have persuaded me to think of Emerald as a better brand than I originally thought.  They have some interesting offerings, and the quality of the ones I've tried has been consistently high.If the flavor combination appeals to you, and you don't mind a bit of sucralose, then by all means give  these nuts a try.

Emerald Dark Chocolate Almonds has just enough dark cocoa to soothe your cravings.  Roasted into the almonds, the cocoa power is not the messy treat that other brands offer.  These are clean eating, delicious nuts.But don't kid yourself.  There's not enough cocoa in these almonds to provide much in the way of antioxidant power.  Eat them simply because they're good, although they are a good source of Vitamin E and potassium.On the down side, these almonds are sweetened with sucrolose (Splenda), so if you're staying away from artificial sweeteners, avoid these almonds.  Hint to Emerald:  Try Stevia as the sweetener.Taste:  Five StarsArtificial Sweetner:  One StarAverage: Three Stars

column9: Elegant healthy alternative to chocolate covered nuts
column10: Could a thin cocoa coating satisfy a chocolate almond craving? I was pleasantly surprised with these almonds. With a big chocolate aroma, delicate dark chocolate flavor and exceptionally crunchy texture they are great as is or I also like to put out a bowl of them mixed with dried cherries.

This snack product is very addictive!  The first few bites actually come across a little strongly, with the "roasted" taste definitely the first thing you'll notice.  However, the cocoa taste, while more subtle, soon overtakes the initial burst and it's almost as though you've got a small candy bar in your mouth.  My eldest daughter wasn't sure at first if she actually liked them, but once she ate a few, she quickly took off with the rest of the jar.  If you love almonds, you will love these bite-sized bits of flavor!

column9: Really Good...just a hint of cocoa
column10: Not as sweet as a chocolate covered nut, these are really good snack. It tones down that "roasted" flavor of the almond with just a hint of chocolate. Great snacks, lots of protein.

The Other Brother and I realized the other day that we've somehow been posting these reviews for ten years already.  Suffice it to say, The Wife has long since lost any sense of excitement she may ever have felt at the piles of free books that have come our way.  At this point, each thud of a package dropped on our front porch produces at best a cringe, at worst a snarl.  Best, that is, until the other day, when we received samples -- through the Amazon Vine program -- of two new nuts from Emerald: Cocoa Roast Almonds and Marcona Almonds.  I like the Marconas, which taste kind of like Macadamias, but don't have the almost soapy texture that has rendered them inedible to me since childhood.  She loves the dark chocolate one, which, "satisfies both the salty and the sweet urge in one snack."  These latter are most notable because they manage to leave a pleasant chocolate aftertaste--not always the case in flavored foods.  Big thumbs up!

column9: Lots of Nut, Little Chocolate; Mixed Results
column10: I was particularly excited to try Emerald Cocoa Roast Almonds when they arrived in the mail today as I love chocolate and I love nuts.Five individuals ranging in age from 2 to 50 tried these together and shared feedback. A few common threads emerged.1. Chocolate doesn't come off on your hands: Very convenient as there is almost no residue left on hands even after holding a handful of nuts for a minute.2. Very subtle chocolate flavor: For some this is a plus and for some this is a negative. You know the chocolate is there, but in my opinion it just leave you wanting more chocolate. I couldn't eat more than 10 or so for that reason. They were just plain frustrating. This was the consensus of 4 out of the 5 taste testers. The fifth loved them and plans on finishing off my canister and probably ordering more. They are definitely not milk chocolately, but have barely discernible, subtle dark chocolate undertones.3. Dry: We all needed to drink water immediately after tasting the nuts as they dried our mouths out, much more than normal salted or roasted almost or any other nut for that matter. Three of us described them as tasting "burnt" or "too roasted".4. We keep eating them: Even though I'm not crazy about these nuts -  in fact only one of us was - we keep coming back for more about every hour or so. I get frustrated every time I do, either wanting a chocolate bar or just some plain old chocolate. Perhaps this is a good trait in a snack, that you can't keep eating them ad nauseum.Other observationsThe 11 oz ergonomically comfortable container is about 8 inches tall and fits perfectly in your hand or in the cup holder of the car. The lid is screw-on rather than flip-top. The package contains 11 servings of 150 calories apiece (120 calories from fat), 13 grams of fat, six grams of carbs, and 6 grams of protein. Very much the same as other nut products.The conclusion? If you aren't sure already that you love these nuts, buying a four-pack might be too much for you. But if you love them, you love them, as evidenced by our one taste tester and many of the other reviews. I'd recommend trying a smaller volume before ordering in bulk here.

If you're like me, sometimes you might just crave the taste of chocolate, despite the fact that you really know you shouldn't eat any (assuming it's not on your eating plan)!Well, if that's the case, than these Emerald Cocoa Roast Almonds will alleviate those cravings while providing a healthy snack chock full of protein and healthy fats.I only ate 5 of these almonds and was completely satisfied. The cocoa has a subtle, yet tasty, chocolaty flavor and the almonds tasted fresh.My son, though, really enjoys these nuts and eats 'em by the handful.  This is a good product I'd completely recommend.

These Emerald "Cocoa Roast Almonds" are a low carb snack that bring a bit of dark chocolate flavor to good tasting almonds. These do have artificial sweeteners, but for those of us that have to watch our sugar intake, this is a very viable treat.Highly Recommended!CFH

I have started eating almonds as a healthy alternative to fatty or high-carb snacks, but wanted something to satisfy my sweet tooth on occasion. These Cocoa Roast almonds fit the bill nicely. They just have a dusting of cocoa, so there's no more fat or unhealthy stuff than you would find in regular almonds, but you still get a nice chocolate taste. They are just a little bit sweeter than I really want (I like dark chocolate, semisweet or bittersweet) but still a great once-in-awhile snack!

Almonds are popular because of their antioxidant capacity. The almond is rich in the antioxidant vitamin E. Antioxidants, such as vitamin E, can help prevent cardiovascular diseases and cancer, and slow down the aging process (hasn't helped me in that area). The magnesium in almonds helps strengthen bones and plays a role in different enzyme processes in our body. Almonds are, like all nuts, rich in unsaturated fat.The nutritional value of almonds is well documented. Some time ago I read an article in a Sunday paper magazines about the health benefits of almonds and have since been eating a daily handful of these tasty, nutritious nuts. Examine the label of any almond product and you'll see that almonds are good sources of Vitamin E, riboflavin, thiamin, niacin and folate. Munch some almonds, and you'll also get a bit of calcium, magnesium, copper, manganese, phosphorus, and zinc. Like other nuts, almonds are calorie intense and must be eaten in moderation. After all, too much of a good thing can result in negative consequences.Do some study and you'll see that almonds are almost universally touted for their health benefits. The antioxidants in almonds are said to help in preventing the aging process, lowering the risk of gallstones, lowering blood pressure and lessening the risk of cardiovascular disease and diabetes. No, munching a daily mouthful of almonds won't guarantee longevity or good health, but it's certainly a step in the right direction and most certainly is more beneficial than a mouthful of sugar-laden candy. I like that almonds are good for me and that they help me maintain my chiseled physique, but mostly I eat these crunchy wonders because they are so delicious and satisfying.Of all the varieties and brands of almonds I have ever eaten these are now my all time and present favorite. The chocolate coating is not what I had imagined. Instead of the milk chocolate candy coating I'd anticipated, the chocolate coating on these almonds is dry and powdery. The taste is subtle but dynamic and satisfying at the same time. Instead of an overwhelming candy sensation, one gets a complementary chocolate taste that heightens and accentuates the almond taste. I like that the dry chocolate coating doesn't insidiously stick to one hands and everything a snacker might touch. It's safe to read your favorite book or the latest edition of the Almondac while snacking on these Cocoa Roast Almonds.Eating these delicious nuts is an almond joy made even more delightful by playing some Almond Brothers music in the background . These nuts are so delicious that one can easily get carried away and eat too many. It's best to set aside a portion first and then seal the container.

I was quite excited to try these cocoa roasted almonds out. I love almonds and I love chocolate. And most reviews of this product imply that you get your fix of both, without the extra sugar.Well there's definitely a whole lot less sugar in this thing - it tastes pretty bad to me. And I was quite shocked. I guess I need at least a little more sweet. But I'm shocked because I'm not THAT much of a sweet tooth. It's the bitter after-taste that really bothers me with this product. I really couldn't take it.So just fair warning to those who might think this is going to be a great combo of chocolate and almond. Think again! This is really just cocoa and almond, and, for me, that left a very bad taste.

column9: Cocoa Covered Almonds are the Best!
column10: I lost over 100 lbs. and these are an excellent and tasty source of fiber and protein.  I love these almonds and I subscribe and make sure I have a container on hand at all times.  The price is great, also, compared to the supermarkets where I live.
What a great idea with the cocoa and they would be great except for the sucrolose "diet" taste.  Don't think I'll buy again.

These nuts are a decent snack on their own and I've made cookies with them as well. They are slightly sweet and I don't think the Splenda taste is overwhelming or unpleasant, but that is obviously a personal preference. Bought them on sale at Target for $3 a package, or about half the current listed price here.

I'm a person that really loves nuts, especially flavored nuts.  When I go the local farmer's market, I always look for the nut stand so I can buy some kind of cinnamon, honey, jalapeño, or whatever-flavor strikes me.When I was offered a chance to try the cocoa almonds, I was pretty thrilled.These nuts just "okay".  They're not spectacular.  As another reviewer noted, they aren't very chocolately.  If you have a chocolate craving, this will just make it worse.  They're also very dry (as are most almonds) and you'll need something to wash down every handful.The almonds are high-quality, and it's a good cocoa taste, but don't expect to be blown away by this.  It just won't happen.The container is probably what impressed me the most.  It's sturdy, resuable, handy to hold, and the screw-top keeps the product fresh.If you're looking for almonds with a subtle cocoa (not milk chocolate) hint then this is for you.  But have a drink handy.

column4: Livin' La Vida Low-Carb Man "Jimmy Moore"
column9: Cocoa-Roasted Almonds, Where Ya Been My Whole Life?!
column10: Can I just tell you right off the bat, this product is utterly amazing!  Ever since I lost 180 pounds on the Atkins low-carb diet in 2004 eating healthy low-carb foods like almonds, I've been looking for ways to enhance my menus with something a little new while still keeping my carbs reduced.  These nuts from Emerald certainly do the trick with a unique twist:  DARK CHOCOLATE!When I first saw these, I thought they were coffee beans.  But upon closer examination, you realize these are almonds that have been dusted with dark chocolate cocoa and Splenda.  That's right, NO SUGAR has been put in these bad boys.  It's the best of both worlds--healthy AND tastes good!  I'm adding these to my regular "must buy" list when I go shopping because you never want to be without these when you need a great-tasting snack.  ENJOY!

Forget the calories -- these almonds are great -- they taste as though they were INFUSED with the chocolate!! A combination of Chocolate-sweet-enough-to-delight the tastebuds, combined with a fresh almond taste.And these almonds are BIG.One almond led to the other and I had to force myself to put the cannister down.Ever the culinary experimenter, I placed some Emerald Cocoa Roast Almonds in my Cuisinart and ground them -- then I added the ground almonds to a bowl of freshly made Instant Vanilla pudding -- great taste -- almost like marzipan. I also added some to a smoothie, with positive results.Almonds are a good health food. Chocolate is the 9th wonder of the world, as far as I'm concerned. In my opinion, Emerald Cocoa Roast Almonds are a great meeting of two "foodstuffs" -  eaten right from the canister or as a special ingredient to some of your recipes.

I try to eat a lot of almonds because they are really good for you. Studies say you should eat about an ounce and a half a day. This product is a tasty way to do that. The cocoa dust on them gives a sweet dark chocolate taste to the almonds without the fat of dipping them in chocolate. Cocoa is good for you, too, reportedly having similar benefits to drinking a glass of red wine every day. The two together here are a real treat that you can feel good about eating. The canister they're in is a good size for sharing or portioning them out over time because it's reclosable. My family loved them and I know we'll be buying these regularly.

column9: A More Flavorful and Satisfying Way to Enjoy Almonds
column10: I started eating almonds regularly after going on the South Beach Diet. I find them quite delicious . . . so delicious that I have to remind myself that I'm only supposed to eat 15 or so a day.  Oh, well.I could easily eat a handful . . . and still wouldn't feel like I had gotten enough flavor.I had no idea what a cocoa roast almond would taste like, but I was pleasantly surprised that the taste was superb. It reminded me a little of eating a high quality fudge with lots of nuts in it.But the nice surprise was that the cocoa taste lingered in my mouth so that I continued to enjoy the flavor long after the almonds were eaten. Even though the cocoa roasting adds some calories and some fat, I would be satisfied after eating far fewer of these almonds. I plan to buy and eat these on a regular basis.Try them. I think you'll like them!

column4: J. Rose "JR From the Ball so Blue"
column9: Chocolate Almonds for the "price" of regular ones? Amazing
column10: I got these because I am familiar with the brand and had enjoyed their products in the past. These things are amazing. They're my new favorite snack.I love chocolate.I love almonds.And here I have two great tastes together, but without the added fat or sugar. As a diabetic, I love finding food that feels like I'm doing something bad, but I'm not.These are it.My biggest problem is making myself measure them out and only eating that amount, and not the entire package.For those with an aversion to Splenda, it is present in this product.For everyone else, enjoy!

These almonds make a good snack. The cocoa coating isn't sweet -- in fact, it's vaguely bitter -- and it isn't overpowering. The nuts themselves were good and fresh. My wife and I both liked them.On the other hand, my daughter said "I don't hate them, but I don't love them either." Save these for the adults -- they'd work well with red wine or sweet cocktails.

If you like chocolate that isn't too sweet, you'll be delighted by this lightly dusted cocoa almond snack. This is the type of snack you can't eat just one of, and would be perfect to serve at a dinner party too, as it is quite elegant.

I wasn't entirely sure what I would be getting when I ordered these, but I'm glad I did. There's just the right balance of salty and sweet -- the chocolate flavoring is perfect.  Plus, the container is great for stowing in a desk drawer or even in the car for an on-the-go treat.

column9: Two Great Tastes Come Together In A Healthy Snack
column10: The front of the label for these almonds from Emerald mentions two things that I am fond of:  almonds and dark chocolate.  I went in with hopes that combining two good things together would result in something better than the two separately.  In this case the result is pretty good.  While this is only mentioned on the product page (and not the actual container itself), the lid doubles as a measuring cup for a single serving.  After having these over the last few days, here are my impressions.While I like the taste (a lot!), it wasn't exactly what I was expecting.  When I think of dark chocolate, I'm expecting a taste similar to a piece of Dove Dark Chocolate miniatures.  It is a taste that is rich with a very mild sweetness.  The coating on these almonds is a little bit sweeter than that.  It's nowhere near milk chocolate, but like I said it wasn't exactly what I expected.  That said these are still really good.  The almonds themselves are great with only a minute amount of salt.  With the chocolate and the natural flavor of almonds this is a sweet treat.Who It's For:  Disciplined people looking for a sweet, but healthy snack.Suggested Use:  A single serving makes a great between meals snack.  If your stomach starts to rumble around 10 a.m., this will bridge the gap to lunch.  I have the canister in a desk drawer at work.  Regardless of when/where/how you use them as snack, discipline and moderation are key.Potential Improvements:  The one thing that bugs me on these is that the 11 oz package does not divide evenly into 1.5 oz servings.  It would seem like a 12 oz canister would have been easy enough.Overall:  This is a great tasting, healthy snack to enjoy in moderation.

This is an innovative concept.  Dust and roast the almonds in chocolate powder so you get the light taste of chocolate, without a heavy candy-coating of chocolate full of calories and sugar.  These almonds are crunchy, non-salted, and not too sweet with a hint of dark chocolate taste.  Only 1 gram of sugar per serving, with 3 g of dietary fiber.  So it meets the South Beach diet criteria.  6% Calcium, 8% Iron and 35% Vitamin E.  My family loved them and these disappeared too quickly.

column9: Chocolate coated almonds, but not in the normal way...
column10: Most "chocolate covered" nuts tend to be a nut with a full coating of chocolate wrapped around it, that can be even slipped off and eaten separately ot licked off, etc.Not so with these Cocoa Roast almonds -- what we have here are full sized almonds with their skin still on given a slight bit of dark chocolate powder over them as flavor.And it works fantastically. Another review mentioned that they may not be sweet enough for soda drinkers, but I disagree. They are nuts, they aren't candy. They are easy to suck the flavor off, or just eat normally. And while the skin is still on them, they don't make a mess like normal almonds do -- perhaps it's the cocoa coating or perhaps they are just processed a certain way.Not only do they taste wonderful, but the added flavor doesn't mean less healthy.Really, a four and a half star product. While it's a fantastically unique taste, the packaging has a really SILLY warning that it "CONTAINS ALMONDS" right under the ingredients list. And $6 a cannister means it's not something everyone can just buy many of and have whenever they want.

column9: Less guilty then a real chocolate coated nut.
column10: For those people who enjoy eating chocolate w/ nuts, this is a great product that gives you a little bit of that taste w/ a lot less guilt.  I enjoyed the product as did my Toddler. The nuts are dry w/ a dusting of chocolate that isn't too sweet to the taste.It's good that it gives only hint of the chocolate. I wouldn't say it is addictive as some of the other flavors like the standard smoked seasoned ones, but it is enjoyable. The coating is pretty dry and doesn't come off on your fingers either, so eating it w/ your fingers is pretty mess free.

column9: Superb Snack - but artificial flavor added
column10: I am torn: 4 stars or 5 stars? I decided on 5 stars:- The taste is great! If you are Coke or Pepsi drinker, then they may not be sweet enough for you. I am not, hence I and my entire family enjoyed their subtle chocolaty flavor.- The nutritional content is not bad at all, except artificial flavoring, which I would never notice on my taste buds if it was not written.All-in-all -- absolutely delicious and filling snack!

The almonds are crispy and delicious, and cocoa powder gives a nice chocolate flavor without being all thick and gummy like the nuts with an actual chocolate coating.So the taste is good, the crunchiness is nice, and apparently they're just about as good for you as normal almonds.I'd get them again.

column9: a tasty, not too sweet snack
column10: If you are looking for a nutty snack that is not too sweet, this might be for you.  My husband and I both tried them.  He thinks this is more of a 5 star item.  He liked the fresh nuts with just a bit of a cocoa taste, and though I liked them, I would say they are maybe in the three star category, because I was hoping for something slightly sweeter.  We both liked that the coating was not a "come off in your hand" kind of variety that makes you look for something to wipe your hands on.We both enjoyed them though I don't know that I would purchase them for myself again.  Nothing wrong with them, just not sweet enough for me.  I would however purchase for my husband.As with any nut product, they are high in fiber and the good kind of fat, but you don't want to dip into too many if you are dieting as they run 150 calories for 1/4 cup, so portion accordingly.
WOW! I can't believe that these chocolaty almonds contain no more calories than plain almonds. They taste sinfully delicious. The perfect balance of nutty flavor and chocolate. Very satisfying!!!

column9: Not sweet enough the first time, but it got better
column10: I like almonds, and I loooove chocolate!  Even dark chocolate.  The problem is that putting the two together doesn't create an especially healthy or low-calorie snack.  But these almonds aren't dipped in melted chocolate, they are dusted with a dark chocolate cocoa powder.  In theory, that sounds like the best of both worlds...... but to me, it tasted kinda like they were covered in dirt.  Well, maybe not dirt, but not exactly sweetness either.  And that may not quite satisfy those of us with a BIG sweet tooth.  But after subsequent servings I grew to like them much more.  I passed some around the office and the reception was much more positive than my initial taste test (of course, it might have just been because it was free food...).  And once I decided to share them with the kids all I had left was an empty container.So, as I sniff the pleasant aroma of roasted almonds and dark chocolate from an empty container, I must admit it makes a good snack for the office, although 4 stars is a bit generous.  Even a small serving is mostly satisfying and low-calorie enough that I don't have to feel guilty.  My biggest complaint, however, is with the lid.  It just won't screw on tight.  Every time I tighten it, the threads slip and it's loose again.  Maybe the next container will be better...

I really thought I would love these.  I like all kinds of nuts, roasted and otherwise.  I like all kinds of chocolate, really like dark chocolate.  Heck, I even love mocha roast coffees and dark beers described as nutty. But I don't love this product.  Maybe it's just me.  I understand it's not cocoa in the sense of a creamy coating, but rather it's a dry dusting that is not unhealthy.  I understand it's dark cocoa.  But I didn't like the taste.  I will end up mixing these in with other trail mixtures.If you havn't tried them, I'd maybe find a way to get a nibble somewhere before buying a four pack.  You might love em.  Or like me, you might be surprised.

Diamond Foods is the company that for nearly 90 years has been ubiquitously marketing its quality packaged nuts throughout the world. The Emerald product line was started by the company in 2003 to market their products to a more upscale consumer segment, where Emerald trades on the particular hipster, dinner-party image that their products sometime bring to mind.Emerald roasted almonds come packaged in durable 11-ounce canisters with screw-on tops to help keep the product fresh (and, it should be noted, indented sides so that one's hands can easily grasp the container even if one has previously imbibed a few cocktails). Sampling the contents, I was not disappointed; I found the almonds to be as flavorful and addictive as they can be. Interestingly, Emerald also chose to provide a variety of flavoring options such as dark chocolate to help keep things interesting for us. Bravo!The bottom line is that if you like almonds, buying the Emerald product should be an easy decision for you to make. Highly recommended!

column9: I like Almonds and I like Dark Chocolate . . .
column10: but I guess I don't really love them together. The chocolate is not sweet at all (they also have no other flavor to them), which means I can only eat about three before I feel like their getting bitter.  It may be that their just too dark for me and they will not be too strong for someone else.  they would probably be good in a trail mix of some kind to give your taste buds some flavor variety.

column9: Not as good as other Emerald nuts
column10: I'm not a huge almond fan but I can like them.  I am a huge dark chocolate fan so when I saw this product I thought "Great".  One serving is approximately 25-27 almonds I measured and contains little "bad fat" and lots of protein and fiber for the amount.  The cocoa appears to be baked on and not merely sprinkled or the nuts rolled in it because it clings really well to the product.  The almonds are nice and big, well roasted, and taste just like you'd expect from an almond.  There in lay my greatest complaint: the cocoa wasn't very noticeable.  Was it dark cocoa?  Maybe but because the taste was subtle it was a bit difficult for me to tell.  In a world where we need to be eating healthier I know that we might have to change how we eat chocolate but unless almonds are one of your favorite nuts, try one of the many other brands of cocoa-covered or yogurt-covered varieties all in easy to open and reseal containers.  So far, the cocoa-dusted walnuts are my favorite.

The almonds are fresh and the addition of the dark chocolate flavor makes for an addicting taste. Almonds in limited quantities as opposed to finishing the entire container can be quite healthy. The problem with these is that it is near impossible to stop eating them. Please note that these are not chocolate covered almonds but rather almonds with a covering of dark chocolate powder. They are healthy and quite delicious.

I think I made a big mistake getting a container of these Cocoa Roast Almonds, because I cannot stop eating them. Everyone I've shared them with (shared 1 or 2 almonds, I'm keeping the rest for me!) gives me a look like they are willing to wrestle me to the ground to get the rest of the container.Very subtle chocolate flavor (I got the Dark Chocolate) that vaguely makes you think of brownies. Not overly sweet, but definitely not bitter the way one worries about [dark chocolate] cocoa powder.I'd give six stars if Amazon had them.The cap of the container is supposed to be used for determining a single serving, but I treated the entire 11 ounce container as a single serving.

ProsExcellent tastingFreshNice hint of chocolate flavoringConsPackage slightly hard to open. Had to tear wrapping from the top then tear it completely off the top before I could open it.Inner seal was a little hard to remove with my fingers.Not vacuum packed as I thought it might be.ReviewA pleasent surprise on my first tasting. Cocoa flavoring is not overpowering. Nuts are firm and easy to chew. The 11 oz package is a good size plus the shape is very good. I like the large indentations on two sides which make the outer container easy to hold with one hand. Seems to be one of those "can't stop eating it" kinds of foods. It's really that good. The serving size according to the package is 11 however I expect to finish the product in 3 to 4 servings. The handy screw top is nice too and would seem to keep this item fresh between servings. This is something I would order fairly often and keep in my house to share with anyone who drops by for a visit. I also found the product information on the back easy to read against a light green background.

column9: The Flavor Has Me Starry Eyed...
column10: ...thus the five star review. Pun intended.Now the critical part.  Wouldn't these lightly-dusted cocoa-y almonds be just as good without the artificial flavors, acesulfame potassium, and sucralose? Whatever those items are. And wouldn't it be a good idea to eliminate them in any case if most people who buy almonds as snacks are prone to being a little health wacky?Still, my Emerald Cocoa Roast Almonds, Dark Chocolate, will become a permanent fixture at my desk to help keep the hunger pangs away when I'm  in the middle of writing a chapter for my new book and just can't pull myself away from the computer.----Reviewed by Carolyn Howard-Johnson, award-winning author of This Is The Place,

column9: Almond Candy Bar without the Candy
column10: I found these delicious and highly addictive... you may not be able to eat just one!According to the wrapper, the Serving Size is one ounce (about 1/4 cup) and there are 11 servings in the container.  Nutritional information includes these facts:Total Fat 13g  (Saturated Fat 1g; Polyunsaturated Fat 3g; Monounsaturated Fat 8g)Sodium 25mgPotassium 210mgTotal Carbohydrate 6g (Dietary Fiber 3g; Sugars 1g)Protein 6gIngredients: Dry Roasted Almonds, Modified Food Starch (potato), Natural & Artificial Flavors, Cocoa Powder (processed with alkali), Salt, Acesulfame Potassium, Sucralose.Allergy information: This product is processed on equipment that also processes other tree nuts, peanuts, wheat, soy, milk and sesame seeds.
Wow, I loved these!  Almonds with a rich dark chocolate taste but with minimal added carbs.  Nice touch with the cap being able to measure out a standard serving.  A great healthy snack.

column9: Not what I expected -- but in a good way
column10: When I opened this plastic jar of roasted almonds, I expected something like chocolate-covered peanuts a la almond.  Nope, that's not what happened.  It turned out that these are almonds that are dusted in cocoa.  The chocolate flavor is really rich, mainly because it's dark chocolate.  I like these as a treat, and I realized that they'd go really well with a cup of coffee.  They aren't snack food, unless the snacker has really odd sense of taste.  I found that they're best if you just eat about two or three of them at a time, with or without coffee.  Come to think of it, I'll likely brew me up a cup of a rich French or African roast, just because that cup of java would go well with this treat.  Be careful, however, when opening the container because the pungent flavor might make you sneeze.  More than three dusted almonds will also likely dry out your mouth.

I like these.  Like the packaging too.  These are not chocolate dipped, but cocoa powdered.  And the flavor is cocoa, not chocolate.  Very sweet.  Probably good because a few go along way.  Very flavorful.

I like a good nut, and these Emerald Cocoa Roast nuts are pretty good nuts.  As I am also a chocoholic, though, my opinion may be biased.  :-)Not that these are overly chocolate-flavored.  This is not a chocolate covered almond.  Instead, these are almonds coated in cocoa powder.  It's not even glazed--just dusted, stuck on with oil.  Because the cocoa powder isn't strongly sweetened, you get a good mix of nut flavor with a chocolate chaser.  They're subtle, and good for a little munching ... but not for prolonged snacking; I found that after five or six nuts, they sort of lost flavor in my mouth until I cleansed my palette with a drink.All in all, these nuts are a nice change of pace from typical salted fare, without bringing the heavy sweetness of a honey raost to the party.  I would definitely buy them again.

I was pleasantly surprised by the Cocoa Roast almonds. They are not dipped in chocolate like a candy, but dusted with a slightly sweet cocoa powder that does not overpower the natural taste of the almonds. It is enough to make a person who does not usually snack on almonds (me) keep reaching for more. They're totally healthy, and totally addictive. A+.

These are nice... the almonds are fresh, and the light cocoa coating is tasty and not bitter.  The marriage here of chocolate and almond is just right; the only negative thing any person could ever say is this:  compared to an almond dipped entirely in dark chocolate, these pale.If you can eat one single chocolate dipped almond, that would be fine and healthy.  These have fewer calories, and they just feel better for you, especially when you have a handful.Good enough so that I long to try the other flavors.
I was excited to try these as a low-carb treat but didn't realize they contain artificial sweeteners.  Terrible aftertaste and the almond and cocoa flavors are overpowered by the fake sweeteners.

column9: Good despite faint terrible fake sugar taste
column10: Great concept and they are pretty tasty -- very chocolately -- but the artificial sweetner taste just kills these.  I wish they'd make a version without the splenda (or whatever it is), they'd be so much better with real sugar or even no sugar.

These were hugely disappointing for me. They just taste bad. They're not very "chocolatey" tasting, but they have a very strong artificial sweetener kind of aftertaste. I can't recommend these on any level.I gave these two stars instead of one simply  because they were on sale cheap when I got them. If they had been at regular price, one star would have been generous.

column9: Good Treat For A Party, But Pricey for Everyday Munching
column10: The Emerald Cocoa dusted almonds were tasty.  The cocoa did not overwhelm the nuts and make them sweet, but rather added just a bit of background interest and flavor.  The almond taste still came through and continued to have the appropriate amount of saltiness.Although the taste was wonderful, you did have to get by the fact that they looked liked "dirty nuts".  Knowing what they were before you ate them helped.  I would not buy these on a day to day basis as they are fairly pricey. I do, however think they would be a hit if placed out on a party tray.  They were excellent with the red wine that we tried them with!

column9: Chocolate + almonds = A match made in heaven!
column10: Let me just out myself from the get-go here--I am a HUGE chocoholic.  I am also an almond lover and eat a small handful of dry roasted, unsalted almonds nearly every day.  So, when I saw dark chocolate cocoa-roasted almonds offered on amazon, it seemed a match made in heaven. :)What surprised me most, I think, about these delicious cocoa-roasted almonds is that they are not over sweet (only 1 gram of sugar per 1/4 cup serving).  I worried that they would taste like candy and that is not something I need more of (I am already slave enough to the Sweet Monster!).Another pleasant surprise was that the almonds are not salty.  I have hypertension and need to limit my salt so, when the almonds arrived and I reviewed the nutrition label, I was pleased to see that they only have 25 mg of sodium per 1/4 cup serving and that they are made with dry-roasted vs. oil-roasted almonds.In my chocoholic fervor while ordering, I hadn't paid attention to what size cannister the almonds would come in, so I was again pleasantly surprised to find that they came in a generous 11 oz. cannister.I had some friends over last weekend and put out a dish of the almonds on the table.  I lost count of how many times I heard "Mmm! These are GOOD!" but I know that the dish was nearly empty when they left.

I am not an almond lover, unless they are deep down inside an Almond Joy bar.  I like cashews, pecans, peanuts--but only the salted varieties. So when these little cocoa dusted beauties arrived yesterday, I was not expecting seduction. I tasted one, and it was good but elusive. So I had a couple. The chocolate taste is so light and tantalizing, it has a sort of cumulative effect, and after the fifth or sixth almond, I could have happily eaten the entire container. They are not very sweet and would make a perfect nibble to serve with dry sherry, if anyone still does that.  (I do, and you should, it's good).  Anyway, I was making a chicken salad for dinner (chunked up chicken, diced apple, green onion and curry dressing which is mayonnaise duded up with a little curry powder, some honey and lime juice).  I looked at the container of cocoa almonds and thought "what the heck" and flung in a big handful. It was the best chicken salad I've ever made. The barely sweet almonds and the barest "what is that???" hint of cocoa, along with the added crunch were knockouts.  Tonight I'm thinking about crushing them and tossing them on top of a microwave baked sweetpotato.  Unless I eat them all first.  Good stuff.

Let me start off by saying that I love seeds and nuts. I've never been overly picky about which kinds. Peanuts and almonds being the two front runners. I try to get lots of proteins and aminos daily and you can't find a better healthier source.The idea of not increasing the calories or fat yet giving a hint of chocolate sounded cool. I like the taste of natural almonds and found Emerald Cocoa Roasted Almonds to be a bit too much for me. I can always tell a good nut by the "can I stop eating" factor. I found it very easy to get away from these almonds and didn't find myself craving them at all like I do most seeds/nuts.I'd be willing to try another flavor, but for the time being its natural (no salt) for me.

column9: The Subtle and Sophisticated Chocolate Almond
column10: This most unusual dry roasted almond from Emerald is lightly coated with dark cocoa powder, slightly salty and slightly sweet, and utterly delectable. This is a scrumptious crunchy snack that can also be reasoned as being healthy, since it has dietary essentials like protein and fiber, and therefore good for the body, as well as the emotions, that desperately need some chocolate now and then!The container information estimates that a serving is 1 oz. (about ¼ cup), which is actually quite a lot, and it's listed as 150 calories. Chances are though, that you won't stop at 1 oz. with these delicious little morsels in front of you. As a party snack, Cocoa Roast Almonds are a super hit. Although it seems that the cocoa is like a dusting over each nut, they don't leave your hands a terrible mess. Cocoa Roast Almonds make a terrific combo with your favorite beverage as a dessert, and they are also a nifty "on the go" breakfast.  The chocolate nutty aroma is wonderful, and the lightweight container is shaped to fit the palm of your hand. Good job Emerald on this excellent product!

column9: I actually LOVE the tast of these.
column10: Unfortunately, Emerald chose to add two toxic ingredients that my family avoids. I was very disapointed to see acesulfame potassium and sucralose listed in the ingredients.

These nuts have so many artificial ingredients on them, don't buy them!  Buy some plain natural roasted almonds by Diamond.  These use the dangerous acesulfame and sucralose, two dangerous aspartamine like chemical ingredients.  Unfortunately I bought these without reading the fine print and once I realized I immediately threw them away.  Same goes for their other flavors.  Do yourself a healthy favor and buy natural nuts.

column9: decent taste, crap ingredients mixed with nuts
column10: These nuts taste alright. My main problem with it is that label makes no mention that is uses sucralose (aka Splenda) and modified food starch (aka MSG). These junk ingredients do not make the nuts taste awesome, so it's not worth it putting this garbage into your body. I guess Emerald doesn't realize that the whole point of buying nuts instead of junk food is so that people have a healthier diet.This is the only brand of nuts that has this garbage, all the other brands I've seen have more natural ingredients. Stay away from Emerald brand.

This is a great alternative for low carb dieters with a sweet tooth.  I also recommend Blue Diamond Almonds Cinnamon Brown Sugar, 8-Ounce Jars (Pack of 6)Dream Whip Whipped Topping Mix, 5.2-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6)Swiss Miss Hot Cocoa Mix, Milk Chocolate, No Sugar Added, 60-Count Envelopes (Pack of 2)

There are only 6g of carbs per serving. Only 1 gram of sugar per serving, vs 4g in a similar brand.(Good Fat): 3g polyunsaturated, and 8g monounsaturated+ 1g saturated fatThe reason these almonds are awesome, is because the chocolate is real, and it tastes sugary enough to feel like you are really eating something delicious, while having a very very low sugar content. Also according to an article I will cite below about the health benefits of almonds, "Almond's Healthy Fats May Help You Lose Weight."I didn't even suspect that they used sucralose until someone pointed it out to me. You can't taste it.There is something about these almonds that never quite satisfy your sugar craving, but you will eventually get full from the sheer number of almonds you will eat, and can snack guilt-free.Because these almonds have low sugar content, they taste like a chocolate snack, while actually providing you with many health benefits, including weight loss, and you can't get enough.Health benefits:[...]

column9: so so...for me, raw almonds are better.
column10: I was waiting with higer expectations to this product, just before yesterday when it was delievered.I expected the taste would be sweet and rich-cocoa since they are saying it is cocoa roasting almonds, but it's just slightly rosted with cocoa. once I taste it, I was pretty disappointed.it's just not only real almonds's taste, but also not strong cocoa's taste. also, they are very dry. that's why it's easy to be cracked.anyway, if I knew it's just weak taste of cocoa, i would just bought the raw ones for rich and fresh taste.

column9: A good idea, but too bitter for my taste
column10: The nuts come in a handy package, and they smell very good. However, the taste is dry and bitter, not the kind of "cocoa" flavor you might expect if you're a fan of most dark chocolate products. Because I didn't enjoy the taste, I couldn't fill up on this snack, so I invariably munched on something else afterwards ... defeating the purpose of this snack.
This product gives you most of the benefits of the real thing, while keeping the sin factor low. Excellent.

People seem to be nitpicking about these nuts.  They're terrific!  They don't have an overwhelming chocolate flavor because they're just lightly dusted with cocoa powder (which isn't messy at all in my experience).  The nuts have a good, roasted almond taste.  The container is easy to handle.For those who like to snack healthy, these are perfect.  A small handful gives me a nice decadent feeling, and satisfies the urge to munch.What more can you ask for?

column9: Emerald Cocoa Roast Almonds disappear from kitchen !!
column10: I'm not a person who eats nuts by the handful, but these were good for a quick snack.  Nuts are a good source of protein and Vitamin E, but these were a little too calorie laden for me to eat a lot of.  They tasted good and the cocoa made a nice addition to the taste of the almonds.  I felt they would have been good crushed on top of ice cream or into a brownie mix.  Unfortunately, they are ALL GONE. My husband and son are extremely busy and need energy on the run; good snack items are eaten up very quickly.  We received our Emerald Cocoa Roast Almonds on Thursday and the container was empty last night.  Sigh.

I have to admit that at first taste I wasn't impressed with these nuts.  I'm pretty sure you can get the same taste if you just lick an almond and dip it in chocolate coco mix.  Plus I'm not a big fan of dark chocolate so that didn't help.  But after having a few, I couldn't stop.  Finally, my wife had to take them away, insisting that she would be using them in some future culinary masterpiece.Conclusion: Almonds are good.I think even if you washed off the chocolate these things would be addictive. And that's probably not a bad thing since as far as I know nuts are good for ya.

These Cocoa Roast Almonds are a great blend of chocolate and almonds.  Although I usually prefer milk chocolate rather than dark the dark chocolate covering of these dry roasted almonds compliment each other beautifully.  A handful of these staves off my late afternoon carving for a little something with only 150 calories and the health benefits of almonds.  I also discovered that they go well with an after dinner brandy.  These are definitely something that needs a permanent spot in the pantry.

These Cocoa Roast almonds are delicious.  They are not too sweet - they seem to be dusted with unsweetened cocoa, which I really like.  They are don't appear to be salted, either.I've used them as a snack and also in a recipe - they were very good in both.  Great texture and taste.The container is a generous size and easy to reseal.

I love both almonds and chocolate and they make a great snack together but often can be quite the mess.  Emerald's Cocoa Roasted Almonds (Dark Chocolate) are an excellent solution to this one drawback.  The chocoalte does not make your hands a mess and you stil get the great taste.One warning perhaps is that this resembles cocoa powder than the form of chocolate one normally gets in a candy bar or in chocolate coated nuts.  It has less of the sweetness than that and more of a bite.  Perhaps an acquired taste, it is none the less excellent and a real treat.

I was quite looking forward to these almonds.  They taste good - with the slight taste of cocoa.  I knew they were better for me as they have much less sugar than chocolate covered - so the intellectual me was highly satisfied; but the chocolate me wanted more.  It's like the devil and angel sitting on your shoulder arguing!  So if you are looking for just a small taste of cocoa and a healthful snack, go ahead and get these - they are great!  But if you are looking to indulge yourself, go for some other chocolate covered treat!

What an interesting combination.  I love almonds and I like chocolate....but the usual "chocolate covered almonds" are always a bit too sweet for my taste.  (Plus, they're not the healthiest thing in the world).These Cocoa Roast Almonds were surprisingly different.  The almonds are great (and no one does them better than Emerald), but instead of being "covered" in milk chocolate......these are "dusted" in a dark chocolate. The result is that they're just right:  not too sweet and the chocolate doesn't overpower the almond.The only reason I gave these 4 stars instead of 5 is the addition of sucralose in the product.  I'm not sure what the best solution would have been for a sweetener but I don't generally choose to use sucralose.  Other than that, it's a perfect snack!

column9: Interesting Take on Chocolate and Nuts
column10: Emerald's Cocoa Roasted Almonds (Dark Chocolate flavor) offer an interesting take on the age-old combination of chocolate and nuts. Instead of being coated in a "skin" of chocolate, the nuts are roasted in what appears to be cocoa powder; the result is a mixed bag.Although there's a definite hint of chocolate flavor, it's not very strong, and if you're looking for a chocolate-y treat, you'll probably be disappointed. However, if what you want are almonds with a twist, then you'll likely be delighted with Emerald's latest  product.

Snack with a subtle chocolate taste, this is going to satisfy only those with a mild chocoholic habit. Still, Emerald's quality nut product shines through. Not the same as eating candy, but you may be able to pass these off as a healthy snack to any concerned parties.

column9: Imagine snacking on almond-flavored Cocoa Puffs and you're just about there
column10: I had such a curiosity about these Cocoa Roast Almonds that when they showed up, I took them into the office and asked coworkers to sample them and tell me what their impressions were. One coworker -- I'm call her H -- described the snack as tasting like "almond-flavored Cocoa Puffs." Another coworker -- let's call him J -- said they took him back to his childhood by reminding him of Ovaltine without the milk. Most of my taste-testers concurred with H's description when they heard it.I have been finding these nuts to be a good afternoon snack. They're vaguely chocolately, but not in an overly rich way and not so much so as to make me feel like I'm indulging.If you avoid artificial sweeteners, take note: Sucralose is an ingredient.  Otherwise the ingredients are pretty natural: Dutch-processed cocoa, almonds, salt.So in short: if you like the flavor of Cocoa Puffs, and you think almond flavoring would improve them, and you like quasi-healthy snacking, and you don't mind artificial sweetener, these will probably be a favorite for you. Otherwise, plain roasted almonds may be a better alternative.

I prefer roasted almonds with salt, but this product comes with a coat of dark chocolate. Dark chocolates are not as tasty as milk chocolates, but health conscious consumers could derive some benefit. Published scientific reports suggest dark chocolate has the ability to lower high blood pressure, and it is also known to be a potent antioxidant. High vitamin E content, low trans fat and low sodium are additional factors for health savvy consumers. The product comes in a nice canister and the twist-on lid locks in the freshness.1. Diamond Whole Almonds, 6-Ounce Bags (Pack of 4)2. Jordan Almonds White3. Marcona Almonds SAUTEED IN OIL - 1 kilo4. Marcona Almonds5. Spanish Marcona Almonds - Fried and Salted6. Sunridge Farms Organic Raw Supreme Almonds, 7-Ounce Bags (Pack of 6)7. Planters NUT-rition Almonds, Lightly Salted, 10.25-Ounce Cans (Pack of 3)

column9: Taste One And You Won't Stop
column10: While I normally review books, today I'm reviewing a snack. Emerald Cocoa Roast Almonds. This is one fantastic snack. Lightly roasted, crisp, crunchy almonds, with a thin velvety coating of dark chocolate flavored cocoa powder. Delicious!These almonds come in a neat plastic screw-top container in case you want to save some for later, but you'll find it hard to do so. Taste one and you can't stop.A great snack to keep near you while you read that book you can't put down. I recommend this one highly. Reviewed by Louis N. Gruber.

I was so looking forward to these chocolate almonds after enjoying the other Emerald roasted nuts, but the too subtle chocolate flavor is overpowered by the taste of the artificial sweetener. And I looked at the ingredients and it uses sucralose. Why didn't they label this as a sugar-free version and also market a real sugar option? I can't stand any artificial sweeteners. I won't buy it again.

Recent research indicates almonds lower blood cholesterol levels, regulate blood pressure, and help prevent osteoporosis.  The fats in almonds are mostly good fats--90% unsaturated. Plus, almonds are decent sources of daily nutrients including, protein, fiber and vitamin E. (Source:  Natural News)Okay, I like almonds--but I love them dipped in chocolate.  That adds a LOT of extra sugar, fat, etc.Emerald has solved that problem with cocoa roasted almonds.  A 1 ounce serving of these almonds is 150 calories, which is the same as regular roasted almonds!  They have zero cholesterols, 3 grams of fiber, and only 1 gram of sugar.They're not 'sweet sweet'.  If you like dark chocolate bars with 70% or better cacao (the good stuff) you are going to LOVE these nuts.The cup-size container's a great size to pack in your car.  It'll fit in a cup holder--or you can sneak it in the movie theatre and have almonds instead of a fat- or sugar-laden snack.Rebecca Kyle, May 2008

column4: Mary Jo Sminkey "15 years of Amazon Reviews!"
column9: Love the hint of chocolate, and without the carbs
column10: If you are looking for normal chocolate-covered nuts, this is not the snack to choose. However, if you love almonds and the health benefits they have, but are on a low-carb diet, you might want to give these a try. I love chocolate, but try to stick with high-protein, low-carb snacks and I really enjoyed these cocoa roast almonds. They have just a hint of chocolate, so it's not going to satisfy a serious chocolate craving, but I really enjoyed it over typical roasted almonds, and was happy to have some chocolate flavor without having to feel guilty about the carbs that usually come with it. The powdery covering does not come off much on your fingers and while it does use Splenda, I could not detect it at all while eating them. I don't eat a lot at one sitting, so a single container lasts me a couple weeks. I definitely will be purchasing these again!

column9: Pure cocoa taste with crunchy almonds inside
column10: It was almost a 'love at first bite' - the perfectly roasted almond with a nice thin layer of pure flavorful cocoa on the top.You can smell the cocoa as soon as you open the canister - making you want to take a bite.You may or may not like the taste of this cocoa roasted almonds depending on your likingness for cocoa.  We are so much used to the taste of chocolate (which is actually cocoa + many other ingredients like milk ...) - that you might have never really tasted really cocoa.Tasting this item it like tasting and enjoying flavorful pure raw cocoa with crunchy almonds in the center.  Get yourself a box and see for yourself what real cocoa + almonds is !Where this product loses a star is in its packaging - the external sleeve is kind of comes in one piece, so if you try to remove the lid, the external sleeve kind of tends to come off fully - so careful when you are removing the external sleeve for the canister.

These cocoa covered almonds are great tasting and make for a healthy snack choice. They have a great chocolate flavor to help with those chocolate cravings we all seem to have. My 12 year old daughter also thinks that they taste great.In a time when it seems that almost most everyone is trying to eat healthier these almonds are a great choice without losing any flavor or adding any additional calories.

column9: Cocoa and almonds, a winning combination
column10: I was surprised at how tasty these are. The almonds are dusted with cocoa powder which provides more chocolate flavor than you would think. Since almonds and cocoa have been proven to be beneficial foods, this makes this snack a treat that you shouldn't be guilty about.

column9: I like my nuts I can not lie
column10: I have always liked chocolate covered almonds. It's just something aout the combination that is really enjoyable. So, when I got a chance to try these I jumped all over it right away.First off, the container is much bigger than I thought. There are a lot of nuts in one package. Secondly, unlike most chocolate covered nuts, these nuts are baked with the chocolate (not dipped). This dramatically cuts down on the mess.Flavor is very good. Normally I am not a very big fan of dark chocolate it always leaves an odd aftertaste in my mouth. Here, that wasn't the case. It was a perfect mix between tastingt he chocolate and tasting the nut and didn't  leave much (if any) of an after taste.Emerald nuts has always had high quality standards and this product is not any different. I enjoyed my can and will certainly be buying more in the future.
These are horrible. I didn't realize they contained artificial sweeteners. They taste like chemical covered almonds. Blech, blech, blech. I'll stick with the plain almonds, sans chemicals thank you.

column9: Very Bad After Taste from Artifical Sweetener
column10: I have a problem with the after taste of all artifical sweeteners.  Sadly, my wife selected the Emerald Cocoa Roast Almonds without looking at the ingredients.  And then I forgot to look at the ingredients when I opened the jar and started eating them. My taste buds were unable to taste food correctly for about 3 weeks. Never again.

This product points to the trouble with modern food-processing: overkill. Do we need fake sugar? Or do we just need to consume (a lot) less of the real thing? I won't wax poetic on that point, except to say that these almonds are gross. They are artificially sweetened, the "cocoa" (it's hard to believe, after tasting these, that it's real) is repulsive and they have an aftertaste---like death. Really, hyperbole aside, these are disgusting.
Not only does it have bad ingredients like artificial flavor and artificial sweeteners, but it tastes HORRIBLE. There is no redeeming value in this product at all. It's going in the trash.

column9: an unforgettable eating experience -- maybe someday I'll be able
column10: My spouse bought these and put them in the pantry.  In cocoa-inspired weakness, I opened the canister, seeking roasted almonds, cocoa, and happiness.  Over the dominant almond and cocoa, it became apparent to me that there was "Something Else" in the can.  No "artificially sweetened" warning.  No "Contains splenda!" flag.  Irresponsible, in my opinion.  I detest the aftertaste of splenda, not mentioned alongside "Emerald Roast Almonds Dark Chocolate flavor" until you read the itty-bitty ingredients text.  Strong black coffee and a slowly nursed-along glass of porter ale over the next few hours finally washed my mouth clean enough to take my mind off of the experience.  When I see an Emerald nut package, it still reminds me of that nasty surprise.The canister went into the trash and I complained to Emerald.  They haven't acknowledged my complaint, and they continue to market artificially sweetened nuts without clearly labeling them as such.  Splenda producers appear to be intent on avoiding the "artificial" label, but that is clearly a misrepresentation on their part.  I now check ingredient lists very carefully.  I don't want to repeat that experience.

My coworker brought these into the office today and placed some in a bowl on my desk. I didn't see the container so I couldn't check the ingredients but knew as soon as I ate one that they had splenda on them. I have nothing against splenda in reasonable amounts (I use it in my lattes) but these taste like splenda covered almonds. These will go into the garbage.

column9: it never arrived and the tracking shows in SA for 5 days now
column10: I bought this 2 weeks ago and it never arrived. the tracking says it's in SA since 5 days ago and I haven't seen the thing show up

column9: TERRIBLE! Taste like cocoa puffs breakfast cereal. BAD!
