I don't even have anything to comare Ezekiel to because nothing else I know of is flourless in terms of bread or cereal.  Great products!  Of course raisin is the best tasting of the cereals in my opinion but the others are fine too.  They are a bit pricy, but you really do get what you pay for.You know why many big name cereals (or any product for that matter) costs less?1. lower quality ingredients2. they add nutritionally USELESS things like trans fat (if you see the word 'hydrogenated' in the ingredients, there are trans fats present.  Yes, even if the label says 0g trans fat because that actually means <0.5g), high fuctose corn syrup, etc. etc. to extend shelf life of the product.In other words, many companies put ingredients in their products that have negative nutritional value so they can make more money by having less products reach their date of expiration.  IMO this should be illegal and until it is, I urge people to make the choice boycott any company that does this...  and instead support real companies that understand the connection between the earth and all living things.plantin seed, just plantin seeds  (lol bill hicks)
I was introduced to this while staying with family last week. Filling and feels good for my body. Wholesome. Nutritious. Just wish I could find it at a cheaper price!

A Crunchy cereal that has  high nutrition content without negatives.Very satisfying. Haven't found a  better cereal to start the day.I eat it every morning and never get tired of it. I add cappuccino  soymilk, a little stevia and a little extra cinnamon.

This is the only Ezekiel 4:9 product I've tasted, but I personally like it.  My first experience with it reminded me of Grape-Nuts - except much more crunchy.  Took a bit to get used to that, but then I was hooked.  I'm not especially fond of hot cereal, so I've never tried it this way, but I bet it would be good if you do like your cereal warmed - or if you find it too crunchy to eat cold.  People with false teeth or chewing difficulties might want to either eat this warm or let it soak awhile.I noticed that many reviewers say they eat this with soy milk.  I recently learned that studies have shown that soy is not healthy for you, particularly the processed forms such as soy milk and soy powder.  Please do your research.  For myself, I've decided I'm actually better off with cow's milk than with soy milk. Here's just one of the many articles on the subject: [...]Back to the subject ... I really do not taste much cinnamon in this cereal, so if you're not crazy about cinnamon, rest assured this cereal will not be overpowering.  It only has 1 gram of fat per 1/2 cup serving and contains 7 grams of protein and 5 grams of fiber.  I find it a great alternative to eggs if you like to start your day with a good source of protein.Now I think I will try the almond variety ... and will post a review after I've tasted it.

After a bout with cancer, I changed my diet to avoid sugar and white flour.  I trust Ezekiel products for this reason.  I now blend the Ezekiel cinnamon raisin cereal with Bob's Red Mill muesli, both of which we order from Amazon.  Then I top it every morning with blueberries.  I look forward to breakfast.

column9: Love the cereal, love the Amazon.com price
column10: This cereal is normally about $7 in the health food stores where I live. I keep buying it because the cereal is worth it. So, when I found it on Amazon with such a great price, I bought the 6 box deal and have been stocked up for a few months now and reduced my cost for groceries. Thanks Amazon.

column9: goodness and sweetness without necessary extras
column10: I have been using this product for about a year now.  It tastes good and the cinnamon and raisins add just the right sweetness, without added sugar.  The price on Amazon makes it more affordable, and since it is organic, the amount of pesticides would be less, making it more healthy for you.  Definitely a winner!
For a healthy cereal that contains no sugar, this is fantastic! Cinnamon and hard raisins are all the elements that the kid in me enjoys when eating these healthy grains.

column9: A great way to start the day..
column10: I have tried the almond and cinnamon raisin and my favorite is the cinnamon raisin.  Love how this cereal supresses my appetite.  Hard to find a really healthy cereal that tastes good but this defiantly does taste great!  I paid $7.00 plus tax at my local health food store for the cinnamon raisin.  I plan to buy this product on amazon.. sooo much cheaper... $2 a box cheaper for me.  Such a great value on Amazon.

I love this cereal!  It is healthy, filling, and tastes great.  All natural ingredients without any added sugar.  The raisins are great, and I don't find them to be too hard as some others have complained of.  I also bought the original kind and I add my own raisins and slivered almonds to it.  Great buy on Amazon as the price is a bit higher in the grocery store.
Weather you are into weightlifting or being fit or just staying healthy, i highly recommend this product!
A small bowl fills me up in the morning, keeps my system working and regular.

column9: Ezekiel Cereals - the best and healthiest!
column10: We try to eat organically whenever possible and have been fans of Ezekiel cereals for a long time.  Only a few stores on our Hawaiian island stock it and they regularly run out.  Ordering them in bulk from Amazon is perfect for us.  My husband is a real raisin fan and on busy mornings appreciates the convenience of having them already in his cereal.  The cinnamon is a bonus, too!

column9: Ezekiel 4:9 Cereal Organic Sprouted Grain, Cinnamon Raisin
column10: This is my husband's favorite cereal, and we get the best price and delivery from Amazon. We were surprised with the latest delivery. The big box was marked Cinnamon Raisin, however, the content was Golden Flax. I was ready to send it back, but my husband said he'd try it. He liked it! He added cinnamon and raisins and has it for breakfast every day.

column9: Didn't think I'd like it but now I'm hooked
column10: My nutritionist put me on on a low carb, no added sugar diet, and this brand was one that was recommended for cereals. When I saw it in the bowl, I worried. The grains are small and the almond milk I added seemed to vanish into the dense cereal quicksand. Yes, it has taken a little to get used to the texture, but I've really grown to enjoy the taste. It is rich, not cardboard- or grass-like, as can happen with so many simple, stripped down cereals. The raisins add just a touch of sweetness; I don't miss the added sugar I would get in a granola or similar cereal. And the nutrition content is excellent compared to many natural cereals.

I was skeptical when I ordered because of other reviews, but I have been so satisfied with other Ezekiel products and I really needed a cereal that was healthy and flourless so I gave it a go. Well, I really like this cereal and do not have any issues with it being to hard to chew like some said, and I just had two crowns put in and still have one temp and no problem. It tastes alot like grape nuts. I will buy again.

I enjoy sprinkling Ezekiel 4:9 Organic Sprouted Grain Cereal on my Spoon Size Shredded Wheat and enjoying it with some fresh fruit and Activia yogurt. We have tried two of their four flavors. It is similar to Grape Nuts, but not as hard on the teeth. We always order more in plenty of time to assure that we never run out.

Ezekiel cereal is crunchy, tasty and fills you up and keeps you satisfied, unlike the light weight cereals on most store shelves. It's great! Try it with Soy milk and your favorite fruit for an even healthier breakfast.

Tastes dry and dense with milk, so I experimented and found that if you eat it in a bowl with some honey (however amount depending on your preference), it's delicious!- the healthiest "granola" ever!!makes for an absolutely wholesome, DELICIOUS snack.I think the one with almonds is best!

I have very healthy 45 year old teeth and one bowl of this cereal was enough to break a large chuck off one of my teeth.  Be careful as I never expected to find gravel hard chunks in my bowl of breakfast cereal.  I am just sickened by it since I do take such pride in my teeth and to make matters worst its a front tooth!  If you don't like to chew gravel for breakfast then you likely won't enjoy this cereal.  Yeah it taste pretty good and may be healthy for you but not worth breaking your teeth over.  We won't even talk about denist bills.  Notice I am not the only review about broken teeth from this cereal.  The chunk broke off my tooth is at least the size of a average size pea so not just a tiny little salt grain.  If you like your teeth stay away from this cereal!  Ezekiel Almond Cereal
I give this cereal plus fruit juice such as mango a short warming--just to soften the cereal--and have a quick, warm, filling breakfast.

column9: best flavor! And healthiest cereals ever.
column10: It is sprouted which means more protein, etc.  Sprouting your food (not all works) is beneficial. I stopped ordering this because I eat too much of it! Cannot control myself. I will try to order it again and limit myself. Such a great tasting cereal and makes me feel great. I do get gas problem... but that's a good thing as it eliminate waste or what ever. I know it can be gross, but I know when is a good time to do that. It is all about common sense!

column9: Doesn't taste as good as other flavors...( EDITED )
column10: I edit this comment and gave it a 5/5 and erased my comment. This cereal is really good... at first, I didn't like the taste at all, but then I loved it.6 boxes lasted me 4 days... I ate too much.. ha ha.. I plan not to do that when the ezekiel's flax seed cereals arrive. I will try not to eat a lot. :)

column9: Tasteless grit that almost broke a tooth
column10: I eat a lot of healthy food and am willing to try new ones.  So recently I tried this cereal.  The only plus I can report is that it had a lot of raisins in it.  Which is a good thing because, without the raisins it would have been completely tasteless.  But the worst thing about it is that it contains some very hard bits that almost broke a tooth.That was my experience the first time, eating it cold with milk.  I noticed that the box suggested it could also be eaten warm...I figured that heating it with milk might soften the hard bits, so I decided to try it (I was also trying desperately to avoid throwing away the $5.49 investment).  My theory was wrong.  The hard bits are un-softenable.  I dumped the rest of the box of cereal...and $5.49 + tax...in the compost bin.

I was introduced to this bread while giving out food to families struggling with addictions in Lake Huges California in the 80's. There was a Seventh Day Adventist commune there at the time and they would give me huge boxes of the bread to pass out.  I became known as the "bread lady" and I was only 24.This product, I believe has saved my life for the last 30 years.  Most of my siblings and all of my parents had cancer and passed on because of the cancer. Not one of them ate this bread. I wish we had known about this bread growing up, thier lives could have been spared. I sometimes eat up to five pieces a day with no weight gain. I eat the slices raw and untoasted, but made into toast or french toast it is delicious too.The price has gone up, but I got a bunch of loafs on sale for $3.99 each at "Down to Earth", in Kapolei Hawaii.If you write the company they will send you coupons.If you want to be regular, energetic, and disease free eat this bread and none other.Deb

I recently discovered Ezekiel cereals, and I bought two boxes: Cinnamon Raisin and Almond. Almond is awesome! I love it with almond milk, agave, and blueberries. It's filling and fabulous!Cinnamon Raisin would be good if it wasn't loaded with rock-hard tiny raisins. They are terrible! They have no taste, and are somewhat difficult to chew.I will never get Cinnamon Raisin again, but I look forward to trying Golden Flax and Original, and picking up another box of Almond.
I broke a tooth eating the cereal.  It's not just a feeling that it could happen. I'm not happy right now.

I bought this based on the great reviews. I appreciate that it's super healthy, but it tastes very bland and the texture is rock hard (think grape nuts w/ hard raisins). I feel like I'm going to lose my fillings w/ every bite. I tried soaking it in milk for a few minutes but to no avail. The box suggests serving it either cold or hot after cooking it over the stove. I can see why it should be cooked soft.I really wanted to like this cereal but I don't. My husband hates it too. We're wondering how we're ever going to finish all 6 boxes (I'm mixing it w/ other cereals for now).

column9: Make your own & save some money
column10: I bought a box of this recently.  Even though it sounded pretty "healthy", I figured, how bad can it be.Well, I just had my first serving, and decided that I would share a recipe that very closely approximates the taste and texture of this cereal.  Here it is:4 cups course saw dust1 cup raisins2 Tablespoons sugar1 Teaspoon ground cinnamonBlend all ingredients, serve with cold milk.How on earth can anyone give this stuff more than one star?  The serving size listed on the box is 1/2 cup. First of all, who eats 1/2 cup of cereal?  I doubled up on the serving, and poured a full cup in the bowl... added some 2% organic milk..... yummmm!  Wrong!  Now I know why the serving size is specified at 1/2 cup..... anybody that can gag down more than a half cup of this stuff in one sitting, is a better man than I am. Seriously.... what possible reason could anyone have for eating this stuff?  I tried my best to choke down this stuff, but the more I ate, the worse the experience became.  About a third of the way through, I cried uncle and dumped the remaining meal in the trash.There may be a use for this cereal, but eating it, is not a viable option.  I don't even think birds or small rodents would want to eat it.  I may mix it with some water, and fill some of the cracks in my driveway with it.

and they aren't softening in the milk. you will need strong healthy teeth to chomp on them.  the cereal itself sops up a lot of milk & it expands quite a bit (so don't pour too big a bowl like i did. now i'm trying to stuff it all down). There is the occasional really hard nugget of grain mixed in. when i come across one it tends to jam into my cavity & is a little uncomfortable.  but for the most part the cereal is soft & easily chewed just like mashed up wheaties.  Honestly this tasted strange to me on the first couple bites but as i sit here enjoying my first bowl i'm getting used to it.  before i bit in i thought i detected a weird smell.  i think it's just the way one or more of the grains smells & i wasn't familiar with the scent of that particular grain. or maybe cause they are sprouted they smell different. OR perhaps the addition of cinnamon did it. if so it's the only time i smelled something w/cinnamon that didn't smell better w/the cinnamon added.  in summary i think this is a pretty good cereal for those into super healthy foods.  The average person looking to add some whole grains could do a lot better in the taste & texture departments. If you are interested in sprouted grains specifically then i can't say for sure as this is the only sprouted grain cereal i've ever had.  I think i may try another box but next time i'll get the one with almond slivers. perhaps those flavors will be more complementary. and i'll bet the almonds are softer than the raisins.......i'll be sure to review it once i try it!

column10: Once upon a time Delouis Fils made  a delicious and authentic dijon mustard vinaigrette.  I discovered its merits when I purchased the product at Whole Foods. It is glutenous and slightly sweet and--to make a long story short--I threw both bottles out.

She will sprint across the house when I get home, jump on the bed and wait for her treats to be delivered. We were worried she was overweight but the vet says she's in great health and a little "fluff" is to be expected on a house cat.

Since using Whiskas we have not had one cat purge a hairball and I am grateful, truly. I would love it if they would come in bulk, on our first shipment, none of the zip locks on the bags worked.
