The peanuts are so small and in such small pieces (more like granules) that I don't consider them anywhere near enough to consider any health benefits from the nuts.The taste itself is good, and it's a bit softer of a crunch than most cereals, but outside of that it's just too many carbohydrates to be on the breakfast table.  Kellog's could really improve this cereal by getting rid of some of the added sweetners and switch to a whole grain recipe.  Until then, if you like sweet cereals with little health benefits then this is for you -- but otherwise, stick with Honey Nut Cheerios.

Breakfast cereal manufacturers try to make their products sound healthy and wholesome, but most are made almost entirely from flour and sugar with added vitamins (and, these days, a little fiber).  And that pretty much sums up Kellogg's Crunchy Nut.  Corn meal, sugar, corn bran (sounds like a good idea, but it's not), peanuts, honey, molasses, salt, and oat flour make up the main ingredients (note the three different forms of sugar).A 3/4 cup serving has 100 calories, 1g fat, 23g carbs (10 of which are sugar), and only 2g each of fiber and protein.  With numbers like that, I consider this to be candy or pastry.  It can be regarded as a "breakfast" item only in the way that a donut can.Having said that, Crunchy Nut does taste great and has a good crunch (which holds up in milk).  When you first open the bag, you'll smell the roasted peanuts (though they are only very scantly sprinkled over the pieces).  I like sweet things, but this is actually a bit *too* sweet for my taste.  My 10-year-old loved it.In summary, this is a (sadly) typical kid's breakfast cereal.  If this were sold as candy, I'd give it four stars.  But I expect a little bit more nutrition from an item that's sold in the breakfast aisle.

column9: Remember Nut & Honey Crunch O's? They're Back... Almost.
column10: I assumed that this would be the Kelloggs version of Honey Nut Cheerios, but actually it isn't.  Instead it tastes like Kelloggs famous cereal from the late 80's - Nut & Honey Crunch.  I hadn't eaten that cereal in forever, but the smell and taste instantly brought back the memories.  I actually remembered that in the early 90's they came out with a Nut & Honey Crunch O's cereal, which wasn't as popular.  To me if you had ever tried that cereal - then Nut & Honey Crunch O's and the new Crunchy Nut cereal would seem very, very similar.  You could almost say that Kelloggs upped the nut flavoring (since the cereal smells slightly more like peanut butter than I expected), but probably pulled out a stock recipe of the original Nut & Honey Crunch flavoring.  This is probably an attempt by Kelloggs to introduce a previous hit to a new generation.  For me, I wasn't disappointed.  The cereal is really tasty, and not too sweet.  But if I hadn't just tried the cereal on a whim, I probably would have never realized the similarity to a childhood favorite.  Remember this popular commercial tagline - "Whatcha eating?" - "Nut'n honey." I highly recommend Gen X and Baby Boomers that liked Nut & Honey Crunch cereal to try Crunchy Nut.

I was expecting Honey Nut Cheerios.  But it was different.  These Crunchy Nuts were much crispier.  I checked the ingredients and the first ingredient was corn, which would explain the Kix sort of crunch.  They stayed crunchy until the last bite, perhaps because of the sugar coating... second ingredient is sugar, which is why I can't give it 5 stars even though it tastes great.  The "nut" in these is just peanut, no tree nuts, and they are very peanutty with chunks of peanut on every O.  I loved the flavor.  My son said it was maybe the best cereal he had ever tasted.  Ten grams of sugar per serving and only two grams of protein, so it's not the healthiest cereal on the market, but it does taste great.

column9: Finally made it to the States!
column10: I tried Crunchy Nut about a year ago when I was visiting the UK. It was absolutely one of the best cereals I had ever had. When I saw it on Amazon, I had to try it to see if it was as good as it remembered. It is!The brand I tried when I was in the UK was more like corn flakes and this one is more like cheerios. I was pleasantly surprised that this was not as sweet as I remember from the flakes brand. I liked the crunch this cereal had and it never got soggy in the six or so minutes it took me to eat a bowl.At 100 calories for 3/4 of a cup, it would seem this cereal delivers taste as well as not hiking up you calorie intake for the day. Now I am no nutritionist so I would advise looking up all its ingredients for things that may not agree with everyone.All in all, I enjoyed this cereal and would not hesitate to get myself another box.

column9: It won't work for my eating habits but it is good
column10: This cereal is NOT for people who limit carbs or sugar intake but compared to many other pre-sweetened cereals it's not as bad (e.g., not as much sugar) as competitive products like Froot Loops or Cap'n Crunch.While of course it's designed to be eaten with milk or yogurt it would also make a fun movie munchie right out of the box.I'm a bit more health food conscious than this cereal's nutritional label would allow for in my household's cupboard but and based upon today's Amazon price of $29.95 for the four pack it's a bit overpriced for our household too; Not that we're poor but we are discerning as to what we spend our money on. We got a trial sample so all we had to lose was a little time on our weight loss efforts for a couple of day.I still rate this product 5 stars because I don't think my personal tastes and preferences are what matters. I think this product is great for the market I perceive it to be aimed at.

If you're going to get a sugar cereal it ought to at least taste great, so you're getting some pleasure in exchange for the unhealthiness. But this cereal doesn't taste very good. Can't see any reason to recommend it.

This cereal is sweeter than the name might imply.  But if one reads the ingredients and sees sugar, honey and molasses as number two, five, and six one might guess as much.  The molasses gives it a different flavor than the other "honey nut" type cereals I have tasted.  While I didn't care too much for it, others might - tastes vary widely between different people.

column9: Won't be at the Top of the Shopping List
column10: Crunchy Nut Roasted Nut and HoneyI shared this with my kids, as they are the cereal connoisseurs of the family. The results were split: two for buying again and two for trying something else.The pro to this cereal is that is stays crunchy in milk until you finish even if you leave it for a minute. The taste is primarily of sweetness/honey flavor. We really didn't taste much of the nutty flavor. This cereal reminded us of the sugariness waffle crisp without the syrup flavor.For myself, I just didn't care for the flavor or texture. There really wasn't a flavor other than the sweetness and by the end of the bowl I had to force the last spoonful in. It was kind of blah.If the kids really want to eat this I would buy it for them but I don't think it will be on the top of the shopping list.

What a delicious breakfast cereal! These aren't dry oatey O's covered in honey and nut like I had anticipated they would be, but rather they're a crunchy, dark-amber, honey-corn O, covered in little nut particles.Crunchy Nut Roasted Nut and Honey cereal stays crispy [enough] in milk. I turned this box into two after work bowls one night, and then two breakfast bowls the next morning. So they're good enough to be considered a multi-bowl-per-sitting cereal.As far as the name goes, "Crunchy Nut" sounds more like a variety of something than a proper cereal name, so maybe they'll change that down the line, but I like them, I'm sure kids will like them and if you're in the mood for a crisp, tasty, moderately sweet cold cereal then I think you will like them too.

Kellogg's new "Crunchy Nut" cereal isn't particularly innovative from a flavor/texture perspective, but it is pretty tasty.  It's flavor is like a hybrid of Kix and Honey Smacks with the texture of Oh!s.  If you like any (or better yet, all) of these cereals, "Crunchy Nut" will probably be a hit at your breakfast table.Don't be caught up in the "Nuts in Every Bite!" hype, though.  You'll barely taste 'em, and they certainly don't raise the nutritional value.  (See below.)  For reference nutritionally speaking, this product very similar to Froot Loops.In short, this cereal is crunchy, not particularly nutty, with a nice mild honey flavor.  It's unlikely you'll be able to use this as a gateway cereal for your kids to start eating muesli regularly.  ;-)NUTRITIONAL INFO:Serving size:  3/4 CupCalories: 100Total Fat:  1gCholesterol: 0mgSodium: 125mgPotassium: 25mgTotal Carbs: 23gFiber: 2gSugars: 10gProtein: 2g

column9: Good taste, and of course, bad for you
column10: Like many other reviewers, I'd have to agree that the cereal is very good. It tastes like Cheerios with a sweet, nutty taste. However, it has 10g of sugar per serving...that's quite a bit for cereal. I actually munch on it as a dessert rather than eating it for breakfast. Just like most things that taste good, it's definitely not good for you, but it's a good little treat in moderation.

My first impression of the Crunchy Nut cereal was how sweet the cereal is.  Eating the Crunchy Nut cereal was like eating Fruit Loops or another sweetened cereal.  A look the ingredients revealed that sugar is the second ingredient after yellow corn meal, resulting in the very sweet taste.  The cereal also has a definite aftertaste of nuts which is pleasant.It is my belief that Kellogg's produced the Crunchy Nut cereal to compete against Honey Nut Cheerios and so I will be comparing the two cereals in my review.  I found that the Crunchy Nut O's were bigger than Cheerios and rougher.  The rough O's tended to irritate the roof of my mouth when I ate the cereal.A comparison of the nutrition information of the two cereals suggests that although neither cereal is really healthy due to the high sugar content, Crunchy Nut is actually better for you than Honey Nut Cheerios in terms of the sodium and calories.  However, this does not take into account that Honey Nut Cheerios is made from whole grain oats whereas Crunchy Nut is made from corn meal.  Surprisingly, Crunchy Nut actually has the same dietary fiber as Honey Nut Cheerios.Of the two cereals, I preferred Honey Nut Cheerios due to its slightly less sweet taste and since the Cheerios did not tend to irritate the roof of my mouth.  Overall, Crunchy Nut is not a cereal that I can recommend to people who do not like sweetened cereals or who are looking for a healthy cereal.

This cereal reminds me of Corn Bran.  I don't know if that stuff is still around.  This cereal was okay.  I liked that it wasn't super sweet.  If you like more of the honey taste, then this isn't the cereal.  I would buy this cereal if it was on a good special, but it wasn't my favorite.  The texture was a lot like cheerios, but it didn't taste as sweet as honey nut cheerios.  I compared the ingredients to that of our other cereals.  It wasn't too bad.  Still had the carbs etc.  A lot like the standard box of cereal.

I enjoy cereal and this cereal is like most sugar coated grains of goodness. It's not going to win any points for originality, but it is a tasty little treat. It's like Cheerios with some added sugar and nut fragments sprinkled on top. I've seen this cereal much cheaper at Wal-Mart than the prices on line, so if you're looking to give it a try, buy it there.

This might be one of my new favorite cereals.  I was amazed at how crunchy the cereal stayed, even after being in milk for several minutes.  It was a great sweet taste to it.  I'm guessing by how great it tastes, it can't be extremely healthy, but I like it anyway!

Loved it. The flavor was great, nice nuttiness, just all around really great. My wife has taken to eating it dry as a snack instead of popcorn! Sugar content is a bit high, but we don't plan to eat this every day.

This cereal is like a more grown-up version of Apple Jacks, with a roasted peanut taste instead of apple. The cereal consists of cherio-type rounds that have the same little sprinkles on them as Apple Jacks, only with a peanut taste. These sprinkles give the cereal a good, crunchy texture. The peanut taste is very pronounced and peanut lovers will delight in it. I've tried other peanut cereals and none tasted more peanutty than this. A good quality cereal, and the box came with a coupon for the next box on it - which I was happy to use after enjoying the cereal. Also has the usual offering of vitamins and minerals you would expect from a major brand cereal. Recommended!

Kellogg's Crunchy Nut: Roasted Nut & HoneyMuch better than expected!  I generally don't gravitate towards the 'O' shaped cereals, my favorite cereal is Honey Bunches of Oats.  That being said, when I saw this Nut & Honey cereal, I figured I'd give it a try.  It's tastier than I imagined, it has a stronger honey flavor than most honey-flavored cereals do.  The 'enlarged' picture of the cereal on the box makes it look like there's more nut 'shavings' than there really are, but that being said, there's enough nut there to make a difference and have the cereal taste slightly nutty, which is a good thing in my opinion.  ...I'm not one to eat (or snack on) dry cereal, but this one makes the cut, it's currently sitting next to me on the desk.

column9: Stays crunchy, a little too sweet
column10: This isn't anything really exciting and it's a little sweet for me, but the kids like it.It's relatively healthy and it stays crunchy. I'll continue to buy this for the kids.

When I first got this box I opened it and munched on it as I watched a bit of TV.  Tasted good.  It was crunchy and just sweet enough.  Not syrupy sweet, but just enough for my sweet tooth.I tried it the next morning with milk and it didn't get soggy.  I found it to be sweet but not overly.  Not sure what I would compare it to.  Didn't hit me as peanut butter or anything similar.  Just a nice nutty taste that was a bit sweet.If you like the sweet and nutty taste you will like this.  The big thing is that is doesn't get soggy and turn to mush.Enjoy.

Lots of reviewers have mentioned how this cereal is similar to Honey Nut Cheerios, and I agree, EXCEPT, I think this is much crunchier.I like crunch, and I also like a sweet breakfast cereal, so I was happy with the taste and consistency.Now, if you don't like sweet in the morning, these may be a little much for you. In addition to sugar, they also have honey and molasses.  The sugar CONTENT however is only 10g. I say "only" because there are some cereals out there, which claim fiber and other health benefits, which have more sugar than these. (Example, frosted Mini-Wheats--12g of sugar. And a certain bran with raisin cereal, 23g of sugar!)Much as I liked these, I wouldn't eat them every single day, because I think the sweet factor might be too much (even for me :>) over time. But they're a nice every-few-days choice.One caution: Peanuts. If you're allergic, be aware that these contain peanuts.

Is this the rich man's Peanut Butter Cap'n Crunch? Or the poor man's Honey Nut Cheerios? It tastes like the former, but looks like the latter. My wife and I dug into this one evening and, 24 hours later, have demolished it. It's not very "peanut-y," except for the artificial peanut flavor (despite, strangely, the flecks of peanut glued onto each "o"). If you're looking for sugar and aren't discriminatory in your brand names, it should satisfy your craving. Om nom nom!

column9: I couldn't even finish the box...
column10: I love cereal and eat it for breakfast almost every day. I've tried just about everything in the breakfast aisle, but I've never found anything to rival my two stand-by favorites, plain yellow-box Cheerios and Honey Bunches of Oats. I figured these Kellogg's Crunchy Nut O's were worth a shot, however, as they had both honey and peanuts going for them.Boy, was I disappointed. I thought this cereal was much, much too sweet, and felt that it left a bad corn aftertaste in my mouth. My husband, a huge fan of Honey Nut Cheerios, didn't like this either. After a few bowls, the box sat untouched in my cupboard for months until I finally threw it out. Definitely not for us!

column9: Doesn't get soggy, but also hard on the mouth
column10: Kellogg's Crunchy Nut cereal is akin to granola being married with Cheerios. The flavor is slightly sweet, and the rings are fun to crunch.Pros:* Takes a long time to get soggy in milk. I got distracted by my baby for about 20 minutes and came back to a bowl of cereal that was still crunchy.* Cereal is sweet, but not overly so (i.e. honey nut cheerios are about 2x as sweet)Cons:* The crunchy nutty bits actually left a cut on the inside of my cheek.* If you have dentures, bridges, or false teeth, you want to have them in before you eat this cereal.The flavor is okay - I didn't love this enough to purchase it on my own, but I also wouldn't turn it down if it was my only breakfast option.

Honestly, it wasn't that good. I didn't finish the box before I moved on. The coating separated in liquid. It didn't taste too bad but also did not taste particularly nutritious. I prefer cereals made of whole grains

I like the texture of this cereal, and I'm a big fan of peanuts, but this just seems a little bland to me.  It's not a bad taste, just not really very strong to me, so it's kinda like eating semi-sweet slightly flavored little crunchy pieces of cardboard or something.  If it had a stronger flavor or maybe another flavor in addition to what it has I think I would enjoy it more.

I found this cereal so uninteresting that I almost forgot to review it, because I'd almost forgotten that I'd eaten it. It is not a bad cereal, just not memorable at all. With so many great cereals on the market, I don't see why this one is being offered. Just ignore this cereal and it will likely go away eventually.

column9: Basically a honey nut cheerios rip-off, but good
column10: This cereal is good, if unoriginal.  My four factor review is below:Crunch: 4/5Flavour: 4/5Nutrition: 4/5Value: 4/5

I am not typically fond of very sweet cereals, so that opinion affects this review.  This cereal has a taste somewhat like peanut butter.  It is shaped liked Cheerios, but tastes a bit like Captain Crunch.  However, the cereal is overly sweet on its own and I didn't care for it.  After the initial try, I mixed it half and half with plain Cheerios and liked it quite well.

column9: Very sugary and probably not the most healthful cereal
column10: This is not a cereal I would personally buy, as it's overly sugary for my taste. Also, it's probably not as versatile as some others - added fresh fruit might not go well with this cereal. More importantly, for health, this is certainly not one of the more impressive (look at the ingredient list).

When I first saw this product all I could think of was another of the Honey Nut cereals that we all love.  I was hoping beyond hope that this wouldn't be a dud as some copies are.  Well this is the best Honey Nut Crunch cereal I have had the delight to enjoy.  It's not as sweet as I thought it would be but is just perfect.  It has a nice crunch that stays well with the milk until you are finished.  Yay, no soggy cereal here.  All in all, this is a fantastic cereal with great flavor and healthy to boot that comes at a price that is very affordable especially with the way the economy is making us pay more for less it seems lately.  You won't be disappointed here.

column9: Tasty. Sugary Sweet. Holds up to Milk. Would be Good in Trail Mix.
column10: If you like a sweet, slightly nutty flavored cereal, then you'll like this new Kellogg's Crunchy Nut cereal.Nutrition Facts:Serving Size: 3/4 cupServings Per Box: 11Total Fat: 1g (cereal only)Cholesterol, 0mgSodium: 125mgPotassium: 25mgCarbohydrate: 23g Dietary Fiber: 2g Sugars: 10g Other Carbohydrates: 11gProtein: 2gIngredients: Yellow Corn Meal, Sugar, Corn Bran, Peanuts, Honey, Molasses, Salt, Whole Oat Flour, Caramel Color, Baking Soda, Annatto Extract Color, Ascorbic Acid (Vitamin C), Niacinamide, Redced Iron, Zinc Oxide, Pyridoxine Hydrochloride (Vitamin B6), Riboflavin (Vitamin B2), Thiamin Hydrochloride (Vitamin B1), Vitamin A Palmitate, BHT (preservative), Foic Acid, Vitamin D, Wheat Starch, Vitamin B12.This cereal holds up well in milk and also is tasty right out of the box.  Also would be good in trail mix and a quick cookie bar recipe.

I am not a big fan of peanut butter, but I must admit to liking this cereal.  It is crunchy and quite tasty, with a light roasted peanut taste.  It was quite enjoyable and passed the test of my eight year old with excellence.  She loved it.  My box came with a nice $1.00 off coupon.  I recommend this if you like the taste of roasted peanuts, if not this will not be on your enjoyment list.

column9: Sorry, a little too sweet for my taste
column10: This cereal would be better, in my humble opinion, if it were less sweet.  When I was a kid I liked really sweet cereal but as an adult, I've grown out of it.  Although I enjoyed the crunchiness of it.  And the nutty taste was not bad at all, simply too sweet.  Now, that's just my personal opinion.  If you like sweet cereal, this may suit you fine.

column9: Not very good, Odd tasting, Not popular with my kids
column10: First, if you look at the picture on the front, you see large pieces of nuts attached to a an O. I understand this is enlarged, but the reality is the nuts are much smaller relative to the O; more like a coating that an attached piece. They were largely encapuslated in the sugar coating. There was no distinct flavor or texture of nut and O, just one experience.The O is not like a cheerio. Instead it is a sugary construct, sort of like captain crunch but a little less sweet. The sugar coating either has honey or honey flavor. In any case, the honey makes for an odd taste as there is a floral overtone to the cereal that doesn't belong. I don't get this with "Honey bunches of Oats" or the like, but have experienced in a cereal called "Puffins".I have four kids (5 through 13) and, although they ate mose of the cereal, no one was eager for more and a few didn't finish. I certainly wouldn't buy this again. There are tastier and healthier (at the same time!) alternatives.

The first thing I noticed about this cereal is the unnatural color.  Sort of a rust/orange, approaching a Cheetos color - definitely looks artificial! But then most cereals are.  Shape-wise they look like Cheerios, especially the honey-nut variety with flecks of peanuts.As far as taste goes, these are fine. They have a nice crunch to them, don't get soggy, and they feel light when you eat them.  As other reviewers have commented, they are not overly or syrupy sweet, which is good because you get a nice balance between the sweet part versus the corn and some nuttiness. These are crunchier than Cheerios.The only non-positive thing about this would be the price.  It seems rather pricey to me.

If you want a cereal that has lots of fiber and protein, and will keep you full for hours.... this is not that cereal.If you want a cereal that is just plain delicious, to be eaten for the pure joy of eating it.... this is not that cereal.If you want a cereal that tastes like stale kix rolled in the crumbs of some honey roasted peanuts, and is  satisfying in neither taste nor quality.... then this is the breakfast cereal for you.I think i've made myself clear.
Not a regular cereal eater but I found this to be a tasty treat.  Sweet, nutty, and a little bit salty which is a great combination.The 11 oz box of cereal did not last long at all.

Very tasty. I like Honey-Nut Cheerios, and these are very similar, but a little less sweet and more nutty. Of course those with peanut allergies/sensitivities will need to avoid. I shared them with my wife, who generally doesn't like cereal except Corn Flakes, and she liked it a lot.
Tastes a lot like honey nut cheerioes but not quite as good. stay fairly crunchy after adding milk. Kids liked them too.

I wasn't a huge fan of the taste of Crunchy Nut Roasted Nut and Honey cereal.  The taste is redolent of corn puffs, with a hint of Multi-grain Cheerios.  Too much honey on the front end, with corn notes that are slightly overpowering in the finish.  The bouquet has distinct peanut notes which is unsurprising as peanuts (which actually aren't a nut) are the main nut in the cereal.  Somehow this combines however, into a cereal that is at once both, overly sweet and mealy.I would also add that the price, $30 + $8 shipping comes out to about .88 an ounce.  Compare that to major grocery chains and other cereals, such as Crunchy Nut Roasted O's at .38/oz, or Honey nut cheerios at .28/oz, and its clear that these are horribly overpriced.Also, when it says nuts (and I realize I'm being a stickler), I really expect it to contain treenuts, like almonds, cashews, etc.  Peanuts are a legume, a groundnut, and technically a bean.  Not a nut.

column9: Why would I want to eat peanuts with milk?
column10: As advertised, Crunchy Nut smells and tastes like peanuts -- something I don't find very appetizing when mixed with milk and ingested in the morning. I eat peanuts with beer at bars, not at breakfast. I'm guessing that the honey is supposed to cut the flavor of the peanuts, but it is hardly detectable.People will of course disagree with my thoughts on peanuts in the morning, but let's take a look at the side of the box.To keep the calories per serving at 100 (without milk), Kellogg's has shrunk the serving size to 3/4 of a cup. That means with milk, a bowl of Crunchy Nut is going to be 300 calories or slightly more. So if you go back for a second bowl, that's a pretty high caloric breakfast. Further, the base ingredient is yellow corn meal, which doesn't have much nutritional value.While there are certainly much more unhealthy cereals out there, in this day and age I'd like to see a more healthy, lower caloric cereal.

I liked the crunch and held up well in milk but there was no nutty flavor and felt it was too sweet.To me, this is more of a snack type than a cereal. Even my husband who eats a cereal daily said there's just 'too much in it." I will just finish the box as a snack but probably would pass it in the cereal aisle.

column9: It's Not Honey Nut Cheerios - but it tries to be
column10: Honey Nut Cheerios (HNC) is a good cold cereal if you're concerned about high Cholesterol and want more fiber.  Kellogg's Crunchy Nut (CN) tries to imitate HNC and doesn't quite get there.  But it's not too far off.They're both tasty.  CN is a bit too sweet for my taste (of course, you might prefer it sweeter) but it only has a little more sugar than HNC.  Must be the way the honey is glazed on CN.HNC is made with Oats, CN with Corn and some Oats.  Oats are supposed to be better for Cholesterol lowering, so HNC gets the edge.HNC and CN both have 2 grams of fiber.  More than most cold cereals so that's good.  (for comparison, Oatmeal has 4 grams).HNC has almonds, CN has peanuts.  I think Almonds are supposed to be a bit healthier but peanuts aren't bad.  Small edge to HNC.Summing up, when i eat cold cereal I prefer HNC to CN but CN is acceptable.

Think of this cereal as a puffed (like Rice Krispies) version of Honey Nut Cheerios, with small pieces of peanut in each O for added crispy-ness and nutty flavor.I say these Os are "crispy" as they're puffed, airy kernels (like Rice Krispies), not "crunchy" like corn flakes or the like.I make the distinction between crispy and crunchy because being the puffed and airy kernels that these are, they have the characteristics of soaking up the milk over time and becoming more dense and taking on a more chewy consistency, but still also holding on to a level of their crispiness. Whereas crunchy cereals tend to get soft and or mushy the longer they're in milk.As to the flavor, these certainly hold-up to the Nut and Honey claim. The sweetness of the nut and honey flavor holds all the way through to staying with you awhile in after-taste (in a good way). I enjoy these Os.Parents concerned about healthy content and sugar might want to be more mindful about this cereal, but otherwise it's a tasty treat.

Kellogg's Crunchy Nut Roasted Nut and Honey cereal is very comparable to my beloved Honey Graham Oh's by Quaker. I  can eat both by the fistful right out of the box.  Got milk?  Who cares!  The Kellogg's offering has a hint of peanut flavor to them as opposed to the Graham flavor of the Oh's but is comparable in texture and crunch.  Certainly you can find a MORE nutritious breakfast cereal but on the other hand you could also find a LESS nutritious snack.  I wouldn't want to eat these every day but with sparing use, these will certainly find themselves on my shopping list again.

This is a very tasty cereal, but I find it a bit too sweet for my liking. The Os look similar to Honey Nut Cheerios, but they taste more like Cap'n Crunch Peanut Butter Crunch. In terms of sugar content Crunchy Nut is comparable to Honey Nut Cheerios (about 10 g each) so if you like that amount of sugar in your cereal then the choice between these two will come down to taste. The little pieces of nuts that are embedded in each O are hardly noticeable, both visually and in terms of the overall taste. It turns out that these are technically speaking not really nuts, but rather peanuts. They mostly have an effect in terms of the overall flavor - the combination of corn/oats and peanut pieces is probably responsible for the peanut-buttery taste. The Os are indeed very crunchy, and they are among the crunchiest cereals that I have ever tried. They don't lose this crunchiness easily even after a minute or two of soaking in milk. Crunchy Nut Os also make a very tasty and convenient snack. I have also tried them with blueberries and the fruity flavor comes as a nice contrast to all the sugariness of this cereal. Overall, this is a very nice cereal but it's nothing spectacular.

Upon first taste, I thought that I was really going to like this cereal. I thought that it was another version of Quaker's Honey Graham O's Cereal, 12-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 12). As such, I was pretty excited. I mean, I like Oh!s. It's one of my favorite cereals.Then the aftertaste caught me. And made me start looking at the ingredient list. I am guessing that it is the corn bran that they put in here, but the aftertaste is somewhere between burned popcorn and Honey Smacks (you know...the one with Dig 'Em Frog). Not so much ideal.If you don't mind the aftertaste, it's pretty reasonable cereal. There are only around 100 calories per 3/4 cup serving, so it's not terribly bad for you like many oversweetened cereal. I think that this is probably the vanguard of an effort by Kellog's to sweeten their cereals with honey, but they haven't quite gotten it figured out just yet. Unlike the other reviewers, I didn't think that it was super sweet, but it certainly was sweeter than my normal cereal.ALLERGY WARNING: THIS PRODUCT CONTAINS PEANUTS.Harkius

The word that comes to mind over and over when eating this is "nutty".  The flavor is delicious and it didn't get soggy in milk.  Has a nice crunch to it and an overall great flavor.  There isn't a whole lot you can say about breakfast cereal but the main thing I want to know is "does it taste good" and my answer is "absolutely". We checked the price in our local grocery, it's selling for four dollars a box around here so that is much to expensive for our price range (a house full of children who eat cereal for breakfast AND snack every day) but definitely yummy!

column9: A pleasant surprise, and quite possibly my new favorite cereal.
column10: When I first got these, I was expecting a Honey Nut Cheerios knockoff. I'm not a big fan of breakfast cereal and normally would rather eat something like bacon & eggs for breakfast, but I ordered these from Amazon since it's been awhile since I reviewed anything for the Amazon Vine Program, and I figured this would be an easy review.Surprisingly, not only are these not a knockoff of Honey Nut Cheerios, in fact the taste reminds me of what was my favorite cereal as a kid, but was sadly discontinued by Post. The cereal I am referring to is Waffle Crisp, a Post brand cereal with a maple-syrup taste to them, and one of the only cereals I actually enjoyed enough that I would choose it over bacon & eggs.This doesn't have the same maple-syrup taste as Waffle Crisp though, it has more of a honey-roasted nut taste like the box suggests. However, something about the taste of the cereal itself, (beyond the honey flavor) reminds me of Waffle Crisp.Once more, I'm not big into breakfast cereal, but I could really see myself buying this in the future, and I most likely will, assuming I can find it at my local grocery store. So if you were a fan of the late Waffle Crisp cereal or just plain looking for something different, try these out.

I would have ranked this cereal 5 stars if the protein count has been higher. Two grams isn't enough for a flea.Taste-wise it's surprisingly good. It's not as sweet as I anticipated but is just enough to satisfy without it being a kids' cereal. It's vitamin enriched, heavily, according to the label.I added a quarter cup of shaved almonds and a scoop of whey protein and it was quite good. That's all I had for my 7am breakfast and I wasn't hungry until my 10 o'clock midmorning nutrition bar.I didn't experience an aftertaste, as one reviewer noted, and I would have to disagree that it's high in sugar as noted by another reviewer.All in all, pretty good for a cereal, one that should satisfy both adults and kids.Loren W. Christensen, author of The Fighter's Body.

column9: Yuk! And who goes to Amazon to buy cereal?????
column10: This stuff tasted like (insert favorite negative adjective that Amazon won't print). I like most cereals but I couldn't put this stuff down, tasted like cardboard something with a half stale texture. Hate to throw 3/4 box of cereal away, we'll see if the birds will eat it - I have my doubts.

I ordered this stuff for the boys since they are the main cereal eaters in the house.  According to them, this is along the lines of Honey Nut Cheerios.  I'll have to agree with another reviewer that mentioned Honey Bunches of Oats.  4 stars, it tastes good but other cereals on the market tastes very similar.  Get it at the grocery store, the price here is crazy!

column9: Like a combination of Honey Nut Cheerios and Honey Bunches of Oats
column10: Kellog's Crunchy Nut Roasted Nut and Honey cereal is (at least it seems to be that it is) designed to be a competitor of Post's Honey Bunches of Oats and Honey Nut Cheerios. This is a good cereal with a slightly stronger taste than the Post cereal, but it is close enough to be of interest to fans of both. To me it tasted like a combination of the two - a very interesting combination.

As other reviewers have noted, this is a round O's-type cereal. I like the fact that it isn't excessively sweet. I avoid most "kid's cereals" these days because of the excessive sweetness, but this cereal is OK from a "grownup taste" point of view (for lack of a better term). The peanut flavor is fairly strong, which is absolutely fine with me. Perhaps a little too carbohydrate-laden to be a main breakfast course for me, but it does make a tasty snack.

Having always liked Honey-O's, I thought I would like these and I found out I liked Kellogg's version better!!!  Honey-Os always had a slight chemical taste but these Crunchy Nuts have all the great flavor (and then some), with NO ODD AFTERTASTE!Sweet but not overwhelmingly so, they have a satisfying crunch to them without tearing up the inside of your mouth! A very strong honey and mild nut flavor top it off to become one of my favorite sweet cereal craving choices!

Just as the description implies, these are very much like Frosted Flakes with specks of peanuts and glazed honey. That said, there isn't much difference since the days of Tony the Tiger, but if you really like them, this is easily a five-star product. Of course, this cereal can't be good for a diabetic or one allergic to peanuts (I am neither, or I wouldn't be writing a review). As a matter of fact, having just eaten a bowl prompted me to type this up! (This is my third review on a food product, by the way.)Eat this in moderation. A new product but probably based on a highly successful product with bits of nut added to the mix. Enough said.

I had been wanting to try this cereal for some time now and it finally went on sale ($1.99 for 10.8oz box) at local supermarket. I expected the texture to be more "weighty" but instead, it has a light crunch.  It has a good amount of sugar but it wasn't super sweet.  I also expected the flavor to be strong but it was rather dainty...not bad, however.  I would only purchase again if it's on sale and I have a coupon.  It's not what I expected, was rather boring; but it is different.  Quaker Oh's: now that's a tasty cereal (mighty hard crunch but tasty)!

column9: Awesome cereal the whole family loves!
column10: This cereal was great!  Sweet enough that the kids like it but not overly sweet.  I also liked that it didn't immediately lose it crunchiness in milk, which means you can take your time eating your breakfast and it will still taste good when you finish.  Have bought again and will continue to buy it again.

column9: Very tasty and liked by all
column10: This cereal is very tasty and was liked by children and adults who tried it which is not an easy accomplishment.  It stays crunchy in milk for a while and is a nice twist on an old cereal.

This product is a mix between honey o's with flavor bits stuck to them. I'd rather go for plain o's or something with a bit more flavor. They did have a good crunch and lasted a good while in milk, but I do not feel they bring anything new to the cereal market.

Initially, it tastes pretty good, but if you wait a minute, it has a sort of ash tray aftertaste. That said, it does stay crispy, but if the flavor isn't great, I'm not sure how much that will matter to you.23 carbs per serving - not Atkins friendly

column9: Sweet, crunchy, and doesn't get soggy
column10: Whether breakfast on a Saturday morning or even as a late night snack, what hits the spot better than a big bowl of cereal?  With dozens of varieties lining the wall of any given grocery aisle, the real question here is whether Kellog's Crunchy Nut is better than the competition and worth the price.Combining the shape and texture of Cheerios with the flavor of a much sweeter treat, the Roasted Nut and Honey cereal is a winner for anyone who likes an intense honey taste and a strong crunch.  Soggy cereal - the bane of any breakfast - isn't an issue here, as it stays firm and crunchy for more than enough time to finish off a full bowl.  The edges of each piece are a little sharp, but they don't shred the mouth like Peanut Butter Crunch or similar breakfast cereals.For the cereal lover with a sweet tooth who doesn't want their breakfast to get soggy, Crunchy Nut Roasted Nut and Honey is a great choice and well worth trying out.

Honey nut Cheerios are very similar to this product except these are darker and sweeter. Kellogs is just trying to put out a better product but I think there was nothing wrong with Honey Nut Cheerios & I prefer them to the Crunchy Nut Roasted Nut and Honey cereal from Kellogs.

I'm always looking for a good breakfast cereal and there are so many on the market now that are both delicious and nutritious that it's hard to choose.  This one I had trouble keeping away from my 14 and 11 year old daughters so that I could review it.  It's not *too* high in sugar and calories and contains a pretty good amount of fiber- two of the key things I look for in addition to taste.  My only knock against the cereal is the same as all of these cereals with "bits" of nuts attached to the cereal, the nuts are too small to really have any texture left and there's not enough of them to really taste. If the box hadn't said there were nuts in there, I would have never known.  I prefer cereals with whole nuts or at least slivers of nuts.

It's hard to say that I "like" Crunchy Nut cereal. It basically tastes like Cheerios, with some nutty sugar sprinkled on top. It's not a super healthy cereal, it's not particularly original, but the taste and crunch are fine.I wound up sprinkling my Crunchy Nut cereal onto desserts to make crunchy treats, rather than eating it as a cereal. My go-to cereal is plain old raisin bran, and I don't see that changing anytime soon.So as a dessert item, Crunchy Nut cereal is very good. As a breakfast item, I think I'm fine with throwing my own sugar on my Cheerios when the mood strikes me. I don't really need that to come prepacked for me.

I tried this cereal at a friend's house and wanted to go out and buy a box for myself. I finally did and I'm glad. Who cares if it's similar to other types of cereal? It's delicious and it's good for you.

At first I didn't like this cereal much, but because it reminded me a lot of Waffle Crisp cereal, I started to enjoy it more.  Then, when I went through my first box, I realized how much I liked Crunchy Nut!It's a great breakfast item with a hint of honey and lots of nutty taste, and has a delicious aftertaste that, like I mentioned already, reminded me of Waffle Crisp.Great new cereal!

Very tasty. I like Honey-Nut Cheerios, and these are very similar, but a little less sweet and more nutty. Of course those with peanut allergies/sensitivities will need to avoid. I shared them with my wife, who generally doesn't like cereal except Corn Flakes, and she liked it a lot.

column9: This is one of the best!
column10: Our whole family loved this cereal, even the 3-yr old asked for seconds. You could taste the nuts but there are no nut pieces. Nuts were completely blended in.Would buy again.

These are obviously closely related to Honey Nut Cheerios, but get less soggy and have a somewhat nuttier flavor. I haven't tried them side by side, but I think they're also a bit sweeter. I like the Cheerios, but I think I'd choose these for the consistency and texture if I were picking on taste alone. That said, if you LOVE Honey Nut Cheerios, I'd just stick with those.

This cereal tastes like Honey Nut Cheerios, but I don't care for the artificial, sugary smell when you first open the box. That plus it leaves the milk looking a beige, peanutty mess! Still the taste is good, just nothing new, unexpected or exciting. Just your basic nutty cereal.

column9: Tastes okay initially but has bad aftertaste
column10: This cereal reminded me a lot of Quaker's Oh's.  It's a lot lighter and less substantial than Oh's, however, and has a weird aftertaste (a bad aftertaste).  The cereal is made with rice and corn instead of wheat, so it doesn't really make you feel full.  The roasted nut and honey taste is somehow adulterated so that it simply does not taste good in your mouth.  Calorically speaking, the folks at Kellogg's did a good job, and the cereal makes a better study snack than breakfast cereal, if not for the horrible aftertaste.Steer clear of this product.  Check out Quaker's Oh's instead.Even if you're on a diet, there is no need to torture yourself with unfilling food that tastes bad.One star.

Is it me? or does this cereal have the lingering taste of corn pops? They even turn soggy like corn pops. I do like corn pops, however a cereal that looks like a 'cheerio' and tastes kinda like a corn pop with a not so pleasant aftertase didnt do it for me.
This cereal not only tastes great but it does not get soggy, which is something my family really appreciates. If you like honey nut o's then you will love Kellogg's Crunchy Nut Cereal!

it took me a while to write my review because i had to eat the whole box of cereal.it has a delicious taste, stays crunchy in milk but the only drawback is that it is a little too sweet for a cereal. it tastes more like a granola bar, a sweet granola bar. dont' get me wrong.  i would buy this again but i would mix it with some other non sweet cereal like cheerios or corn flakes.  this cereal alone is a little sweet but if that's what you like then you will LOVE this cereal.it really has a delicious taste.

Sweet without being overpoweringly so, Kellogg's Crunchy Nut Roasted Nut and Honey is a cereal that both kids and adults will like.  It has a nice flavor, and it provides the energy boost I need to get up and going in the morning.  I would highly recommend this cereal to anyone who likes a breakfast that leaves one full and satisfied without making them feel bloated.

This is a decent enough corn-based breakfast cereal, but frankly I found it rather bland. It's sweet enough, and it's a relatively low-calorie food, but compared to other oat-based or multi-grained cereals that I like, it doesn't have a very distinctive flavor.  I could taste the honey, but the nuts are a bit too subtle.  I kept comparing this cereal unfavorably to Quaker Oh's, which are crunchier, sweeter, and have a more satisfying flavor.

I like this cereal, but then again I like almost any kind of cereal. The product definitely lives up to its name and stays crunchy in milk; it is great as a dry snack, too. Flavor-wise, it reminded my of a cross between Honey Nut Cheerios and Ohs; there was a nice balance between the roasted nut and honey flavors. I'll buy this if I ever see it on sale; otherwise, I'll stick with the generic (but just as flavorful) cereals that cost much less.

column9: Good, but Not What I Expected
column10: My kids really enjoyed this cereal, but it wasn't quite what I expected. I assumed from the cereal's shape and packaging design that this product would be like Honey-Nut Cheerios. It's not like that at all. It's not an oat cereal. The cereal tastes more like Pops, but shaped like Cheerios. It's a pretty tasty cereal, and health-wise it seems pretty typical for the breakfast cereal market.

I liked the crunch but it was a bit too sweet for me. I like my cereals low on sugar and the calories that this had from sugars was more than I cared for. The taste was ok. I wouldn't buy it again. Glad I got to try it for free.

Crunchy Nut cereal is really good :) I like that it stays crunchy in the milk longer than most cereal. It is also sweet without being sweet like a kid's cereal. They also taste great with vanilla yogurt, which is important to me because a bowl of cereal with yogurt is a great bedtime snack without the risk of spilling milk into your bed when one of your children come in and jump on the bed. It is a smaller size box. Hopefully Kellogg's will come out with a family size box. This cereal will be eaten up quickly.

column9: Not Something I Would Spend Money On
column10: I like the version of this cereal that is made by the competitor of this cereal and eat it periodically. I tried this hoping to find a very similar product that I could buy on sale if the other wasn't. The other option was a cereal that was so different that it would  become a new option for me.The taste was adequate. The nuts were almost nonexistent....at least to the naked eye. They may have been rolled in dust, but there were definitely no pieces on the side of the cereal.The color of the cereal was awful, reminding me of the color of what babies leave in a used diaper. It was not at all appealing. In addition, there is a lot of sugar in this cereal.For the above reasons, I wouldn't bother to buy this in the future.

column9: My Rabbits Loved It. Me...Not So Much
column10: First of all, i was really happy to see that this new Kellog's cereal was all natural. I try to stay away from cereals that are more chemical compounds than foodstuffs I can actually recognize. So i was happy to give this cereal a try.I didn't hate it, but I didn't like it either. It had a burned popcorn aftertaste that I really didn't care for, but the actual cereal itself wasn't too bad. It was something to take a bite of here or there as a dry snack. It didn't seem to work too well with milk.That being said, my rabbits were willing to kill for a bite of Crunchy Nut Roasted Nut and Honey as if they were crack addicts looking for a fix. At one point, one of them snuck into the kitchen, jumped up on the counter, pushed the box off, jumped down onto the box and then began dragging it to her cage. Something about the smell of the cereal just drove them into voracious eating. Maybe Kellog would do better selling this as a pet food treat rather than a human one.

I do use this more as a snack. They are really sweet and make a healthy treat in between meals if not for breakfast. I wish they had something like this with almonds instead of peanuts. I am not a huge peanut fan. My toddler prefers colorful cherios to this. Nonethless , Another great breakfast food from kellogs.

This cereal was just okay. It tasted a little like plastic. I liked Kellogg's other new cereal in this same genre, but this one just didn't quite cut it for me. It was boring and waxy. I wasn't impressed.

I admit that I don't like most breakfast cereals, they are usually too sweet, too much one flavor (like Cinnamon) or too "healthy" (i.e. no flavor). But this one, I do like!It has a great combination of flavors, the roasted nut and honey are just right. They stay crunchy in milk, but are not too hard to eat. They taste good as a dry snack as well. I didn't feel they needed any added sugar or anything other than milk.The one bad thing is that the box is smaller compared to other cereals, so the value vs. price isn't as good. But overall, I do like this cereal and have already bought another box.

We eat a lot of cold cereal for afternoon snacks, instead of for breakfast, and this cereal fits in with its not-too-sweet not-too-peanut flavor and crunch.  But it's also not-too-interesting and not-too-memorable.  I would never crave it and don't plan on purchasing it if I see it on the grocery store shelf.  Ho hum.

column9: A solid addition to the cereal aisle
column10: Cereal lovers should check out Kellogg's latest.  The Roasted Nut and Honey is comparable in shape to Cheerios, but the flavor is like nothing else out there.  This product stands out much more than the other Crunchy Nut new flavor.  The taste may not blow your mind, but this flavor quickly distinguishes itself from many others in the same category.

The flavor of the cereal is pleasantly toasty.  It's a strong flavor but not overpowering.  They stay crunchy in milk for some time and the flavor of the left over milk at the bottom of the bowl, an important part of any breakfast, is nicely sweet.Two down sides.  For me, the cereal sat heavily in my stomach for the better part of the morning. A friend who used the same amount of cereal and milk didn't experience that, so it's probably different for everybody.Secondly, several times as I was eating, I found a clump of compressed peanut bits and dust.  It was a very unpleasant contrast of texture and flavor with the sweetened milk and the rest of the cereal.
This cereal didn't last long in our house. Within a couple days it was gone - good, crunchy and tasty!

column9: another sweet, non-nutrious cereal to add to the list
column10: First off I think the Crunchy Nut Golden Honey Nut, 14.1-Ounce (Pack of 4) taste better than this version, but I had to try it.Also, the cereal stays crunch for a bit in milk, but that is because it seems like a big bit of honey coated batter. Not much nutty crunch, more like a cracker crunch to it.Ingredients: Yellow corn meal, sugar, corn bran, peanuts, honey, molasses, salt, whole oat flour, caramel color, baking soda, annatto extract color, ascorbic acid (vitamin C),niacinamide, reduced iron, zinc oxide, pyridoxine hydrochloride (vitamin B6), riboflavin (Vitamin B2), Thiamin Hydrochloride (Vitamine B1), vitamine A, Palmitate, BHT (preservative), Folic acid, Vitamin D, Wheat starch, Vitamin B12.Well? Ehh. Some of the cheapest ingredients (i.e. corn) so don't expect much here. Just surprised that with the heal conscious movement that a more healthy option isn't being made here.It's a nice crunchy snack you could eat straight form the box without milk, like fiddle-faddle or something.I ate a two servings an hour before a bike ride. Went out for a ride and 30minutes into ride I had no energy left. I wasn't surprised as this is just an empty sugary cereal.I personally wouldn't buy it again, but it isn't a bad cereal don't get me wrong. Just wasn't spectacular and doesn't give me a reason to leave my honey-nut cherrios (seeing a pattern here in the ingredients?)For those that need a little something to snack on vs. making this a meal it could be a good option.

I got these expecting them to pretty much be Honey Nut Cheerios, but was pleasantly surprised.  They had a much more distinct nut flavor and actually tasted more like Cap'n Crunch Peanut Butter but without the kind of waxy coating that cereal has.  Overall, the flavor was good (could have been a bit stronger), the texture was great, and it was very fresh and crunchy.  The reason I didn't give it five stars was simply due to value.  The box is quite small and the price is not.  I'm not sure how many servings the box claims, but I'd say you can expect three cereal bowls full and that is about it out of a single box.

column9: Misleading photo, but they still taste great.
column10: My kids really enjoy this cereal probably because it is so sweet. Even sweeter than Honey Nut Cheerios!The image on the box shows each piece coated in nut flakes, far from accurate! You will find a few nut flakes on most of the Os, some with none at all.however, even though the photo isn't accurate, they still taste great. I would like to try some with more nuts as shown though, they might be even better and the additional nuts might better balance the sweetness.The cereal stays crunchy in milk and is very satisfying to eat. They also make a good dry snack and don't leave your fingers sticky.

Pretty good for a sweetened cereal, tastes a bit like a sweeter version of Honey Nut Cheerios, but not too sweet.I went to have a second bowl the third day we had them, but they were gone. That's a pretty good vote of approval from a variety of ages (two parents, 9 year old, 17 and 19.)The remained crunchy, held up to milk, and had a nice bit of substance, a bit more than Cheerios.

column4: Jason P. Pumphrey "the movie & music man"
column10: This is tasty cereal.  It's kind of like Honey Nut Cheerios but a heck of a lot better! I'm a bit stanege since I don't really eat cereal the traditional way. I eat it "dry", sometimes strait from the box! I like this so much I went and bought three more boxes to put in my pantry!. I usually have some as a snack, as it's much better than chips and candy. The other day I ate some while watching a movie, instead of popcorn. This is very tasy stuff indeed and I hope Kelloggs keeps producing it. Hopefully enough people will like and buy it so it won't get discontunued.

column9: Crunchy Nut Roasted Nut and Honey Cereal
column10: The cereal looks like Cheereos, only a darker brown. I didn't see any peanut pieces in the little grain morsels until I got to the bottom of the box, but maybe I just didn't look hard enough.  I couldn't really taste the peanuts either. The cereal tastes like sugar. There's not much difference in taste between this cereal and prepackaged donuts. The crunch is more similar to a donut than to a potato chip, so the cereal is easy to chew.

This Kellogg's Crunchy Nut is very nutty. The cereal is good, slightly sweet and has lots of flavor. But perhaps too much peanutty flavor for a cereal. We like it best in a dry mix with other cereals, nuts, pretzels and things like that.

column9: Crunchy Nut Roasted Nut and Honey
column10: I agree with some of the other reviewers that this cereal is definitely on the sweet side. If you are looking more for flavor than health benefits, or just a sweet treat for your kids, then by all means there is nothing wrong with that. Just please don't think that these are anything close to Cheerios, because they are not. These are much, much sweeter and more tasty, in my opinion. The packaging and amount of product was typical for cereal - nothing out of the ordinary.
Liked the taste and they held up well in milk. I also tried the other variety, Crunchy Nut Golden Honey Nut, 14.1-Ounce (Pack of 4). Preferred this one by an edge.

column9: Not sure this is filling any cereal void for me.
column10: Crunchy Nut cereal is definitely tasty.  For me, it's just a little too nondescript.  If I want a healthy cereal, I go towards a GoLean and add some raisins to jazz it up.  If I want to splurge with a little sugar I'll hit the Cinnamon Toast Crunch.  I thought this Crunchy Nut might fall in between and allow for a healthy, compromised, third option.  For very little Fiber and Protein (2g each), I needed to be more excited to dig in.  But it's just - meh.I couldn't go as low as three-stars because it is tasty and nutty, I just don't think it's found a spot in my regular cereal rotation.  If you don't focus on getting some protein or fiber out of your cereal, than this might be an option for you.

We had been eyeballing this on the shelf for a couple weeks at the local grocery store and were thrilled to get it to review.  My favorite cereals are Honey Nut Cheerios, Honey Bunches of Oats, or Crispix.  If it is my birthday or a camping trip and I am going to indulge in a sweet cereal I prefer Frosted Flakes. Cereal tends to be a sweet breakfast treat, and not a staple in our home, so I can overlook the nutrition facts.Probably the best way I could describe Kellogg's Crunchy Nut is "greasy Kix."  It left a funky aftertaste and slime on my tongue.  The flavor, even before the aftertaste, wasn't good, though it was not the most horrible cereal in the world.  It was edible so I gave it an one star more than something... inedible.  My son thought it was ok, though not a favorite, but this seems to be packaged as an "adult" cereal so his vote doesn't count.  I was done after my first bowl and let him finish the rest over the course of two weeks.  This is unusual in my house as we usually go to blows on who gets the last bowl of cereal.  Even my son did not ask to repurchase!Unfortunately this failed for me.  Sorry Kellogg's!

column9: Will be joining my regular cereal rotation!
column10: I was really pleasantly surprised by this cereal. I eat cereal almost every day so I'm a big fan and very picky about what I eat. I prefer cereals that are actually good for me (like the Kashi stuff), but I never compromise on taste. A lot of cereals nowadays either taste like cardboard or are too sweet. Surprisingly enough, this cereal is delicious, keeps me energized for average or above average compared to my other cereals, and is not too sweet at all.If you've ever had Oreo O's it reminds me of that flavor EXACTLY but more nutty instead of chocolatey, and not quite as sweet. I know that sounds crazy, but if you eat one after the other I think you'll agree with me.Anyway, if you're a fan of peanut butter and cereals that are a bit sweet and crunchy, you'll really enjoy this one.

This is a really tasty cereal that has a nice nutty taste and that stays crunchy and doesn't get soggy in milk.  That being said, they are void of any nutritional value.  I usually try to buy cereals that have less sugar and a lot more fiber, and these don't fit the bill in either way. If you don't mind that and want a tasty cereal that is even good enough to snack on on its own (without milk), then I'd recommend giving them a try.

This is a very nice cereal.  It is very crunchy and is sweetened with honey.  I would have preferred that the cereal not be quite as sweet as it was so I gave it four stars rather than five.  This may not be an issue for other consumers.  It is not as sweet as a product like Cap'n Crunch or Cinnamon Toast Crunch.  I do not care for milk in my cereal but another family member tried it with milk; the cereal held up and did not become soggy. I would buy this cereal again.

This cereal is a great compromise for everyone in the family - sweet and very much like cheerios for those of us that like kids cereals, and healthy for my boyfriend that loves bran and granola. Great buy!

I'm not going to review the nutritional value since everyone should know this isn't a cereal you would buy for that.  The taste however was slightly disappointing.  It's a sweeter Cheerio, but not worth the extra sugar and calories.  I was hoping they would taste similar to Honey Graham O's Cereal, 12-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 12)! cereal, which is a favorite of mine and worth the calories and sugar.  There isn't much nut taste in this, only sugary cereal that doesn't stand out much.  It's not really bad, but I wouldn't bother buying it.  I did like it better without milk.  I could see kids enjoying it as a snack, though I'd stick with Cheerios.

column9: Not super-healthy but a good cereal
column10: I and my kids all enjoyed this cereal.  It's not as healthy as some quality, tasty cereals out there (Fiber One, for example) but it's a tasty alternative for breakfast or snack.

Kellogg's Crunchy Nut is a tasty yet unremarkable breakfast cereal.  I've given it a 4 star rating because I enjoyed it.  Yet at the same time, I probably wouldn't go out of my way to buy it again.One of the main ingredients is peanuts, yet the nut taste is not pronounced.  In fact, I wouldn't have known that it even contains peanuts if I didn't already know.  The flavor reminds me of a cross of regular Cap N Crunch and Cheerios.Sugary sweetness is the dominant theme here.  I like sweet, so I'm not complaining too much.  But I suppose they could throttle back on the sweetness a bit.A 3/4 serving provides about 25% of many of the major vitamins, so there is certainly some nutritional benefit to the cereal. It also provides about 8% of your recommended daily allowance of fiber.The ingredients appear to be decent for the most part, although I have no idea what Pyridoxine Hydrochloride is.  The first ingredient is yellow corn meal followed by sugar, corn bran, peanuts, honey, molasses, salt and whole oat flour.  Again, generally not bad at all.  As noted, I'd prefer that they cut back on the sugar, but then I suppose that they probably wouldn't sell as much of the stuff.So I liked it.  I probably won't buy it again, but if someone served it to me in the future, I'd be perfectly happy.  3.5 stars rounded up to 4.

This is a very tasty cereal with the look of Cheerios.  The nuts are not a major presence, and the flavor is similar to honey smacks.  The sugar content is pretty high, which is probably why it tastes so good.  It is not so much better than other cereals that I would pay extra for it, but it is as good as any other mini-doughnut shaped cereal I have tried.

It takes real innovation to start with corn and sugar to put together scrumptious miniature glazed doughnuts (mmmm ... doughnuts).  The doughnuts of this cereal are about the size of Cheerios, and surprisingly have the same calorie content despite being made of twenty-five percent sugar.  It is real sugar, not the fake high-fructose stuff.  To me, they taste a lot like Belgium waffles smothered in syrup.As an experiment, I sprinkled some under my bird feeder.  The regular birds ignored them.  However, a flock of crows was attracted, probably by the orange color.  The crows hung around for a while but lost interest without sampling the cereal.  Squirrels then appeared to consume the cereal.If they give a Nobel Prize in Food, I think that the designers of Crunchy Nut Roasted Nut and Honey deserve the trip to Sweden.  I am still trying to decide whether this is a good snack or whether the rest of it should go under the bird feeder.

column9: Excellent cereal is a  welcome surprise
column10: "Crunchy Nut Roasted Nut and Honey" is a new fine new cereal from Kelloggs that is most definitely worth a try. It's got a nice nutty flavor and texture, the honey flavor is pleasant but not overwhelming, and although sweet, doesn't overdo it with the sugary taste.Originally at four 10.8 oz. boxes for $7.48 each, the price here on Amazon.com was a bit of a sticking point for what you get. Fortunately, the price is has gone down to a more reasonable price of $4.37 a box, and that is a fair deal for what you get.In all, a very good cereal, and well worth picking up, either here or at your local food market.

This is my first time trying these they are very tasty and I would recommend them. That being said, if you are trying to loose weight or simply watching your diet you probably wont want to eat too much of these outside of occasional use it not for the health-conscious. The young ones and even my husband enjoys these they are very very yummy even to eat dry as a snack. The crunchy nut and gloden nut are both very good.

I really thought these would be a home run but found them bland and disappointing.  I would prefer to eat Quaker Ohs! And they are always cheapier.  So many good cereal choices out there to waste time on something boring.  Skip them.

column9: This Cereal Gets the 4-year Old Seal of Approval...
column10: My 4 year old likes this cereal, and I like giving it to him because it isn't garbage like frosted flakes, etc.This cereal has a sweet taste without being too sweet.  I don't think it has a noticeable "nut" taste to it like you might think.  Definitely stays crisp in milk as others have indicated.Serving size is .75 cups, 100 calories (less than Special K), 1g fat, 23g carbs (10g sugars), 2g dietary fiber, 2g protein.No partially hydro oils, No high fructose corn syrup!

This seems to be Kellogg's answer to GM's Honey Nut Cheerios. The o's themselves resemble their cheerios counterparts except for the fact that they are studded with nuts so gives a more bumpy appearance. I think this is the most detailed observation I ever made on a cereal. It tastes great...better than cheerios..possibly due to its crunchy taste or the rugged structure tickling my taste buds in a different way. Whatever it is, it tastes great and I like it.

This "O's" version is not quite as satisfying as the flake version I have also reviewed, but it is tasty and keeps its crunchiness in milk.  I actually like this one as a snack dry rather than as a cereal in milk.  Of course, I feel the same way about Cheerios - its obvious competition.  Still, a good entry into a crowded cereal market that is not just another kids' sugarcoated cardboard choice.

column9: Very crunchy with real nut pieces!
column10: This cereal is real good. It is very crunchy and has tiny pieces of nuts and a hint of honey. They taste somewhat like honey nut cheerios but these will not get soggy as fast as the cheerios. They are probably as crunchy or more like apple jacks. I eat slow and by the time I finish the last bite is still crunchy. My favorite part of the cereal is the actual nut pieces on the cereal. It gives it that real nut flavor and bite. The nut flavor is not overwhelming either. Nor is the honey. It is a great balance between the two. If you like honey nut cheerios and the crunchiness of apple jacks then you will really like this cereal.

column4: Agatha Kristy "•The secret of getting a...
column10: Sweet, Crunchy, holds up to milk, good for you, lowers cholesterol, flavor filled...what more could you want in a cereal? This is tastier than cheerios, with all the fiber and benefits! It doesn't get soggy in the milk and stays crunchy to the last bite! EVERYONE in my family loves this cereal! The kids, my husband and me! It is good for breakfast, lunch, dinner and a midnight snack!

How much can be said about a cereal?  Crunchy Nut lives up to it's name.  The O's are crunchy and covered with nuts.  Together they create a sweet taste with a little bit of saltiness.  It's a little on the sugary side, but still tasty for adults.  I swear this combination and taste had been done before in a long lost cereal of whose name I can't remember.

My daughter and fiance adored this cereal. I personally thought it was just alright. It seemed reminiscent of Honey Bunches of O's, or whatever that cereal used to be called. It wasn't too sweet, but still tasted very Kellogg-y, if that makes any sense (I know it doesn't, but that's okay).Definitely not the worst cereal on the market. It simply doesn't stand out to me. The pricing is also pretty reasonable.

Far from a "perfect mix" of flavors, Cruchy Nut cereal is basically your average sugary cereal.  Sadly, the sugar is about all you taste, there is no distinct honey or nut flavor, just sugar and crunch.I can't imagine this is any healthier than Captain Crunch or Lucky Charms, and with those cereals, you actually have distinctive flavors.  As an attempt to invade the Honey Nut Cheerios market, this is entirely a failure.

I got this shipped to me on time. The packaging was good, I like that the seller included instructions for planting these. I probably had 99% germination. I was amazed & absolutely thrilled! This encouraged me to buy more seeds online, however I was disappointed with the products from other sellers.Anyway, these seeds were really good. I would buy again.

I have been able to germinate the seeds and ALL of them have popped. I live in Florida so putting them outside is not recommended. It's too hot. I have killed all that have popped by putting them outside. Even though it says they can take the heat, Florida sun is still too hot.

column9: My Yorkies have been on Back to Basic since 2003
column10: It's a good quality dog food, I recommend it. I have been giving it to my Yorkies since 2003. They used to have 2 options: chicken and pork, now they have turkey and pork. The ingredients are good, no by-products or grains and they are small bites, perfect for a little Yorkie's little mouth.

I bought this product hoping that perhaps my finicky Chihuahua would eat it, but... no, she didn't. I did feed it to our other Chihuahua and Dachshund - who will eat anything. Wouldn't buy again due to cost of product and shipping.

column9: Fabulous New Product From Peeled Snacks
column10: We have been fans of the PEELED SNACKS product line for years now. We love their line of organic dried fruits. We really appreciate having a snack that not only is delicious but is organic and has no added sugar. Kind of nice that the taste is really high but the calories are really low. Now we have discovered that PEELED SNACKS has a new product: Apple Crunch. Wow! We are in love again! Apple taste with a really fun crunch. Not only a fantastic healthy and delicious snack but really fun to eat! If you take your peeled snacks to the movies, as we do, be sure to chew your apple clusters with your lips closed or everybody in the theater will be looking at you! Maybe you should take a few extra packages to share. Thank you PEELED SNACKS for giving us not only tasty and healthy snacks but clusters that are just fun, fun, fun to eat! We are a senior citizen couple and take great care to eat healthy. We appreciate that the entire PEELED SNACKS line lets us snack while having fun and not having to worry about sugar and our waistlines. We can't wait to see what the folks at PEELED SNACKS have in line for us next. Until then, we have a lot to enjoy!
