I've commented on the Vino Italiano Motepulciano kit, and this review will have some of the similar info.  I really like the Italian reds, and the Valpolicella the best of them (I am currently racking my 4th batch of the Valpolicella).  If you make the kit by following the instructions, it will turn out dry.  I drink dry, but my preference is for a wine to be slightly dry, so I make modifications to the program.I have just started my 15th kit so my experience level is getting up there. I've done kits from a couple of other companies; Wine Expert, and Vino Vida. I've bought kits from other online companies, from a local brew hut, and from Amazon. I'll continue to buy these kits so long as they are selling them at this value.You cannot beat the Vino Italiano Kits. They are complete with everything, delivered to your door with free shipping, and they make a really good wine. Let me back up and say first that a wine I like may not be good to someone else. We each have our own preferences. I've had many a wine served up at restaurants with price ranges of [...] to [...] a bottle. And the wine I am making now I like better than pretty much anything I've tasted from the restaurant, or the store.I have tried the Valpolicella, Shiraz, Reisling and the Montepulciano from Vino Italiano. I have made a couple merlots, some white zinfandels also, but from other companies. I prefer the reds, and made the others because my kids requested.I'll typically, but not always, spike the kit with additional sugar to up the alcohol content slightly. If you follow the instructions, the initial specific gravity comes out around 1.080-1.084. By adding a couple pounds of sugar in the form of corn syrup or simple syrup, you get to around 1.09 or better. That usually will give a final ABV of 11.5 - 12%. Other things that I do outside of the kit instructions include adding 1 cup of black oak chips, 1-2 tbsp of vanilla extract, and a lb or two of some black cherries, blue berries or black berries (found in the frozen foods section at the store). Lastly, I like my wine not so dry, so I'll back sweeten just as I am bottling. Again using corn syrup and usually between 8 - 16 oz per 6 gallons. To me the corn syrup seems to be better than simple syrup, but that's just my preference.I love the stuff. Currently my production is having a hard time keeping up with my consumption. Cheers.Dec 31, 2010 Update!!!We opened several bottles of the Valpolicella over the holidays.  This is from wine that I made in March 2010.  With every batch, I retain 2 - 5 bottles and let age somewhat.  Usually I drink the rest, beginning immediately after bottling.  The wine is pretty good, even though it is pretty young.  Let me state for the record, this is my preference and everyone's taste is different.  Make/drink what you like, and don't let anyone tell you its wrong...  The Valpolicella that we drank over the holidays had aged about 9 months, and I must say, it was very good. The aging had made a good wine even better.  For the most part, I followed the instructions included in the kit with some additions.  In this batch, I had added 2 lbs of corn syrup and about 1 1/2 cups of black oak chips to the kit at the start of the fermentation process.  The alcohol content, after 2 weeks of fermentation, calculated to be around 14.7%.  A little high, and no doubt due to the added corn syrup.  I racked the wine, clarified and aged it another 4 weeks before bottling.  And when I bottled the wine, I back-sweetened with another 1 lb of corn syrup and added some potassium metabisulfite (1/4 tsp dissolved in 1/2 cup of water to preserve and prevent after-fermentation).  This wine has received the most compliments from family and friends.  I just ordered 2 more kits and will try to replicate the recipe (I keep a wine log of every batch so as to capture the important points of the good, and the bad!).  I hope this helps with your wine making and you enjoy the fruits of the vine as much as I do...  Cheers.  SamMay 2012 Update!!!I have made a couple of changes to the recipe that have been an improvement.  First, I included the recommendation from another review that said to make the kit to only 5 gallons instead of the 6 gallons that the recipe calls for.  Sure, you get 4 less bottles of wine.  But, this improves the fullness of the wine and its finish.  Secondly, I boil 2 - 4 ounces of dark oak chips in a quart of water for 5 minutes. This is then added to the juice and then diluted to the 5 gallon level.  Be sure to let the whole solution cool to 70 - 75 deg F before the yeast is added.  Add the oak chips and all the liquid!  This really improves the flavor, adding a powerful oak flavor that smooths the final wine and improves its overall taste.  I have incorporated both these steps into all the Vino Italiano wine kits.

I've been making wine at home for a couple of years now and have over a dozen kits under my belt.  I buy all of my kits at a local brew/wine store and am also somewhat active on an on-line winemaking forum so I'm pretty familiar with the various wine kits available out there.When I ran across these Vino Italiano kits on Amazon I was a bit leery as I had never heard of them before.  They were having a great special at the time, though, so I couldn't afford not to give them a try.I am very pleasantly surprised! It's a small volume kit at 5.1 liters of concentrate, but still makes the typical 6 gallons of wine. The packaging is first class and while the wine is still young (clearing in my carboy) I have every indication it's going to make a nice, red table wine.  If you've come across these and have been hesitant to order, there's no need.  They are quality, small-volume kits AND the even come with labels, corks, and foil tops.  I will buy again in the near future.04-28-2010 Addendum: This wine has been in the bottle for a little over 6 months now and I thought I'd update my initial report.  In a nutshell - this is a very pleasant, medium-bodied, red table wine.  It finished very dry, not fruit forward at all, but at the same time it goes down very easily.  I'd almost refer to it as "gulpable".If you're looking for a big, full-bodied Cabernet or Bordeaux style of wine, this kit isn't for you (probably not any of the Vino Italiano kits for that matter).  But if you're looking for a lighter, nice drinking red, I don't think you'll be disappointed.  I'd view this wine as food-friendly and it'll make a great pizza or picnic wine.I plan on making two more of these Vino Italiano kits and giving them a nice long rest in an oak barrel to see how good these kits can be given a little more patience and time.

For the money this has been the best wine kit I have ever bought. I have been making wine for years and I have paid a lot. Now that I have found a more affordable way to do it I may be making more than just a few a year! Would recommend. Came quickly good product.

All went well and when done I racked some of the lees into a clean milk jug so I could taste test it. You know I had to do this! (grin) Color is a deep rich red and taste is really quite good even at this stage, I can't wait for the finished product.My thanks again to Sam for his review this may be my favorite wine too. Still 5 stars plus on rating>UPDATE:Bottled yesterday after racking and filtering. Tasted some and found it to be slightly fruity semi dry with no  after taste. It was as good as most wines at the package store and I bet with some age it will be better than most. This morning I put the shrink caps on and the labels. The instructions are quite simple and if you're a newbie at wine making, you should definitely try these Vino Italiano kits made by Paklab as they are fool-proof.  This "Val" kit is my absolute favorite.  It's completely drinkable in 4 weeks, but give it 4 months in the bottle and it's ridiculous the value you get for a buck fifty a bottle.

First off you can't beat the price....which can be concerning when looking at wine kits.  The kit is of nice quality with many nice extras when compaired other kits.  Incldues corks, shrink caps, labels and all the ingrediants needed to make wine.  The wine came out great.  The flavor is great and I would highly recommend it.

I did not expect much from this kit but got more than I thought.  I made it to 5 gallons, as this is what others had mentioned.  That was likely the key to this kit.  Had I made it to 6 gallons it would have been extremely watery.  I tweaked it with a banana skin, 1 pound of raisins, Hungarian medium oak, and 1 can of dark sweet cherries.  At 4 months it wasn't so good. At 8 months it was a tasty wine.  I turned out to be a light to medium bodied wine.  Buy it and tweak it a bit.

column9: can't beat price not a all afternoon drinking wine
column10: This wine was ok not really alot of flavor. I had to add about 16oz of conditioner to it to try to over come the alcohol taste and still it was very dry. Alcohol was app. 14% but for the price can't really complain. I have also purchased three other kits from vino besides this one moscato,tuscany rossa and chardonnay.I will comment on chardonnay as it is finished now and the others as soon as they are completed

column9: Good for a snack! (Not just for baby)
column10: I picked these up today and thought I would try them out for myself, since I don't have a baby.  They are pretty good, a lot of apple flavor with a nice texture.  I enjoyed them and plan to purchase more to use as a great snack.

These are very good. As an adult I use them as a fruit snack.  I can't believe that someone is charging 49.99 for an 8 pack!  That is over $6 a package!  They are under $3 in the local grocery store.If Amazon offers them in the future at a reasonable price I will order them but not from some outfit gouging people!
The tastiest and sweetest strawberry soda out there, I love this soda! Great with ice, reminds me of a snow cone.

column9: Its free range so i guess its okay
column10: The chicken pieces inside are not firm. Some of them have disintegrated into dust like residue and they line the bottom of the can. The other solid pieces are powdering slowly. Not at all appealing to watch when you open the can expecting chunk chicken. Still since this is a healthier option and maybe they are not using any preservatives to keep the firmness, i dont have much problem with this product.

column9: a bit pricey but really handy
column10: I never used canned chicken before so cannot compare this to other brands.  I buy this because even though it is not organic it is the healthiest canned chicken I can find anywhere.  YES, it does fall apart and there are some teeny bits in the can as the other reviewer pointed out.  However, it has a really nice rich flavor.If you hate handling raw chicken as much as I do you will find these little cans to be just the right thing when you want to make white chicken chili or chicken noodle soup for 2, or when you want just a bit of meat to toss into a veggie stir fry right at the end.  I use Imagine brand organic free range chicken broth.  The combination of that broth and this chicken is very tasty indeed.

This tea is wonderfully light, smells so intriguing, nice and fresh and piney.  The leaves are absolutely perfect, not broken or squished!  Beautiful product inside and out.  Would highly recommend to every tea drinker who seriously loves certain types of tea.  This silver needle was superb, I even skipped using a dash of honey it was that good.  The price I felt was fair too. It comes with two tins which is perfect for gift giving, sharing, or just plain enjoying a few well brewed pots a day!

column4: M. B. Alcat "Curiosity killed the cat, but sa...
column10: If you want to taste something different, and truly wonderful, buy this product. "Dulce de leche" is a typical Argentinian product, and one of my favorite temptations. In case you are not familiar with it, I must say that you are really losing something great...Dulce de leche is a dessert that can be eaten alone or as a topping (for example, on waffles, bread or ice cream). It is also used a lot in cakes and other pastries, and its savor is sweet. It is made by blending hot milk, sugar, and vanilla, and as a result has some nutritional value. However, the most important thing is that it is mouthwateringly delicious :)Even if this product is extraordinarily good, it is important to choose the right label, because a good one can be guarantee of excellence. In my opinion, "La Salamandra" is one of the few labels that allow you to be certain that what you are going to eat is not only tasty, but also made of  superior quality raw ingredients. "La Salamandra" is very well-known in Argentina, but has also won some prizes in USA. For example, this product won the 2000 Fancy Food Show's Gold Trophy for spreads/sweet toppings. All in all, I advise you to indulge yourself and give "La Salamandra"'s dulce de leche a try. The price isn't overly high, so you don't have much to lose, and all to win :)Belen Alcat

This is a caramel flavored filling/topping that is very popular among people from Latin America. I grew up eating dulce the leche, as my parents were Cuban. My ex-husband is from Argentina, and he, too, grew up eating this mouth-watering, sweet dessert topping.It is delicious with ice cream, with flan, and as pastry filling. I even know people who eat it as a spread on white bread. It is also delicious by itself, though one cannot eat all that much of it in one sitting as it is so sweet. When I discovered its availability on Amazon and saw that it was recommended by a fellow reviewer, I immediately bought three jars, even though the shipping was on the high side. Well, the actual product more than met my expectations, as it was absolutely delicious. I can certainly understand why it was the Gold Trophy winner in the spreads/sweet toppings category at the 2000 Fancy Food Show.I am only sorry that I did not buy more than three jars of it, as I see that it is no longer available through Amazon, and I am plumb out of it. The good thing, however, is that I know how to make dulce de leche. I am, however,  notoriously lazy about cooking. Maybe the fact that it is no longer available will galvanize me into whipping up a batch of this delicious taste treat. If not, I can only hope that it will become available.

I am from Argentina, and have eaten Dulce Leche since almost birth in almost any imaginable way. Its excellent and this particular brand is excellent as well. Hence the 5 StarsOnly problem is this is NOT made by La Salamandra, but by a company called Andyson (little known in Argentina as they are export-only). As far as i know La Salamandra has not bought them, and they are in fact their competitors.

Nothing that I have found compares to the quality of this product.  Unfortunately shipping is high because it is a food product.  Igourmet however is a class act that I'd purchase from again.  Excellent customer service...even over a weekend.

I was born in Argentina, so probably enough said.  It's the most versatile wonderful spread ever.  We ate it with croissants, filled crepes with it, filled cakes with it, and I and my brother (and now my children and grandchildren) ate it with a spoon.  It's great stuff!

This dulce de leche was so delicious.  I used it to fill pumpkin cupcakes at Thanksgiving and had nothing but rave reviews.  For taking the lazy way out this is the best product to still make whatever you make taste homemade.  I just did not have the time or inclincation to make the dulce myself and I honestly don't think it would have tasted as good as this product's!

This is an assortment of K-cups for chai tea and chai tea lattes.  It is a convenient way to taste test various products without buying a lot of any single one.  They come loosely packed in a plain white box.

column9: Beware of the k-cup count, not worth it!
column10: I did not read the k-count carefully and was extremely disappointed to realize that I paid over $1 each per k-cup for these teas. In addition, it is packaged in a "gift box" which is just a plain white box that look like someone took their leftovers and sold them. I was expecting more quantity and something that looks store bought. I am very disappointed for the price.

column9: Will work in a pod machine
column10: This looks like it is meant for a store counter, not a gift or home purchase.  The tins would make nice favors, hostess gifts, stocking stuffers, etc.They don't mention it, but the bags are pods.  Not that you can't use them as a bag, but still a surprise.  I also didn't expect the tins to be as large as they are, I was thinking pocket size. The tin is about 3.5" square by 1.5".  The eight bags are sealed in a foil package so you know it is fresh when you open it.  The tin has a tight fit so they won't go stale right away after you open the package.I am not a big tea drinker.  I love the tea I get in Chinese restaurants, but I have never been able to duplicate the taste.  I know it is good for me so I have experimented a lot this year.So far I have only drank the pomegranate.  It smells divine. I used one pod to make a small teapot of tea and it steeped quickly, has a rich color and a sweet and delicate aroma.  I detect no bitterness to the tea itself.  Success!I am pleased with the Bentley brand and have given it as a gift to great acclaim.I recommend it.

If you're ever near Savannah (GA) swing down to their waterfront River Street.  River Street Sweets takes up the better part of a block.  As you enter, a candy maker will offer you a sample of their famous pralines, but check out all the other stuff they make.  The kids will be entranced with the wall lined with bins of every known individually wrapped candy and begin filling a bag.  Adults prefer the hand-made chocolates and caramels and their almost endless combinations. They have a web site, of course, but that and this on Amazon doesn't begin to do the place justice.

column9: Like sitting in a cafe in Paris...
column10: I had this tea for the second time yesterday, at a fine local tea house, and my friend and I drank two pots of this luxurious liquid.  Paris tea is one of the finest teas I have ever tasted.  It is delicious plain, and is decadent with cream and sugar.  I feel like I am sitting at an outdoor cafe in Paris while drinking this.  Very lovely!

This was the first time I've purchased a product from Lana's Little House, and I will definitely be a regular customer in the future. I was searching for a good jasmine tea, but when I read the reviews for Paris I couldn't resist adding a tin to my shopping cart.  It has quickly become my "go-to" tea.  The flavor is smooth and lovely--I'm typically more a fan of green tea, but this black tea has become a favorite.  A perfect winter day is coming in from the slopes to enjoy an evening with a pot of Paris (just a touch of honey and lemon!), a good book, and my husband napping on the couch with the cat curled up on his chest.  The bonus is that the shop owner, Lana, provides excellent service.  I received my package in the mail very quickly, she included a sweet little handwritten note and free sample in the package, and when I had a question for her she answered promptly. Additionally, her prices are very competitive for a good tea.  Not only can you feel good about purchasing a high quality product, but you can feel great about supporting an excellent small business!

I first tasted this tea in a fine resaurant. I ordered it the next day from Amazon.I never grow tired of the flavor. Paris tea constantly surprizes and delights me with its many layers and textures of taste.

I purchased this tea after seeing all of the great reviews, and I was not disappointed. Once it arrived, I immediately opened it and was delighted by the fragrance of the tea. I took several deep breaths before actually making the tea it smells so good. It is very comforting, and now one of my new favorites. If you like fragrant teas like I do (I'm also a huge fan of Jasmine tea), then you want this tea! I like how you can reuse the tea bags, although the second cup isn't quite as nice. It's nice plain, but I feel like the comfy aroma just begs to be complimented with a little milk and honey. I will definitely be ordering more of this tea and more from Harney and Sons, if only to get the adorable tins the tea comes in!
Not only is this a delicious tea, it smells wonder, too. This makes for a very tasty tea experience and one that brings comfort any time of day.
Very pleased with this tin of tea!  My girlfriend was thrilled.  We both love the little sachet bundle they use to pack the tea... very delicate!  Thank you so much!

You haven't had a cup of tea until you've had a cup of Harney & Sons Paris tea.  Before I discovered Harney & Sons Paris, I didn't realize tea could taste so delicious, so elegant, so lovely.  It comes in a beautiful tin, love the silk bags, and it's difficult (if not impossible) to return to grocery store brands after trying this.  But for the price, why should you?  Harney & Sons has taken something as simple as tea and elevated it to a whole new level.  Highly recommended (makes a wonderful gift, too!).
After reading all the reviews I was somewhat disappointed.  I read on the Harney and Sons website that this tea had a vanilla caramel flavor..but it has more of a fruit flavor.

I first had Harney and Sons Paris tea at the Sunriver Resort in Oregon in May 2007. It was rainy & cold out and I was sick & stuffy but I looked forward to this tea each morning.  It has an amazing aroma and flavor and was incredibly soothing.  I ordered some online shortly after getting home.  It is my favorite tea. Ever.  And when I ran out of the sachets, I saved the tin and my little secret is that I occasionally open that tin and take a whiff because it just smells that good!!

I bought this for my son. We sat at the counter in the kitchen and talked of tea, Shoguns, Japan, and many other things that interest him. Yes, the tea is superb, but more than that, two tea bags and 30 minutes made magic in my kitchen. It is not often that you get the chance to appreciate your child as an intelligent, thoughtful person. That is the real magic of the tea.

This is very similar in flavor to Kusmi St. Petersburg, although St. Petersburg is far superior in complexity of flavor. Ultimately, I find Paris to be a little boring.I've noticed that the caffeine in Paris makes me feel jittery for some reason. I drink black tea every morning and don't have this problem with other brands. Not sure why Paris seems intensely caffeinated in comparison.For those who'd like to try this tea without breaking the bank, I've found Paris and other selections at The Fresh Market for just $5.99. My local grocery store carries a few flavors as well, all for around $6. H&S Dragon Pearl Jasmine is my favorite from this line.If you're willing to shell out $15-20 for a tea, try Kusmi instead.

I read the review and was wondering if the tea was as good as everyone said.  Wow, it is even better!!  Reminiscent of Earl Grey, but slightly different, and much better. My favorite tea in the world.Perhaps it's expensive at 45 cents a satchel, but I get 2 cups out of each, and it's much cheaper than a Starbucks latte.  And this is certainly NOT Lipton tea.
I just love this tea! I love vanilla tea, fruity tea, and black tea, and this has the perfect combination. I save it for the weekends when I have time to savor it. It does remind me of Paris....

Ordered this tea recently and their Hot Cinnamon tea also. I have to say both are exquisite but this Paris Tea is the best black tea I have ever had! It's a perfect blend of black with a touch of Earl Grey and a nice Vanilla note. It is suppose to be one of the most popular tea blends in Paris. I am getting 3 small tea cups brewed per sachet (bag). If you love tea you have to try this one! The tins are cool also!
This tea is outstanding!  Tea use to give me side effects, so I gave up on it.Not only is this product delicious, but I must say, "Viva Le France"!Harney and Sons Paris I use honey to sweeten.
This is my most favorite tea ever. Expensive but worth the splurge - I also think it makes a great gift.

column9: Difficult to describe how amazing this tea is
column10: You must taste it for yourself. It has a floral sweet scent, and the taste is creamy and rich. It's almost like the best Earl Grey with something added. It's excellent. This is now my go-to cuppa!
I had this flavor tea while visiting a coastal coffee/tea house. I had truly enjoyed it and was thrilled to find it here. I still enjoy this as part of my tea rotation.

The sweet, floral notes of the Paris blend tea infuse a delicate balance of citrus and fruit flavor. Tea sachets are meshed for adequate steeping, though nothing can replace properly brewed loose-leaf tea. The bagged tea leaves are high quality, noticeably more natural then mashed contents of typical American tea bags. Texture of tea is highly smooth, leaving behind a pleasant, velvety taste. Wonderful with cream and sugar! Perfect for breakfast or an afternoon cup. Worthy of pinkie lifting, fine bone china, and a fresh made scone or two. Definitely recommended.

I have purchased Paris tea several times and it is great.  I give this as hostess gifts to my tea loving friends and they are always so happy to receive it.Thank you for carrying this item.  I cannot find it locally.

I adore "Paris" tea by Harney & Sons.  In fact, I love all H & S teas, but Paris is my fave!!!  It has a hint of bergamot among the blend of other palette-pleasing herbs and spices, which always seems to transport me to a pleasant and soothing place. I recommend it highly.
ordered this for my daughters paris tea birthday party, what a perfect fit, smells and tastes soooo good.
I was given a tin of Paris tea for Christmas.  I loved it. Ordered as gifts for Mother's Day. All that received "Paris" loved it too.
This is a very tasty tea. I served it at a bridal shower and it was one of the favorites. My husband loved it and took the remaining tea bags to work. We'll be ordering more!

I was  very pleased with this item I purchased and will order it again.  The tea is most delicious and I really love the tin it is packed in.  I found the Amazon pricing  the most economical.Leah M. Barone
THE COMPANY DISTRIBUTING THIS TEA ARE FABULOUS PEOPLE TO DEAL WITH....AND IN THIS DAY AND AGE...IT WAS A MOST PLEASANT SURPRISE......LOVELY TEA............

This tea has the best flavor!  I've tried it in a local cafe and in a nice restaurant, where I order it every time.  It's delicious and I'm always sad when my cup is empty!  I can't wait to be able to make it for myself at home!
Treat yourself to top quality tea and feel like Parisian royalty. Steeping instructions included to ensure a top quality experience.

This tea is soo good.  This is the only flavor I've tried, so I will by more.  I wish you could find it for sale in shops, I noticed Starbucks has their basic mixes like black and green teas...but no other markets have it.  I think I saw some at Williams Sonoma, too.  But that's it.
...but man do I like this tea. It has a nice aroma and nice flavor. Of course... how do I better express this in a review. Oh! Put your nose up to the computer screen... Smell... Ah! Isn't that nice?

Finicky cat loves this flavor and stores locally do not stock it. She tends to leave many of the chunky bits but after having her turn her nose up and leave everything in her dish with other flavors it's clear she likes this cat food. Purchase it for her on the Amazon subscribe & save option so she always has plenty of cans available.  Subscribe and save price is a few cents over PetCo price but Amazon includes shipping and PetCo does not so Amazon comes out less expensive overall.

My cat is really, really finicky.  I needed to get her on a lower fat diet pronto and it had to be low carbs as well.  This fits the bill and I was SHOCKED when she gobbled it up.  She LOVES this stuff.  Will be trying the roasted Turkey next.  In looking at the ingredients, it has muscle meat and not just by products.  It has a very high protein % as well.  For those wondering it is 56% protein, 34% fat and 10% carb.  Very good food for a diabetic cat or a cat who needs to lose some weight.  I will be ordering from Amazon on their subscribe and save plan and have cases delivered to my front door.  Calories per 3 oz can are 78.  I have done my homework!

My two kitties enjoy a diet of all natural top of the line cat food, but they are not above enjoying a little "junk food" now and then. I ran out of their natural brand between shipments and went to the supermarket where I grabbed a few cans of Fancy Feast, not even looking at what flavor it was. The kits were pawing at the can as soon as I popped the top and started gobbling the food before it even hit the dish! I was shocked! None the less, I can't help calling Fancy Feast Roasted Chicken "junk food", since chicken,( which is "supposed" to be in the can---and, by the way, ROASTED !!!! if we are to believe the label), is listed in a distant fifth place, after fish broth, meat by products, salmon, and wheat gluten. I care about what goes into the pets' food as much as I do my own and I have seen the benefits of a good healthy diet on their general health, appearance and well being... however, that being said, I can't see the harm in indulging in some tasty little food by products now and again...we all need a junk food fix now and again, and since the kitties love it so much, it makes me happy to give it to them as  a treat.
only $13.29 a case on the petco site (Oct 20, 2011) - not worth the .70 cents a can they're charging here.
Walmart has them for $5.99 a box...Thats $24 for 4 boxes... Why so expensive?These bars are a very airy crisp type consistency. They are very light and tasty. Great job Atkins on this bar.

My mother won't use any othe tea.  We spent years picking up boxes here and there until I decided to check Amazon on chance that it would have it, and it did.  Now my mom can order directly from Amazon.  My mother is Scottish and this is her first choice of tea.

column9: The Great Taste of London Cuppa
column10: I grew up in Scotland in the 1930's. The three daily meals were called breakfast,dinner, and tea, in that order. Yes,tea was so important that the last meal of the day was called tea.  I've lived in the USA for over 50 years. It's been great but finding an easy source of good tea has been a chalenge, until now. That is until I found London Cuppa and an easy and affordable source via Amazon.com. The taste is rich and very smooth; the best tea I've ever had.

As one other reviewer said... I found this tea by accident, and now I search for it.Everything else pales in comparison.  This is absolutely the best black tea anywhere.  I've tried brand after brand, both major and obscure.  London Cuppa beats everyone else.  You haven't really had tea until you've tasted London Cuppa.I used to read novels where the heroine was in (mostly emotional) distress and some kindly woman would say, "Here, love, let me fix a good, strong cup of tea."  And I could never identify with that, because tea for me was that watery stuff with barely any flavor or color that people drank because it was "better for you than coffee".  "Strong Tea" seemed an oxymoron.  Now, it's London Cuppa, and it's great!  Try it, and you won't be able to live without it.

I have been drinking London Cuppa tea for a few years, always getting the 80 or 40-bag boxes from tjmaxx.  However, I can't find them there anymore and luckily Amazon carries them.  I go through about 2 to 3 bags a day.  At 7 cents a tea bag, this is the best deal if you must have strong, unflavored black tea.  It is great drinking by itself, with cream, and/or sugar.  I can't recommand it enough to strong tea lovers!  Amazon has the best deal and at this price, you don't pay for shipping.

column9: It was love at first cuppa!
column10: Once upon a time I dated a Brit who taught me to appreciate tea that actually has some flavor and body, which teas "blended for the American palate" do not have, and also how to make it (the water MUST be BOILING when poured over the bags).  And once you know what tea SHOULD be, you can't ever go back. I was spending a fortune getting various brands from importers when I tripped over London Cuppa at TJMaxx and bought a box...After I'd made the first cup I went back and bought every box they had...and continued to do that every time I saw it at TJMaxx till I found the 440 bag pack at an importer. Their price was good, but their shipping charge was outrageous! I was about to order again from them anyway till it occurred to me to check Amazon (what the heck, they have everything else!)--and there it was, even eligible for free super saver shipping! Woohoo! :)My only quibble with the 440 count bag is that, unlike other English tea brands, the tea bags aren't in 40 or 80 count air tight pouches. 440 bags is a LOT of tea bags, and tea deteriorates when not stored in air tight conditions for any length of time. But I have a Food Saver and a Fresh Saver (vacuum baggers for frozen and fresh foods), so I repack it myself in bags of 80 and keep those in the big bag in the pantry (yes, those bags ARE expensive, but they're re-useable). When I open a pouch it goes into a sealable tin by the stove.If you like GOOD strong black tea, you'll love London Cuppa. And Amazon has it for the best price.

Strong English tea, no doubt about it.  No funky after taste, either.  Just bold and delicious and the best pick me up.  It's my preferred brand and I've been drinking English teas for a good 25 years now.  I've been known to clear the shelf at TJMaxx when the boxes of 40 and 80 pop up.  Imagine my surprise and delight when I discovered that I could get 440 bags from Amazon!!!  If you buy the 440 of London Cuppa, then please keep your tea in a tin, to preserve the flavour and don't ever store it in the freezer.  It will moisten and mold there.

London Cuppa is the best tea I have tried.  I am not a coffee drinker but I love tea.  I have tried a lot of different breakfast type black teas and London Cuppa is by far the best.  It is my daily morning hot beverage.  Not only does it make great hot tea but it is just as good, if not better, as an iced tea.  I cannot buy London Cuppa in stores locally so I have to order it online.  Being able to get it through Amazon now makes it even easier for me to get my favorite tea.  Try London Cuppa you'll love it.
Found this tea in my local Marshalls; and then it disappeared!  I was so happy to find it on Amazon I ordered the 440 bags of tea. Thanks to Amazon for always carrying what I want and need.

I was first introduced to good tea by a couple of expatriates from Britain. This is the tea they drank. The only place to find it was at TJMax, if you can believe it. The chance of actually finding it on the shelf was iffy at best, considering I was competeing with about a dozen serious tea drinkers who also knew about this stash. I actually walked into the store one time to find my good friend who introduced me to London Cuppa walking out with 10 boxes, he was kind enough to have left one behind. Needless to say, it is absolutely wonderful to have found this source. I was really delighted to find the bag of 440 tea bags to be huge.

I first tasted The London Cuppa years ago buying a box at a local store. Since then I have searched for it every time I am in a store that sells tea. Lo and behold, finally after about 10 years, Amazon has it! I bought a package of 440 tea bags packaged in a resealable bag that will keep it fresh. I now have this robust and flaverful black tea twice a day (at least). I brought some to my office to share and will still have enough to last me more than half a year. Wonderful!

column9: I found this tea by accident, NOW I SEARCH for it!
column10: This is my favorite daily tea. And while this is a huge bag, I use a "pretty tin" that I never wanted to get rid of for 3 weeks of tea close to the kettle. This is an GREAT buy! Enjoy, and relax with a great black tea!

column9: false economy - do not waste your money
column10: I always purchase either Yorkshire Tea or London Cuppa from TJMaxx but, recently, they have been out of stock.  I was delighted to see this supersize 440 London Cuppa teabags on Amazon and did not hesitate to spend $33.  Delivery was efficient but I am so disappointed with the taste.  There is very little tea in the bag which means you have to use two bags to make a decent cuppa.  Yesterday my usual 80 bag box reappeared in TJMaxx (price $6) and I snatched every one off the shelf to compare ... as I suspected, the teabag from the 440 pack weighs 2g and the bag from the 80 box weighs 4g.

column9: My favorite tea - - it's strong and flavorful!
column10: I'm not an expert, but I can say Cuppa London is smooth and strong and has a rich flavor, more so than any other I have ever tried.  I, therefore, always order this giant 440 bag size, about once a year (or a bit more), for my own personal use.  I drink it every day, rather than coffee, and keep the bag tightly sealed and refrigerated, taking out only a week's worth of tea bags at a time for easy access.  You don't need to let it steep very long, which is great for us impatient people!

I have been drinking London CUPPA for many years now; my day begins and ends with it!  This is freshest, most delicious shipment I have yet received. I love being able to go to amazon.comLondon Cuppa Tea 440 Bags and with one click, make shopping the easiest on Earth! My items always arrive in record time. Thank you amazon for carrying this delightful remedy for the daily grind!  Like a magical elixir, it refreshes and livens up even the most tedious day!  I highly recommend adding it to your beverage list!Blessings! :>)di

This is a very good cuppa tea. I would highly recommend. I like a dark tea that is not bitter when steeped for 2-3 minutes. I like mine with a bit of sugar and milk. Very good I will buy it again and again.
I love this tea!!  I have been drinking it for years.  I've tried so many other kinds, and, I have never tasted any I like better.

This is an excellent tasting tea.  The tea when set draws rapidly as compared to other teas and is strong in consistency.  Prior to tasting this tea, I always preferred Lipton tea bags but have switched to London Cuppa as it's not only refreshing but very tasty and encourages you to replenish your cup of tea.  My wife says she's now hooked on this tea.  I endorse this tea to all you tea lovers. My next move is to try this tea as an Iced tea as well.

I found that this always makes a consistantly good-tasting and substantial cup of tea. The plastic bag stores well which is good as this quantity is the better part of a year's supply for me. Ordering from amazon also means incredibly fast shipping.
I love this tea!  It's a simple, plain black tea & nothing more.  Yet it's an amazing cuppa tea!  I love it!Definitely worth having on hand.  And this bag is going to last all year for me.

London Cuppa Tea 440 bags is a good everyday black tea. The only thing I would like to see different is the packing which would be on the freshness if the tea bags are vacuum packed. Also if the tea bags are arranged or grouped like those in the box versions, they would be less messy every time the bag is opened.

column9: Don't like this tea at all
column10: It has that weird metallic taste. Also, it looks strong but tastes mellow. For me the yorkshire red and yorkshire gold are the best english teas I have tasted. I do not like PG Tips either.

I make this like coffee, no sugar, hot water with or without cream added later. It is delicious and does not need sugar or (heaven forbid!) artificial sweeteners. I have been a Droste Cocoa (Dutch cocoa, and Dutch processed) customer for nearly 50 years, but was running out last week and I had another look at what's available at Amazon in the way of cocoa. The almost uniformly highly positive reviews here made me decide to try Pernigotti, another Dutch processed cocoa. I've cooked with cocoa over the years but am not in the habit of doing so recently. My usage has been limited to hot cocoa, and that's what I have tried so far with the Pernigotti, and I've compared it several times with both Droste and Valrhona cocoa. They are all good, but somewhat different. I definitely notice the vanilla accent of the Pernigotti. I wasn't sure I liked that at first, but decided that it's a subtle accent and not too intrusive. I wasn't used to it, but I think it's OK. The chocolate flavor is very nice, I think maybe better than the Droste, even, which was the best cocoa I had ever experienced. I once bought a can of Hershey's cocoa to see if it was OK, this was back in the 1970's and I was disgusted and I think I actually returned it to the market for a refund. I prefer Droste to Valrhona, but I may have found a new favorite now. The reviews at Amazon for Droste cocoa are not nearly as positive as for Pernigotti. Droste is more expensive here, but I can get it locally for about the same as the Pernigotti online, however I may stick with the Pernigotti now.I have developed a system for making hot cocoa that removes the guess work and results in uniformly pleasing cups of hot cocoa. Here it is:It's (by weight) 1 part cocoa, 2 parts sugar, 3 parts non fat dry milk, all mixed very well together and stored. To make, boil 3 parts water, pour over 1 part the mixture (again, by weight), stir well.Out of curiosity, I dug up a long time favorite chocolate recipe of mine (my own creation) and tried it with the Pernigotti -- Cocoa Pecan Cookies. It came out great. This recipe is to make cookie rolls, you bake a batch very quickly and easily any time you care to. To prepare the cookies, you preheat the oven, slice up a cookie roll, spread the slices on a cookie sheet and bake. Very simple. Here's the recipe:Cocoa Pecan Cookies(Dough for 8 batches)1 stick melted butter3/4 c. cocoa powder1.5 c sugar2 eggs (large)2 c flour1/2 t salt (this can be adjusted according to preference)1 t baking soda1 t vanilla (this was with Droste cocoa, since Pernigotti has vanilla this can be eliminated or adjusted)1 cup pecans (previously kept in freezer to prevent staling)Melt or soften the butter. Put all the above except the flour and pecans in bowl and beat well. Add 3/4 of the flour and beat and then add last portion of flour (1/2 cup) and mix in. Then add the pecans and mix reasonably well and then scoop out on a floured board and knead to get the nuts evenly distributed. Cut in 2 and cut one of those in 2. Take one of those and roll to about 10 inches long and cut it in 2 (you have an eighth). Cylinder should be about 1 inch thick and about 5 inches long. Press ends to flatten with blade and put in pan. Do same with the rest and put pan in bag, seal and place in refrigerator to firm for a few hours. Remove the rolls to plastic bag for refrigerated storage.To cook, preheat oven to 350 degrees, using sharp knfe slice one cookie roll into approximately 30 cookies, place them evenly on cookie sheet (teflon coated) and cook 10 minutes. Immediately scrape off with plastic spatula and let cool upside down. They should cool to crispness if they've been cooked properly. Cook only to that point and no more or there will be some burning. Enjoy.Here's a breakdown nutritionally (calories, that is)eggs 158butter 864sugar 1155flour 825pecans 750vanillacocoa 1683932 for 8 batches491 per batch, 181 fat calories37% from fat

I bake.  A lot.  Everyone looks for my baked goods at the holidays, but no one was expecting the chocolate cake made with Pernigotti.  Another reviewer commented about the rich aroma when the bag is opened, and she's right. The cocoa is a beautiful reddish-brown, and has the richest, most delightful smell ever. The only cocoa I found that remotely reminds me of this one is Schokinag. I found this at Williams-Sonoma, but it's priced much better here, even with shipping.  The only thing I have to say, to those who are not aware that there is a difference between Dutch Process and regular cocoa, is that you have to either watch the recipes you use it in or find a way to modify the recipe you have. I did the latter for the chocolate cake and it was wonderful. My brownies, which don't need modification came out so perfect that no one could believe that just changing the cocoa made that much of a difference.  I would definitely recommend purchasing this product, and had I not bought enough from WS to last the holidays, I would be buying this last one available now. Someone needs to snatch it up quick!

I am a hot chocolate connoisseur and have tried many different cocoa powders and drink mixes.  This has to be one of the best I have ever tried.  The second you open the bag, the most intense chocolate scent wafts up to you nose. Try that with regular cocoa. I haven't ever made cookies or anything else with it, but I imagine it would be just as delicious in those recipes as well.

I do a lot of home baking for my wife and others, and wanted a great dutch-processed cocoa to use.  One of the cakes I make uses cocoa in both the icing and the batter.  When I made the cake, which I usually do not care to eat, I loved it.  The usual bite of a natural cocoa was gone, the usual bitterness was non-existent.  I also made some brownies using this cocoa and a high quality natural cocoa.  I did blind taste tests with four other people.  Four of the five of us chose the brownies with this cocoa over the natural cocoa.  The only one to choose the brownies with the natural cocoa was someone who loves dark chocolate.  She did say that both were excellent, she just liked that little bite that the natural cocoa provided.  I will purchase this cocoa from now on, it is well worth it!

column9: Now this is great cocoa for syrup

The Hershey's was actually just what was left in an older tin, but I figured it would add a baseline (I'm generally not a fan). All three were prepared from a common simple syrup base, and all were whisked the same amount of time and brought to the same temp before taking off the heat.The Hershey's was fine, better than a bottle, but not as good as our usual Bensdorp ( from King Arthur Flour). The Valrhona was so bad, I'm not sure I'd even use it in milk or on ice cream. Pernigotti was the favorite of all three of us, by a good margin.  There were no strident or bitter flavors, and was as close to a dense, liquid chocolate flavor as we've tasted.
